rows.output: He said that the solution is to find a type of oil that Russia and Iran have in other places. He also emphasized that Russia has nothing else to rely on for its economy if it is not oil.
rows.reference: "The economic option on Iran and Russia is, more or less, leveraging and replacing fuels," he said, while referring to Russia as a "one trick pony" with an economy dependent on fossil fuels.

rows.source: Àwọn gbólóhùn yìí wáyé pẹ̀lú bí ìṣàkóṣo ìjọba Trump ń gbìyànjú láti fikún iye gáàsì tí ó ń tà ní Europe pẹ̀lú ìgbìyànjú láti fi ìdínwó gáàsì ti wọn lé Russia kúrò lọ́jà.
rows.output: These statements were made in conjunction with the Trump administration's efforts to increase the amount of gas being sold in Europe while trying to remove Russian gas from the market.
rows.reference: The statements come as Trump administration has been on a mission to boost the export of its liquefied natural gas to Europe, replacing Russia, the far cheaper option for European consumers.

rows.source: Nítorí ìdí èyí ni àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ Ìjọba Trump àti Trump fúnra rẹ̀ ṣe ń gbìyànjú láti yí orílẹ̀èdè Germany lọ́kàn padà kí wọ́n lè jáwọ́ nínú iṣẹ́ àkànṣè Nord Stream 2 pipeline project tí Trump wòye pé òun ló mú Russia jẹ gàba lórí ìjọba Germany.
rows.output: Because of this, Trump's government and Trump himself are trying to turn the country of Germany against itself so that it will stop working on the Nord Stream 2 pipeline project, which Trump believes he is responsible for making Russia control the government of Germany.
rows.reference: For that effect, the Trump administration officials, including US President Donald Trump himself, try to persuade Germany to pull out of the "inappropriate" Nord Stream 2 pipeline project, which according to Trump, made Berlin Moscow's "captive."

rows.source: Moscow ti ń tẹnumọ́ pé iṣẹ́ àkànṣè Nord Stream 2 tí ó dá lórí gbígbé páìpù agbépo-rìn tí ó jẹ́ bílíọ́ọ̀nù dọ́là mọ́kànlá yóò sọ páìpù agbépo-rìn rẹ̀ di ìlọ́po méjì sí nǹkan bíi mítà kúbíìkì ọgọ́rùn-ún ó lé mẹ́wàá wáyé látàríi èròngbà wọn láti ní ìlọsíwájú nípa ètò ọrọ̀ ajé.
rows.output: Moscow has been emphasizing that the construction of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which is worth $11 billion, will double the capacity of the existing pipeline by about 55 million cubic meters per day, as they seek to advance their economic interests.
rows.reference: Moscow has repeatedly stressed that the $11 billion Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which is set to double the existing pipeline capacity to 110 billion cubic meters, is a purely economic project.

rows.source: Ìjọba Russia wòye pé ìjọba orílẹ̀èdè Amẹ́ríkà ń tako iṣẹ́ àkànṣè náà nítorí ìtara àti wọn kò fẹ́ kí Russia ní ìlọsíwájú nípa ètò ọrọ̀ ajé bíi tiwọn.
rows.output: The Russian government believes that the US government is sabotaging the project because of its enthusiasm and does not want Russia to have economic success like theirs.
rows.reference: The Kremlin argues that Washington's fervent opposition to the project is simply driven by economic reasons and is an example of unfair competition.

rows.source: "Mínísítà fún ọ̀rọ̀ epo ní orílẹ̀èdè Russia Aleksandr Novak, lẹ́yìn ìpàdé rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú Sẹ́kẹ́tìrì fún ọ̀rọ̀ epo ni US tó wáyé ní oṣù kẹsàán ní Moscow sọ pé àwọn Mínísítà méjèèjì gbàgbọ́ pé epo kìí ṣe ohun tí ó tọ́ láti máa fi jẹ gàba lórí àwọn ènìyàn àti o yẹ kí àwọn oníbàárà le yan ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó bá wù wọ́n láti ra epo lọ́wọ́ rẹ̀.
rows.output: Minister of Energy of the Russian Federation Aleksandr Novak, after his meeting with the US Secretary of Energy in September in Moscow, stated that both ministers believe that oil should not be used as a weapon against people and that consumers should be able to choose anyone they want to buy oil from.
rows.reference: "I believe we share the view that energy cannot be a tool to exercise pressure and that consumers should be able to choose the suppliers," Russian Energy Minister Aleksandr Novak said following a meeting with US Energy Secretary Rick Perry in Moscow in September.

rows.source: Ìgbésẹ̀ US lórí ọ̀rọ̀ yìí ti mú kí orílẹ̀èdè Germany bu ẹnu àtẹ́ lu wọ́n ,Germany sì pinnu pé àwọn kò ní jáwọ́ nínú iṣẹ́ àkànṣè náà.
rows.output: The US's actions on this matter have led to Germany's criticism, and Germany has decided not to participate in the project.
rows.reference: The US stance has drawn backlash from Germany, which has reaffirmed its commitment to the project.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ tí ó ga jù lọ ní orílẹ̀èdè Germany, Federation of German Industries (BDI) ti képe orílẹ̀èdè US láti gbójú kúrò lára adehun tí Russia àti Germany ṣe lórí ọ̀rọ̀ à ń ta epo.
rows.output: The leading industrial federation in Germany, the Federation of German Industries (BDI), has urged the US to reject the agreement between Russia and Germany on the issue of oil exports.
rows.reference: Germany's leading organization for industry, the Federation of German Industries (BDI), has called on the US to stay away from the EU energy policy and the bilateral agreements between Berlin and Moscow.

rows.source: "Ọ̀gá ilé iṣẹ́ Federation of German Industries (BDI), lẹ́yìn ìpàdé pẹ̀lú adarí orílẹ̀èdè Germany Angela Merkel àti ààrẹ orílẹ̀èdè Russia Vladimir Putin ní àìpẹ́ yìí ṣàlàyé pé òun kò nífẹ̀ẹ́ kí orílẹ̀èdè kan máa dásí àdéhùn tí àwọn orílẹ̀èdè mìíràn ṣe pẹ̀lú ara wọn.
rows.output: The head of the Federation of German Industries (BDI), after a meeting with German Chancellor Angela Merkel and Russian President Vladimir Putin, explained that he does not want a country to be forced to sign agreements that other countries have made with each other.
rows.reference: "I have a big problem when a third state interferes in our energy supply," Dieter Kempf, head of the Federation of German Industries (BDI) said following a recent meeting between German Chancellor Angela Merkel and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

rows.source: Aṣòfin fún ìlú Massachusetts Elizabeth Warren yóò ronú jinlẹ̀ nípa bóyá yóò díje fún ipò ààrẹ ní ọdún 2020
rows.output: Senator for the Massachusetts city of Elizabeth Warren will consider deeply whether to run for the presidency in 2020
rows.reference: Elizabeth Warren Will Take "Hard Look" At Running For President in 2020, Massachusetts Senator Says

rows.source: Aṣòfin fún ìlú Massachusetts, lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta sọ pé òun yóò ronú jinlẹ̀ nípa bóyá yóò díje fún ipò ààrẹ ní ọdún 2020 lẹ́yìn ètò ìdìbò àárín sáà.
rows.output: The Massachusetts legislature, on Wednesday, said it will consider whether to run for president in 2020 after the midterm elections.
rows.reference: Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren said on Saturday she would take a "hard look" at running for president following the midterm elections.

rows.source: Nínú ìpàdé tí ó wáyé ní gbọ̀gán ìlú Massachusetts, Warren fi dá àwọn tí ó wà nibẹ̀ lójú pé òun yóò ronú púpọ̀ nípa ọ̀rọ̀ náà.
rows.output: In a meeting held in the town of Massachusetts, Warren assured those present that he would think a lot about the matter.
rows.reference: During a town hall in Holyoke, Massachusetts, Warren confirmed she'd consider running.

rows.source: "Gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìwé ìròyìn The Hill ṣe àfihàn hàn, arábìnrin náà sọ pé ó ti tó àkókò fún àwọn obìnrin láti gbà ìṣàkóso ìjọba, kí wọ́n sì ṣe àtúnṣe ìjọba pẹ̀lú obìnrin gẹ́gẹ́ bí adarí.
rows.output: As reported by The Hill, the sister said it is time for women to take over the government and reform it with a woman as leader.
rows.reference: "It's time for women to go to Washington and fix our broken government and that includes a woman at the top," she said, according to The Hill.

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn ọjọ́ kẹfà oṣù kọọkànlá, n ó ronú nípa gbígbé igbá ìdìbò fún ipò ààrẹ.
rows.output: After six months, I was thinking about holding a referendum for the presidency.
rows.reference: "After November 6, I will take a hard look at running for president."

rows.source: Warren bu ẹnu àtẹ́ẹnu lu ààrẹ Donald Trump ní ìpàdé náà, ó ṣàlàyé ọ̀nà àìtọ́ ni ọ̀nà tí Trump ń ti orílẹ̀èdè US sí.
rows.output: Warren criticized President Donald Trump at the meeting, explaining the wrong way that Trump is leading the country.
rows.reference: Warren weighed in on President Donald Trump during the town hall, saying he was "taking this county in the wrong direction.

rows.source: “Ó ń kan mí lóminú ohun tí Trump ń ṣe sí ìjọba tiwantiwa” ni ohun tí Warren sọ.
rows.output: "He's just so dismissive of the whole idea of democracy" is what Warren said.
rows.reference: "I am worried down to my bones about what Donald Trump is doing to our democracy," she said.

rows.source: Warren ti ń ké gbàjarè látẹ̀yìnwá pé Trump àti ẹni tí ó yàn sípò ilé ẹjọ́ tí ó ga jù lọ Brett Kavanaugh ń ṣe ìjọba báṣubàṣu.
rows.output: Warren has been warning for some time that Trump and his Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh are making a mockery of the judiciary.
rows.reference: Warren has been outspoken in her criticism of Trump and his Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Warren sọ̀rọ̀ ní ọjọ́ ẹtì lórí ẹ̀rọ tíwítà pé ó ṣe pàtàkì kí àjọ FBI ṣe ìwádìí ìjọba kí ètò ìdìbò mìíràn tó dé."
rows.output: Warren spoke on Tuesday on Twitter that it is important for the FBI to investigate the government before another election.
rows.reference: In a tweet on Friday, Warren said "of course we need an FBI investigation before voting."

rows.source: Lódì kejì, ọ̀pọ̀ nínú àwọn olùgbé agbègbè tí Warren ti wá ni kò fara mọ́ ọ pé kí Warren díje ní ọdún 2020 gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìbò afèròhàn lórí ẹ̀rọ ayélujára ṣe fi hàn ní Ọjọ́bọ̀.
rows.output: Secondly, many of the residents of the area that Warren came from were not in favor of him running in 2020 as a write-in candidate on social media showed on Thursday.
rows.reference: A poll released on Thursday, however, showed a majority of Warren's own constituents do not think she should run in 2020.

rows.source: Ìdá méjìdínlọ́gọ́ta nínú àwọn tí ó lè dìbò ló sọ pé kí amòfin náà má díje gẹ́gẹ́ bí Suffolk University Political Research Ceenter àti Boston Globe poll ṣe fi hàn.
rows.output: 58 percent of those who could vote said that the judge should not run, as shown by a Suffolk University Political Research Center and Boston Globe poll.
rows.reference: Fifty-eight percent of "likely" Massachusetts voters said the senator should not run, according to the Suffolk University Political Research Center/Boston Globe poll.

rows.source: Ìdá méjìlélọ́gbọ̀n ló faramọ́ kí Warren díje.
rows.output: Twenty-six of them supported Warren's candidacy.
rows.reference: Thirty-two percent supported such a run.

rows.source: Ìbò afèròhàn náà fi hàn pé àwọn ènìyàn agbègbè náà fún Gómìnà tẹ́lẹ̀ tí Deval Patrick ní àtìlẹyìn nígbà tí ìdá méjìdínlógójì faramọ́ dídíje Deval, tí ìdá méjìdíláàdọ́ta sì tako rẹ̀.
rows.output: The referendum showed that the local people supported the former Governor Deval Patrick when 58% voted for Deval, and 42% against him.
rows.reference: The poll showed more support for a run by former Governor Deval Patrick, with 38 percent supporting a potential run and 48 percent against it.

rows.source: Nínú àwọn gbajúmọ̀ olóṣèlú tí orúkọ wọn jẹyọ pé wọ́n lè díje dupò ní ọdún 2020 ni igbákejì ààrẹ tẹ́lẹ̀ rí Joe Biden àti Amòfin ìlú Vermont, Bernie Sanders.
rows.output: In the most popular politicians whose names were mentioned as potential candidates in 2020 were Vice President Joe Biden and the former Attorney General of Vermont, Bernie Sanders.
rows.reference: Other high profile Democratic names discussed in regard to a potential 2020 run include former Vice President Joe Biden and Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn Associated Press sọ pé Biden ṣàlàyé pé wọ́n di January kí òun tó pinnu bóyá òun máa díje.
rows.output: The Associated Press news agency reported that Biden said he would not decide until January whether to run.
rows.reference: Biden said he would decide officially by January, the Associated Press reported.

rows.source: Sarah Palin mẹ́nu ba àìsàn PTSD tó mú Track Palin níbi ìwọ́de Donald Trump
rows.output: Sarah Palin mentioned her son Track's PTSD, which led to his arrest at a Donald Trump rally
rows.reference: Sarah Palin cites Track Palin's PTSD at Donald Trump rally

rows.source: Ògbẹ́ni Track Palin tí ó jẹ́ ọmọ ọdún mẹ́rìndínlógún Track Palin lo ọdún kan ní Iraq lẹ́yìn tí ó darapọ̀ mọ́ àjọ àwọn ọmọ ogun ní oṣù kẹsàán.
rows.output: Mr. Track Palin, who is 26 years old, served a year in Iraq after joining the military in September.
rows.reference: Track Palin, 26, spent a year in Iraq after enlisting on Sept.

rows.source: Àwọn agbófinró mú u ni ọjọ́ Ajé lórí ẹ̀sùn ìwà ipá abélé
rows.output: The police arrested him on Monday for alleged assault.
rows.reference: He was arrested and charged in a domestic violence incident on Monday night

rows.source: Níbi ìwọ́de fún Donald Trump ní ìlú Tulsa, Oklahoma ni Sarah Palin rí sọ fún àwọn èrò pé “Mo mọ̀ pé ohun tí ọmọ mi ń là kọjá jẹ́ ohun kan náà tí àwọn ìdílé mìíràn là kọjá látàrí ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ sí àwọn ọmọ wa lójú ogun“
rows.output: At the rally for Donald Trump in Tulsa, Oklahoma, Sarah Palin told the audience that "I know that the struggles of my son are the same struggles of other families that have been through what has happened to our children in the war."
rows.reference: "What my own son is going through, what he is going through coming back, I can relate to other families who feel ramifications of PTSD and some of the woundedness that our soldiers do return with," she told the audience at a rally for Donald Trump in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

rows.source: Palin ṣàlàyé pé ohun ìtìjú ni mímú tí àwọn agbófinró mú ọmọ òun àti àwọn ọmọ ogun mìíràn. Ó tẹ̀síwájú pé àwọn ọmọ ogun máa ń padà wálé ní àrà ọ̀tọ̀ pẹ̀lú ojúúwòye mìíràn, ìbéèrè tó sì ń sọ sí gbogbo wọn lọ́kàn ni pé ṣe èrè tí ó tọ́ sí àwọn ọmọ ogun tí wọ́n ti farajìn fún orílẹ̀èdè wọn nìyí."
rows.output: Palin explained that the real shock was the arrest of his son and other soldiers. He continued that the soldiers would return home in a different manner, with a different perspective, and the question that was on everyone's mind was whether the gains were worth the sacrifices made by the soldiers for their country.
rows.reference: Palin called his arrest "the elephant in the room" and said of her son and other war veterans, "they come back a bit different, they come back hardened, they come back wondering if there is that respect for what it is that their fellow soldiers and airmen, and every other member of the military, has given to the country."

rows.source: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí Dan Bennett, agbẹnusọ fún àjọ ọlọ́pàá mí Wasilla ṣe sọ, Ọjọ ẹtì ni àwọn agbófinró mú Track ní ìlú Wasilla, Alaska, wọ́n sì fẹ̀sùn kàn án pé ò na obìnrin, ó tún wà pẹ̀lú ohun èlò ìjà ní ipò ẹni ti ó ti mú ọtí yó.
rows.output: As Dan Bennett, spokesman for the Matanuska-Susitna Valley Police Department, said, the police arrested Track in Wasilla, Alaska, on a Tuesday, and charged him with domestic violence, and also with being in possession of a firearm while intoxicated.
rows.reference: He was arrested on Monday in Wasilla, Alaska, and charged with domestic violence assault on a female, interfering with a report of domestic violence and possession of a weapon while intoxicated, according to Dan Bennett, a spokesman for the Wasilla Police Department.

rows.source: Ìpínlẹ̀ méjìdínlógún pẹ̀lú D.C. fọwọ́ sí àbá láti tako ofin titun lórí gbigba àwọn tó ń wá àbò wọlé sí orílẹ̀èdè US.
rows.output: Eighteen states, including DC, signed a letter to oppose the new law on immigration to the US.
rows.reference: 18 states, D.C. support challenge to new asylum policy

rows.source: Ipinlẹ mejidinlogun ati Ẹkun Columbia n kin itako ofin ilana U.S tuntun lẹhin ti o kọ aabo nilu ibomiran fun awọn ẹgbẹ ti a n fi iya jẹ ti o n sa tabi inilara inu-ile.
rows.output: Twenty-two states and the District of Columbia are leading the way in the new U.S. legal landscape following the rejection of the defense of "reasonable self-defense" for individuals who are being abused or harassed in their homes.
rows.reference: Eighteen states and the District of Columbia are supporting a legal challenge to a new U.S. policy that denies asylum to victims fleeing gang or domestic violence.

rows.source: Àwọn aṣojú láti àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ yìí tako ètò àmúlò titun yìí nílé ẹjọ́ lọ́jọ́ Ẹtì nílùú Washington gẹ́gẹ́ bí NBC News ṣe sọ.
rows.output: Representatives from these states oppose this new plan in court on the day of the Washington Post.
rows.reference: Representatives from the 18 states and the district filed a friend-of-the-court brief Friday in Washington to support an asylum-seeker challenging the policy, NBC News reported.

rows.source: Orúkọ olúfiṣe ní kíkún ni Grace v. Àkóónú àbá tí American Civil Liberties Union fà kalẹ̀ nílé amòfin lóṣù kẹjọ kò ti di mímọ̀ fún àwọn ènìyàn.
rows.output: The name of the case is Grace v. The ACLU's proposed amendment to the Constitution, which was introduced in the House of Representatives in August, has not yet been made known to the public.
rows.reference: The full name of the plaintiff in the Grace v. Sessions suit that the American Civil Liberties Union filed in August against the federal policy has not been revealed.

rows.source: Grace sọ pé olólùfẹ́ rẹ pẹ̀lú àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ oníjàgídíjàgan rẹ̀ ṣe ìpalára fún òun ṣùgbọ́n àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ orílẹ̀èdè US tako sísálọ òun lọ orílẹ̀èdè náà.
rows.output: Grace claimed that her lover and his militant group had harmed her, but US officials thwarted her attempt to leave the country.
rows.reference: She said her partner "and his violent gang member sons," abused her but U.S. officials denied her request for asylum July 20.

rows.source: Wọ́n jù ú sí àtìmọ́lé ní ìlú Texas.
rows.output: They arrested her in the city of Texas.
rows.reference: She was detained in Texas.

rows.source: Àwọn agbẹjọ́rò ìjọba tó dúró fún Grace sọ pé El Salvador, Honduras àti Guatemala tí wọ́n jẹ́ ìlú tí ó ń kojú ìṣòro jàgídíjàgan àti rògbòdìyàn abẹ́lé látàríi ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ènìyàn tó ń sá kúrò níbẹ̀ fún ààbò ní US.
rows.output: The government lawyers representing Grace said that El Salvador, Honduras, and Guatemala, which are countries facing high levels of violence and insecurity due to a large number of people fleeing for safety, are the countries that should be held responsible for her death.
rows.reference: The states' attorneys supporting Grace described El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala, which produce a large number of applicants for U.S. asylum, as nations facing pervasive problems with gangs and domestic violence.

rows.source: Òfin titun tí US ní lórí àwọn tó ń wá ààbò ṣe jẹ́ àtúnṣe sí ipinnu ọdún 2014 tí ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń rí sí ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn aṣíkiri tí ó gba àwọn aṣíkiri tí kò ní ìwé láyè láti bèèrè fún ààbò ní orílẹ̀èdè US.
rows.output: New US law on asylum seekers is a revision of the 2014 decision by the Board of Immigration Appeals that allowed asylum seekers without documentation to request protection in the US.
rows.reference: The new U.S. asylum policy reversed a 2014 decision by the Board of Immigrant Appeals that allowed undocumented immigrants fleeing domestic violence to apply for asylum.

rows.source: Agbẹjọ́rò àgbà fún District of Columbia ṣàlàyé lọ́jọ Ẹtì pé ètò àmúlò titun yìí yẹ̀ba kúrò lára ofin tí àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ àti orílẹ̀èdè ti ń ṣàmúlò fún ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ọdún sẹ́yìn."
rows.output: The Attorney General of the District of Columbia stated on Thursday that this new plan would be exempt from the laws that states and the country have been implementing for decades.
rows.reference: District of Columbia Attorney General Karl Racine said in a statement Friday that the new policy "ignores decades of state, federal, and international law."

rows.source: "Ọ̀rẹ́ ilé ẹjọ́ kan sọ pé òfin ìjọba gbogbogbò là á kalẹ̀ pé kí a dájọ́ àwọn tó ń wá ààbò lórí òótọ́ àti àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó rọ̀gbà yí irúfẹ́ ẹjọ́ bẹ́ẹ̀ ká.
rows.output: "A friend of the court said that the general law provides that those seeking asylum should be judged on the truth and on the circumstances of the case, not on the type of case."
rows.reference: "Federal law requires that all asylum claims be adjudicated on the particular facts and circumstances of the claim, and such a bar violates that principle," the friend-of-the court brief said.

rows.source: Àwọn agbẹjọ́rò túbọ̀ wòye pé ètò àmúlò titun yìí ń mú ìpalára bá ètò ọrọ̀ ajé orílẹ̀èdè US nítorí àwọn tó ń wá ààbò yìí sábà máa ń di oníṣòwò àti òṣìṣẹ́ tí ìlú nílò."
rows.output: The lawyers argue that this new system is causing damage to the US economy because these people seeking asylum often become entrepreneurs and employees that the city needs.
rows.reference: Attorneys further argued in the brief that the policy denying immigrants entry hurts the U.S. economy, saying they are more likely to become entrepreneurs and "supply necessary labor."

rows.source: Amòfin àgbà fún ìjọba Jeff Sessions ní oṣù kẹfà pàṣẹ kí àwọn adájọ́ tó ń rí ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn aṣíkiri má ṣe fún àwọn aṣíkiri náà ni àyè láti fi orílẹ̀èdè US ṣe ibùgbé.
rows.output: The Attorney General ordered the Department of Justice in June to instruct judges to not allow the asylum seekers to stay in the US.
rows.reference: Attorney General Jeff Sessions ordered immigration judges to no longer grant asylum to victims fleeing domestic abuse and gang violence in June.

rows.source: “Àyè wà fún àwọn tó fi ìlú wọn sílẹ̀ nítorí ìyà àìtọ́ bóyá lórí ẹ̀yà, ẹ̀sìn, orílẹ̀èdè tí ènìyàn ti wá, ẹgbẹ́ tí ènìyàn ń ṣe tàbí ojúùwoye ènìyàn nípa ìṣèlú” Sessions sọ èyí nínú ìkéde ètò àmúlò ní ọjọ́ kọọkànlá, oṣù kẹfà.
rows.output: "There is a place for those who have left their country due to injustice, whether on the basis of race, religion, nationality, group, or political perspective," Sessions said in a statement on the rule of law on June 11.
rows.reference: "Asylum is available for those who leave their home country because of persecution or fear on account of race, religion, nationality, or membership in a particular social group or political opinion," Sessions said in his June 11 announcement of the policy.

rows.source: Sísá kiri fún ààbò kò lè tán gbogbo ìṣòro -- kódà gbogbo ìṣòro tí ó kẹnú -- tí àwọn ènìyàn ń là kọjá lójoojúmọ́ kaakiri agbàayé.
rows.output: Surfing for safety cannot solve all problems -- even all the complex problems that people face every day around the world.
rows.reference: Asylum was never meant to alleviate all problems -- even all serious problems -- that people face every day all over the world.

rows.source: Ìgbiyànjú ń lọ lọ́wọ́lọ́wọ́ nílùú Palu láti ṣe àwárí àwọn tí ó yé bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé àwọn ènìyàn tí ó pàdánù ẹ̀mí wọn ti di ìlọ́po méjì
rows.output: The rescue operation in Palu is ongoing to find survivors, even though the number of people who have lost their lives has doubled.
rows.reference: Desperate rescue efforts in Palu as death toll doubles in race to find survivors

rows.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ náà ti di ẹsẹ̀ kan ayé, ẹsẹ̀ kan ọrun fún àwọn tí ó yé ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà.
rows.output: The news has become a foot in the world, a foot in heaven for those who witnessed the event.
rows.reference: For survivors, the situation was increasingly dire.

rows.source: “Ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí múnilára gidi gan” ni ohun tí ọmọ ọdún márùndínlógójì tí ó jẹ́ ìyá Risa Kusuma sọ bí ó ṣe ń tu ọmọ rẹ̀ tí wọ́n ń ṣàìsàn nínú ní àyè ìgbénìyàn sí ní ìlú Palu.
rows.output: "This incident is very sad" is what a 45-year-old mother of Risa Kusuma said as she was taking her sick child to a public hospital in the city of Palu.
rows.reference: "It feels very tense," said 35-year-old mother Risa Kusuma, comforting her feverish baby boy at an evacuation centre in the gutted city of Palu.

rows.source: "Ìṣẹ́jú-ìṣẹ́jú ni ọkọ̀ aláísàn máa ń gbé okú wọlé..
rows.output: "Every minute, the ambulance driver brings in a dead body.
rows.reference: "Every minute an ambulance brings in bodies.

rows.source: Omi tó mọ́ ṣọ̀wọ́n."
rows.output: The water is very clear."
rows.reference: Clean water is scarce."

rows.source: A rí àwọn olùgbé tó ń padà lọ sí ilé wọn tó ti bàjẹ́ láti mú ohun tí wọ́n bá lè rí mú nínú ẹrù wọn.
rows.output: We saw the residents returning to their damaged homes to gather whatever they could find in their belongings.
rows.reference: Residents were seen returning to their destroyed homes, picking through waterlogged belongings, trying to salvage anything they could find.

rows.source: Ọ̀gọ̀ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn ènìyàn ló farapa nínú ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ilẹ̀ mímì tí agbára rẹ̀ tó 7.5
rows.output: The casualties were all people, in the 7.5 magnitude earthquake.
rows.reference: Hundreds of people were injured and hospitals, damaged by the magnitude 7.5 quake, were overwhelmed.

rows.source: Díẹ̀ nínú àwọn tó fara káṣá nínú ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí, èyí tí Dwi Harris tí ó ṣìṣe léjìká ,tí egun ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ sì kán sinmi ní iwájú ilé ìwòsàn Palu's Army, níbi tí àwọn aláìsàn ti ń rí ìtọ́jú gbà.
rows.output: Some of those who were injured in this incident, including Dwi Harris, who was shot in the back, are resting in the Palu Army Hospital, where patients are receiving treatment.
rows.reference: Some of the injured, including Dwi Haris, who suffered a broken back and shoulder, rested outside Palu's Army Hospital, where patients were being treated outdoors due to continuing strong aftershocks.

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú omijé ni Dwi fi ń ròyìn ìṣẹ̀lẹ ilẹ̀ mímì tí ó ká òun, ọmọbìnrin àti iyawo re mọ́ àjà-ile karùn-ún ní hòtẹ́ẹ̀lì.
rows.output: With tears, Dwi reported the incident of the earthquake that hit him, his daughter, and his wife, who were staying in a hotel.
rows.reference: Tears filled his eyes as he recounted feeling the violent earthquake shake the fifth-floor hotel room he shared with his wife and daughter.

rows.source: A ò ráyè kankan láti sá àsálà fún ẹ̀mí wa.
rows.output: We will not be silent in the face of our own death.
rows.reference: "There was no time to save ourselves.

rows.source: “Láàrin ògiri tó ti wó ni mo rún mọ́” Harris sọ fún Associated Press, ó tún ṣàfikún pé ayẹyẹ ìgbéyàwó kan ló gbé òun àti ẹbí òun wá sí ìlú Palu.
rows.output: "Between the walls that were destroyed, I ran to them," Harris told the Associated Press, adding that a wedding celebration had brought him and his family to the city of Palu.
rows.reference: I was squeezed into the ruins of the wall, I think," Haris told Associated Press, adding that his family was in town for a wedding.

rows.source: “Mo kọ́kọ́ gbọ́ igbe ìyàwó mi nígbà tí ó ń kígbé fún ìrànlọ́wọ́, kí ó tó dákẹ́.
rows.output: I first heard my wife's scream when she was calling for help, before she collapsed.
rows.reference: "I heard my wife cry for help, but then silence.

rows.source: Mí ò mọ ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ sí ìyàwó àti ọmọ mi
rows.output: I don't know what happened to my wife and child.
rows.reference: I don't know what happened to her and my child.

rows.source: Mo ní ìrètí pé kò sí ohunkóhun tó ṣe wọ́n”
rows.output: I hope that nothing can stop them.
rows.reference: I hope they are safe."

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba US ní orílẹ̀èdè China fẹ̀sùn kan orílẹ̀èdè náà pé ó ń ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn orílẹ̀èdè mìíràn pẹ̀lú pípolówó ẹ̀tàn.
rows.output: The US State Department accuses the country of harming other countries with its propaganda.
rows.reference: U.S. ambassador accuses China of 'bullying' with 'propaganda ads'

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn ọ̀sẹ̀ kan tí ìwé ìròyìn fún ìjọba China gbé ìròyìn olójúùwé mẹ́rin kan jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn kan ní US. Ìròyìn náà ṣe àtòólẹ̀ àǹfààní tó wà láàrin òwò láàrin China àti US, èyí tí aṣojú ìjọba náà na ìka àbùkù kan China pé ó ń fi àwọn ìwé ìròyìn orílẹ̀èdè Amẹ́ríkà tan àwọn ènìyàn.
rows.output: After a week of coverage in the Chinese government-controlled media, a four-page article in a US newspaper published a report on the advantages of trade between China and the US, which the Chinese government representative criticized as a "smear campaign" against the Chinese government.
rows.reference: A week after an official Chinese newspaper ran a four-page ad in a U.S. daily touting the mutual benefits of U.S.-China trade, the U.S. ambassador to China accused Beijing of using the American press to spread propaganda.

rows.source: U.S. Ààrẹ orílẹ̀èdè U.S. Donald Trump ní Ọjọ́rú tó kọjá tọ́ka sí ìròyìn tí China gbé jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register- ilé-iṣẹ́ ìwé ìròyìn tí ń tà jùlọ ní ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa fẹ̀sùn kan China pé ó ń gbìyànjú láti dásí ètò ìdìbò ilé fún ilé amòfin tí yóò wáyé ní ọjọ́ kẹfà oṣù kọọkànlá. Orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ pé àwọn kò mọwọ́-mẹsẹ̀ nípa ẹ̀sùn náà.
rows.output: On December 5, U.S. President Donald Trump accused China of attempting to influence the upcoming midterm elections through a Des Moines Register article, which is the largest newspaper in Iowa. The Chinese government denied the allegations.
rows.reference: U.S. President Donald Trump last Wednesday referred to the China Daily's paid supplement in the Des Moines Register - the state of Iowa's biggest selling newspaper - after accusing China of seeking to meddle in the Nov. 6 U.S. congressional elections, a charge China denies.

rows.source: Ibu ẹnu atẹlu Trump ti Beijing n gbiyanju lati dasi ninu idibo U.S saami si ohun ti awọn osisẹ U.S sọ fun Reuters jẹ ipele tuntun ninu irusoke ipolongo ibo lọdọ Washington lati funmọ China.
rows.output: Trump's trade war with Beijing is trying to intervene in the U.S. election, which is a new level of escalation in the Washington-China campaign to pressure Beijing, according to U.S. officials who spoke to Reuters.
rows.reference: Trump's accusation that Beijing was trying to meddle in U.S. elections marked what U.S. officials told Reuters was a new phase in an escalating campaign by Washington to put pressure on China.

rows.source: Bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ kìí ṣe ohun àràmọ̀ndà kí àwọn ìjọba òkèèrè ṣe ìpolówó fún ìlọsíwájú ọrọ̀ ajé, rògbòdìyàn nípa ọrọ̀ ajé wà láàrin Beijing ati Washington, èyí tí ó sì fà á kí àwọn méjèèjì gbé owó lórí àwọn ọjà tí ó ń wọlé láti orílẹ̀èdè kejì.
rows.output: While it is not a secret that foreign governments promote economic growth, there is a debate between Beijing and Washington about the economy, which has led both to impose tariffs on imports from the other country.
rows.reference: While it is normal for foreign governments to place advertisements to promote trade, Beijing and Washington are currently locked in an escalating trade war that has seen them level rounds of tariffs on each other's imports.

rows.source: Àwọn onímọ̀ lórílèedè U.S. wòye pé China ṣe àfikún owó lè ọjà tó ń wọlé sí U.S. láti orílẹ̀èdè China pàápàá jùlọ ní àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ bíi Iowa tí ó gbárùkù Trump àti ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú rẹ̀.
rows.output: US experts believe that China has added to the trade deficit with the US, particularly in states like Iowa that Trump and his party have targeted.
rows.reference: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba U.S. ni China àti Gómìnà tẹ́lẹ̀ rí fún ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa, ẹni tí ó ń ta ohun ògbìn sí China jù, Terry Branstad sọ pé China ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn òṣìṣẹ́, okoòwò àti àgbẹ̀ nílẹ̀ Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: The U.S. Ambassador to China and former Governor of Iowa, who has done more business with China than anyone, Terry Branstad, said that China has harmed American workers, businesses and farmers.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: Branstad wòye nínú ìwé tí ó kọ sínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register ní ọjọ́ Àìkú pé China ti sa gbogbo ipa wọn láti ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn nínú àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn ní Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: Branstad wrote in an op-ed column in the Des Moines Register on Sunday that China has had a significant impact on the spread of propaganda in the media in the United States.
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: "Ìjọba China ń ṣe àmúlò ètò ìròyìn tí kò ní ìpalára láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba tí ó wà ní Amẹ́ríkà láti sanwó ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn àti irọ́ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register,” ni ohun tí Branstad kọ.
rows.output: The Chinese government is implementing a non-toxic media strategy from the American government to subsidize the cost of running a campaign of lies and deceit in the Des Moines Register, according to Branstad.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: "Ó tún tẹ̀síwájú pé “Lódì kejì ẹ̀wẹ̀, kò fi bẹ́ẹ̀ sí àwọn alátakò tàbí ààfihàn èrò àwọn ará China lórí irúfẹ́ ọwọ́ ti ìjọba fi mú ètò ọrọ̀ ajé. Èyí rí bẹ́ẹ̀ nítorí abẹ́ ìṣàkóso ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Chinese Communist Party ni àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn wà.
rows.output: He also continued that "The second wave of the epidemic, did not have any impact on the views of the Chinese people on the style of government management of the economy. This is because under the control of the Chinese Communist Party, the media outlets were.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ó tún fikún un pé ọ̀kan nínú àwọn ògbóntarìgì ilé ìwé ìròyìn ní orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ láti tẹ iṣẹ́ òun sínú ìwé ìròyìn wọn bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé Branstad kò dárúkọ ìwé ìròyìn náà ní pàtó.
rows.output: He also added that one of the editors of a Chinese newspaper wrote an article about his work, even though Branstad did not mention the newspaper by name.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ Ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì ń ya àwọn obìnrin kúrò pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀ Kavanaugh, Àwọn Onímọ̀ kìlọ̀
rows.output: The Republican Party is splitting over the issue of Kavanaugh, the Experts warn
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú bí ọ̀pọ̀ nínú àwọn àgbà ọ̀jẹ̀ olóṣèlú ẹgbẹ́ republican ṣe ń gbárùkù ẹni tí wọ́n yàn ní ilé ẹjọ́ tí ó ga jù lọ pẹ̀lú gbogbo àwọn ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀, àwọn onímọ̀ tí ń kìlọ̀ pé ọ̀rọ̀ yìí yóò lẹ́yìn pàápàá jùlọ láti ọwọ́ àwọn obìnrin nínú ètò ìdìbò áàrin táàmù.
rows.output: With many of the old guard republicans in the house of representatives, the nominee of the party, who is also the incumbent, is facing a serious challenge from a number of women in the primary.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ náà ti fa ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀pọ̀ rúkèrúdò, àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sì ń takú àwọn yóò tún dìbò fún àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ wọn.
rows.output: The statement has caused a lot of controversy, and Republican politicians are pressuring their members to vote for their candidates.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Ọ̀jọ̀gbọ́n nínú ẹ̀kọ́ ìṣèlú ní Maxwell School tí ó wà ní Yunifásítì Syracuse Grant Reheer ṣọ fún àwọn ìwé ìròyìn The Hill lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta pé ọ̀rọ̀ náà yóò lẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Professor of political science at the Maxwell School at Syracuse University Grant Reheer told the news outlet The Hill on Wednesday that the issue would be resolved.
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reheer sọ pé òun kò rò bóyá ìgbésẹ̀ tí Amòfin Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) nípa pípè àjọ FBI láti wá ṣe ìwádìí àwọn ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan Kavanaugh yóò tó láti pẹ̀tù sọ́kàn àwọn olùdìbò tí inú ń bí lọ́wọ́ lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà.
rows.output: Reheer said he did not think the step taken by Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) of calling the FBI to investigate the allegations against Kavanaugh would be enough to sway the voters who were already leaning against the issue.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: "“Àwọn obìnrin ò ní gbàgbé ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní àná, wọn kò ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ lónìí, wọn kò sì ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ nínú ètò ìdìbò tí yóò wáyé ní oṣù kọọkànlá” ni ohun tí Karine Jean-Pierre, olùbádámọ̀ràn àgbà àti agbẹnusọ gbogbo fún ẹgbẹ́ MoveOn sọ lọ́jọ Ẹtì, èyí tí ó sì jẹyọ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday, they will not forget it today, and they will not forget it in the upcoming election in November" said Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, on Thursday, as reported in the Washington Post.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: Oṣù kọọkànlá ń bọ̀! Ní ohun tí àwọn afẹ̀hónúhàn ń ké bí wọ́n ṣe fi ìtaara wọn hàn ní ilé Aṣòfin pẹ̀lú bí àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì tí ó wà ní ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń ṣàkóso ọ̀rọ̀ ilé ẹjọ́ ṣe ń tẹ̀síwájú láti yan Kavanaugh sípò. The Mic jẹ́ kí ó yé wa pé èyí wáyé lẹ́yìn ẹ̀rí dọ́kítà Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic ní ó ń jọ́bọ̀ ìròyìn.
rows.output: November is coming! The Mic highlights the hypocrisy of the Democrats in the Senate who are pushing for a vote on Kavanaugh after the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, the Mic reports, is a jobless lawyer.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: Onímọ̀ ìṣèlú Stu Rothenberg sọ “Ìmọ̀sílára kò ní í sí lára àwọn ènìyàn, èyí yóò sì mú wọn dìbò”
rows.output: Political scientist Stu Rothenberg said, "The public is not paying attention, and that will lead to a low voter turnout."
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: Àwọn ènìyàn tilẹ̀ ti ń sọ pé àwọn kò lè dúró kí ọjọ́ ìdìbò dé.
rows.output: People are even saying that they can't wait for the election day.
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Ó ṣeéṣe kí ìmọ̀sílára pọ̀ sí pàápàá jùlọ láàrin àwọn obìnrin tí ó wà ní ìgbèríko àti àwọn ọmọbìnrin láàrin ọmọ ọdún méjìdínlógún sí óòkandínlọ́gbọ̀n tí wọ́n ò nífẹ̀ẹ́ ààrẹ, síbẹ̀ tí wọ́n kìí dìbò.”
rows.output: It is possible that the sense of alienation will be even greater among rural women and young women between the ages of 18 and 24 who do not support the president, but who do vote.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Kí Ford tó jẹ́rìí ní gbangba nípa ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀ tí ó fi kan Kavanaugh ni àwọn onímọ̀ ti ń kìlọ̀ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí yíyan Kavanaugh sípò bu ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì lọ́wọ́.
rows.output: Before Ford publicly confirmed the sexual assault allegations against Kavanaugh, experts were warning that the Republican Party could be at risk of losing the Senate seat.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí ti dá yánpọyánrin kalẹ̀ fún ẹgbẹ́ wa” ni ohun tí Michael Steele tí ó fìgbà kan jẹ́ alága fún ìgbìmọ̀ gbogbogbò ní ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sọ ní ọ̀sẹ̀ tó kọjá gẹ́gẹ́ bí NBC News ṣe sọ.
rows.output: "This has been a very difficult week for our party" is what Michael Steele, the former chairman of the Republican National Committee, told NBC News last week.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí kìí ṣe nípa bóyá àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì yan Kavanaugh sípò nìkan, ó tún nííṣe pẹ̀lú ọwọ́ tí ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì fi mú ọ̀rọ̀ náà àti ọwọ́ tí wọ́n fi mú Ford” Olùdarí ẹgbẹ́ tó ń ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ fún ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Dẹ́mókírààtì Priorities USA, Guy Cecil ló sọ èyí fún ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn náà.
rows.output: "This is not just about whether the Republican Party nominated Kavanaugh, but also about the hand that the Republican Party has in the narrative and the hand that they have in Ford."
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀, èrò àwọn ọmọ Amẹ́ríkà pín sí méjì lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà pẹ̀lú bí wọn kò mọ ẹni tí ó yẹ kí wọ́n gbàgbọ́ nínú Kavanaugh àti Ford.
rows.output: However, American public opinion is divided on the issue with many not knowing who to believe in either Kavanaugh or Ford.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Ìdìbò afèròhàn tí YouGov gbé kalẹ̀ fi hàn pé ìdá mọ́kànlelógoji nínú àwọn tó kópa nínú ètò ìdìbò náà sọ pé àwọn gba Ford gbọ́ nígbà tí ìdá márùndínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn gba Kavanaugh gbọ́.
rows.output: A survey conducted by YouGov found that 54% of participants in the survey said they trust Ford, while 45% said they trust Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Ìdá méjìdínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn ní ìgbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Kavanaugh ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí rẹ̀ nígbà tí ìdá ọgbọ̀n ló gbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Ford ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí tirẹ̀ bákan náà.
rows.output: Eighteen percent said they believed that Kavanaugh lied under oath, while 30 percent said they believed that Ford lied under oath.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: The Guardian ròyìn pé lẹ́yìn tí amòfin Flake ké sí àjọ FBI, ìwádìí ti ń lọ lọ́wọ́ lórí ẹ̀sùn tí Ford and afẹ̀sùkan mìíràn Deborah Ramírez fi kan Kavanaugh.
rows.output: The Guardian reported that after Flake's request to the FBI, the investigation was continuing into the allegations against Ford and another accuser, Deborah Ramirez.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford jẹ́rìí níwájú ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń rí sí ilé ẹjọ́ nílé Aṣòfin pé Kavanaugh mú ọtí yó, ó sì fipá bá òun lòpọ̀ nígbà tí òun pé ọmọ ọdún mẹ́tàdínlógún.
rows.output: Ford testified before a committee in the House of Representatives that Kavanaugh drank alcohol, and he assaulted her when she was 15 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez ṣàlàyé pé Kavanaugh ṣí nǹkan ọmọkùnrin rẹ̀ fún òun láti rí nígbà tí wọ́n ń dìjọ kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ní Yale. Èyí ṣẹlẹ̀ ni patí kan tí wọ́n lọ láàrin ọdún 1980 síwájú sí i.
rows.output: Ramirez explained that Kavanaugh opened his son's locker for him to see when they were studying at Yale. This happened in a class that they took between 1980 and 1981.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Olùdásílẹ Ìtàkùǹ Àyélujára ń gbèrò láti Bẹ̀rẹ̀ Íntánẹ̀ẹ̀tì Tuntun kan láti lé Mú Google àti Facebook
rows.output: The founder of the Internet Archive is planning to launch a new Internet service to compete with Google and Facebook.
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, olùdásílẹ̀ Ìtàkùn ayélujára, ń ṣe ifilọ́lẹ̀ ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ kan tí ó máa jẹ́ orogún pẹ̀lú Facebook, Amazon àti Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a new initiative that will be funded by Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Iṣẹ́ àkànṣe Ògbóǹtarìgì onímọ̀ ẹ̀rọ, Inrupt, jẹ́ ilé iṣẹ́ tí ó dúró lórí i orísun ìpìlẹ̀ iṣẹ́ Berners-Lee.
rows.output: The World Wide Web project, Inrupt, was a company based on the original source code of the World Wide Web by Berners-Lee.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid fààyè gba àwọn aṣàmúlò láti yan ibi tí dátà wọn yóò di fífipamọ́ sí àti àwọn ènìyàn wo ní wọ́n le ráyè sí àti irú ìwífún tí wọ́n le ráyè sí.
rows.output: Solid fààyè gba àwọn aṣàmúlò láti yan ibi tí dátà wọn yóò di fífipamọ́ sí àti àwọn ènìyàn wo ní wọ́n le ráyè sí àti irú ìwífún tí wọ́n le ráyè sí.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: Nínú ìfọ̀rọ̀wánilẹ́nuwò pẹ́lú ilé iṣẹ́ Fast, Berners-Lee ṣàwàdà pé èròńgbà lẹ́yìn Inrupt ni láti le “jẹ gàba lórí ayé.”
rows.output: In an interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the idea after Inrupt was to "take over the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “A gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe báyìí," ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ nípa ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ náà.
rows.output: "We must do this now," he said, about the start.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: "Ó jẹ́ àkókò onítàn."
rows.output: "It's a time of stories."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ìṣàfilọ́̀lẹ̀ náà ń lo ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ Solid láti fààyègba àwọn ènìyàn láti ṣẹ̀dá “ilé ìtàjà dátà adáni lórí ayélujára” tàbí POD.
rows.output: The campaign is using Solid's technology to empower people to create their own "online data marketplace" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ó le ní àwọn àtòkọ olùbásọ̀rọ̀, ohun-àti-ṣe, kàlẹ́ńdà, ibi ìpamọ́ orin àti àwọn irinṣẹ́ àdáni àti àfyṣiṣẹ́ mìràn.
rows.output: It can have lists of speakers, actions, calendar, music storage, and other custom and automated tools.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ó dábí Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack àti Spotify tí gbogbo wọ́n wà nílẹ̀ lórí aṣawákiri ní àṣìkò kannáà.
rows.output: He also mentioned Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify, all of which were available on the browser at the same time.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ohun tí ó dá yàtọ̀ nípa ilé ìtàjà dátà àdáni ayelujára pé aṣàmúlò ló kù sí lọ́wọ́ láti mọ ẹni tí ó le ráyèsí àti irú ìwífún tó le ráyèsí.
rows.output: The difference with the online data marketplace is that the consumer has no control over who can access and what type of information can be accessed.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ pè ní “Ìrónilágbára àdáni nípaṣẹ̀ dátà.”
rows.output: The company is called "Data-Driven Decision Making."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Èròńgbà fún Inrupt, gẹ́gẹ́bí Olùdásílẹ̀ ilé iṣẹ́ náà John Bruce ṣe sọ, ni pé ó wá fún ilé iṣẹ̀ láti mú àwọn ohun àmúlò, ìlànà àti àwọn ọgbọ́n àtinúdá láti ṣèrànwọ́ láti mú kí Solid wà nílẹ̀ fún gbogbo ènìyàn.
rows.output: The purpose of Inrupt, as stated by the founder of the company John Bruce, is to bring practical, proven methods and tools to bear on making Solid real for everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ náà ní Berners-Lee, Bruce, ètò ìpèsè ààbò tí IBM rà, àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ fúngbàdíẹ̀ tí wọ́n gbà láti ṣiṣẹ́ lórí iṣẹ́ àkànṣe náà, àti àwùjọ àwọn akọkóòdù tí wọ́n jẹ́ olùfarajìn.
rows.output: The company included Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security provision system that IBM acquired, a number of employees who were hired to work on the project, and a community of volunteers who were passionate about the project.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Bẹ́rẹ̀ láti ọ̀ṣẹ̀ yìí, àwọn aṣàmúàgbà ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ káàkiri àgbáyé le ṣldá àwọn ìṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ tiwọ́n ní àkàtà wọ́n nípa lílo àwọn irínṣẹ́ tó wà nílẹ̀ lórí wẹ́ẹ̀bù Inrupt.
rows.output: From this point on, global tech leaders can develop their own decentralized applications by using the tools available on the Inrupt website.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee sọ pé òun àti àwọn akẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀ kò bá “Facebook àti Google” sọ̀rọ̀ nípa bóyá tàbí ki wọ́n ṣètò ìyípadà pátápátá níbi gbogbo àwòṣe òkòwò wọn tí máa yípadà tàbí kí ó soríkodò láìròtẹ́lẹ̀.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said he and his colleagues were not talking to "Facebook and Google" about whether or not to make a fundamental change to their business model that would disrupt the entire advertising industry.
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: "Àwa kò bèèrè fún ìyànda wọn."
rows.output: "We don't need their mercy."
rows.reference: "We are not asking their permission."

rows.source: Nínú àtljíṣẹ́ lórí Medium tí wọ́n tẹ̀jáde ní sátidé, Berners-Lee kọ lórí Inrupts pé “àfojúsùn ni láti pèsè ohun àmúṣagbara olókòwò àti àyíká ilegbèè láti ṣèrànwọ́ ìdáàbòbò àti àmúyẹ wẹ́ẹ̀bù tí a fi Solid ṣe.”
rows.output: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote on Inrupts that "the goal is to provide a robust marketplace and ecosystem to support the development and deployment of web technologies that are built on Solid."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Ní 1994, Berners-Lee tí Ítánẹ̀ẹ̀tì padà nígbàtí ó dá ilé iṣẹ́ wẹ́ẹ̀bù ayélujára sílẹ̀ ní ilé ẹ̀kọ́ ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ ní Massachusetts.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee returned to the Internet when he founded the World Wide Web Company at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: Ní àwọn oṣù bí díẹ̀ ṣẹ́yìn, Berners-Lee ni ó ti jẹ́ ẹní àwòkọ́ṣe níbi ìjíròrò aláìṣègbè.
rows.output: In the past few months, Berners-Lee has been the guest of honor at several international conferences.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Kódà lákòókò ìṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ Inrupt, Berners-Lee sì máa jẹ́ Olùdásílẹ̀ àti Olùdarí ilé iṣẹ́ wẹ́ẹ̀bù ayélujára, ìpìlẹ̀ Wẹ́ẹ̀bù àti ilé iṣẹ́ Dátà Àjọlò.
rows.output: Even during the Inrupt launch, Berners-Lee would remain the founder and director of the World Wide Web, the foundation of the Web and the Open Data Institute.
rows.reference: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: "Mó ní ìrétí ayọ lórí sáà tó ń bọ̀ yìí lórí wẹ́ẹ̀bù,” Bermers-Lee ṣàfikún ọ̀rọ̀.
rows.output: "I am also looking forward to the upcoming session on the web," Bermers-Lee added.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.source: Bernard Vann: Àlùfàá Victoria Cross ti WW1 ní wọ́n ṣayẹyẹ rẹ̀ ṣayẹyẹ rẹ̀
rows.output: Bernard Vann: The WW1 Victoria Cross recipient was honored by a statue
rows.reference: Bernard Vann: WW1 Victoria Cross cleric celebrated

rows.source: Àlùfáà Sọ́ọ̀sì kannáà tí ó wà ní ilẹ̀ Gẹ́ẹ̀sí tó jẹ ẹ̀bún Victoria Cross lákòókò Ogun Àgbáyé Àkọ́kọ́ bí jagunjagun ni wọn ti ṣayẹyẹ rẹ̀ ní ilú abínibí rẹ́ lẹ́yín bí 100.
rows.output: The Anglican priest, who was a Victoria Cross recipient during World War I, was celebrated in his native city after 100 years.
rows.reference: The only Church of England cleric to win a Victoria Cross during World War One as a combatant has been celebrated in his hometown 100 years on.

rows.source: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann gba àmì ẹ̀yẹ náà ní oṣù kẹsàn án 1918 nínú ìkọlù ní Bellenglise àti Lehaucourt.
rows.output: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann received the award in September 1918 in the Battle of Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.
rows.reference: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann won the award on 29 September 1918 in the attack at Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀síbẹ̀, asọnipa kán ló pa á ní bí ọjọ̀ mẹ́rin lẹ́yìn náà tí kò sí mọ̀ pé ó ti jẹ ẹ̀bùn tó ga jùlọ nínú ọ́wọ̀ tó ga jùlọ nínú ilé iṣẹ́ ológun tí ilẹ̀ Gẹ́ẹ̀sì.
rows.output: However, he was only able to survive for four days without knowing that he had been given the highest honor in the hands of the greatest military organization in the British Empire.
rows.reference: However, he was killed by a sniper four days later and never knew he had won the highest British military honour.

rows.source: Òkúta ìṣèrántí ní àwọn ọmọ rẹ̀ méjèèjì fi lọ́lẹ̀ ní ibi ìtólẹ́ṣẹ́ ẹ̀yẹ ní Rushden, Northamptonshire, ní Sátidé.
rows.output: The memorial stone was laid by her two sons at the Rushden Memorial, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.
rows.reference: A commemorative stone was unveiled by his two grandsons at a parade in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.

rows.source: Ọ̀kan nínú àwọn ọmọ ọmọ rẹ̀, Michael Vann, sọ pé ó jẹ́ “àmí tó fọ́gbọ́nyọ”, òkútà náà ní wọ́n máa filọ́lẹ̀ ní kété tí ọdún 100 tí bábá bàbà wọ́n gba àmì ẹ̀yẹ ìborí náà bá pé.
rows.output: One of his grandchildren, Michael Vann, said it was a "symbol of shame", the plaque was removed shortly after the 100th anniversary of the grandfather's award of the medal.
rows.reference: One of his grandsons, Michael Vann, said it was "brilliantly symbolic" the stone would be revealed exactly 100 years on from his grandfather's award-winning feat.

rows.source: Gẹ́gẹ́bí Gásẹ́ẹ̀tì London, ní 29 oṣù kẹsàn án 1918, Lt Col Van ló saájú ìkọ̀ àwọn ọmọ ogun ní ìkọjá Canal de Saint-Quentin “láàrin kurukuru tó nípọ̀n àti lábẹ́ ẹ iná ńlá ńla láti ara àwọn ìbọ́n ẹlẹ́rọ ńlá."
rows.output: As the London Gazette reported, on 29 September 1918, Lt Col Van led the advance of the troops across the Canal de Saint-Quentin "between the gloom of the fog and the glare of the great searchlights from the guns."
rows.reference: According to the London Gazette, on 29 September 1918 Lt Col Vann led his battalion across the Canal de Saint-Quentin "through a very thick fog and under heavy fire from field and machine guns."

rows.source: Ó wà ṣáré lọ sí ibi ìlà ìfàyàgbọta pẹ̀lú “Ìgbòyà tó ga jùlọ” tí ó sì siwájú ikọ̀ náà kí ó tó di wípé ó da ìbọn bolẹ̀ ní òun nìkan tí ó sì pà mẹ́tà nínú àwọn èni náà.
rows.output: He ran to the front of the line with "the highest praise" and continued to the line before he dropped the gun and shot himself alone.
rows.reference: He later rushed up to the firing line and with the "greatest gallantry" led the line forward before rushing a field-gun single-handed and knocked out three of the detachment.

rows.source: Asọnipa Jamaní ló pa Lt Col Vann ní ọjọ 4 oṣù kẹwàá 1918 - ní bí oṣù kan kọjá díẹ̀ kí ogun tó parí.
rows.output: Lieutenant Colonel Vann was killed in action by German sniper fire on 4 October 1918 - just over a month before the end of the war.
rows.reference: Lt Col Vann was killed by a German sniper on 4 October 1918 - just over a month before the war ended.

rows.source: Michael Vann, 72, sọ pé àwọn ìgbéṣẹ̀ bàbà bàbà rẹ̀ jẹ́ “ohun tí mo ma tí ń kóm sì le dà láyé ṣùgbọ́n tí ó jẹ́ ohun ìrẹ̀lẹ.̀”
rows.output: Michael Vann, 72, said that his grandfather's actions were "something I can't live with but that's the way it is."
rows.reference: Michael Vann, 72, said his grandfather's actions were "something that I know that I could never live up to but something which is humbling."

rows.source: Òun àti ẹ̀gbọ́n rẹ̀ Dr James Vann gbé àmì ẹ̀yẹ kalẹ̀ bakan náà lẹ́yìn ìtòlẹ́ṣẹ ẹlẹ́yẹ, èyí tí ẹgbẹ́ eléré ọba Brentwood darí.

rows.source: Michael Vann sọ pé “inú òun dùn láti kópa nínú ìtòlẹ́ṣẹ ẹlẹ́yẹ náà” tí ó sì tún sọ pé “Àtìlẹyìn ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ènìyàn ó ṣàfihàn ìgboyà ojúlówó akọni ńlá."

rows.output: It could be the end of the Ryder Cup that did not meet its own expectations.

rows.source: Mickelson ní ìborí 18. ìpàdánù 20 àti ìdọ́gba méje, lọ́ọ̀tọ́ Furyk sọ pé wíwà níbẹ̀ rẹ̀ mú ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ìyàtọ̀ kan bá àwọn alájọṣepọ̀.
rows.output: Mickelson had a 18-hole lead. Furyk, who was in second place, said that being there made him feel like he had a lot of advantages over his competitors.
rows.reference: Mickelson has 18 wins, 20 losses and seven halves, though Furyk said his presence brought some intangibles to the team.

rows.source: "Ó jẹ́ apanilẹ́rìn ín, ó jẹ́ aláwàdà, ó nífẹ́ láti máa ṣ’ẹ̀fẹ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn ènìyàn, àti pé ọkùnrin tí ó dára ni látin í nínú yàrá alájọṣepọ̀,” ó ṣàlàyé.
rows.output: He was a prankster, he was funny, he loved to be around people, and he was a great guy in the bedroom, he explained.
rows.reference: "He's funny, he's sarcastic, witty, likes to poke fun at people, and he's a great guy to have in the team room," he explained.

rows.source: "Mo rò pé àwọn àkópa tó kéré díẹ̀ gbádùn ara wọn pẹ̀lú rẹ̀, bakan náà, ní ọ̀ṣẹ̀ yìí, tí ó jẹ́ ohun tí ó dùn mọ́ni láti rí.
rows.output: I think that a few of the smaller characters enjoyed themselves with it, too, in this case, which is something that I find very enjoyable to see.
rows.reference: "I think the younger players had fun having a go at him, as well, this week, which was fun to see.

rows.source: Ó pèsè ọ̀pọ̀ ǹkan jú kíkopa nìkan lọ."
rows.output: He provided more than just a role.
rows.reference: He provides a lot more than just play."

rows.source: Olórí yúròpù Thomas Bjorn mọ̀ pé ìléwájú tó pọ̀ má tó tán.
rows.output: European Tour leader Thomas Bjorn knows that the lead is not too big.
rows.reference: Europe captain Thomas Bjorn knows big lead can soon disappear

rows.source: Thomas Bjorn, olórí tí yúrópù, mọ̀ nípa ìrírí pé ìléwájú níwọ́nba tó súnmọ́ ọjọ̀ ìkẹhìn ẹlẹ́nìkan fún Ìfe ẹ̀yẹ Ryder le ṣàdédé yí padà sí ohun tí kò ní rọrùn.
rows.output: Thomas Bjorn, the European Ryder Cup captain, knows that the experience of coming up so close to the last man standing for the Open Championship can make it difficult to adjust to something that is not as easy.
rows.reference: Thomas Bjorn, the European captain, knows from experience that a sizeable lead heading into the last-day singles in the Ryder Cup can easily turn into an uncomfortable ride.

rows.source: The Dane fakọyọ ní ọdún 1997 ní Valderrama, níbití Seve Ballesteros ti ní àmì ayò márùn lórí akẹgbẹ́ wọn láti Amerika, ṣùgbọ́n ṣóńsó imú wọn ní wọ́n fí gbégbá orókè ní ìlà-ìparí tí wọ́n sì borí pẹ̀lú 14½-13½.
rows.output: The Dane won in 1997 at Valderrama, where Seve Ballesteros had a five-point lead on his American opponent, but they were both disqualified in the final round for cheating.
rows.reference: The Dane made his debut in the 1997 match at Valderrama, where a side captained by Seve Ballesteros held a five-point advantage over the Americans but only just got over the finishing line with their noses in front by the narrowest of margins, winning 14½-13½.

rows.source: “Kí ó máa rán ara rẹ létí pé a gbégbá orókè ní Valderrama; a gbìyànjú Brookline bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé a fìdí rẹmi, ṣùgbọ́n ní Valderrama a bórí gíníngínín. Bjorn, sọ pé nígbàtí òun wó ìdíje àwọn kíílàsì 2018 bí wọ́n ṣe borí pẹ̀lú 5-3 ní ọjọ́ Furaide àti ní àná bí wọ́n ṣe borí Le Golf National pẹ̀lú 10-6.
rows.output: "Remember that we were the favorites in Valderrama; we tried Brookline as if we were the favorites, but in Valderrama we were the underdogs. Bjorn said that when he played the 2018 classes as if they were the favorites, they won with 5-3 on Friday and on Saturday they won Le Golf National with 10-6.
rows.reference: "You keep reminding yourself that we had a big lead at Valderrama; we had a big lead at Brookline, where we lost, and at Valderrama, where we won, but only just," said Bjorn, pictured, after watching the Class of 2018 win 5-3 both on Friday and yesterday to lead 10-6 at Le Golf National.

rows.source: Fún ìdí èyí ìtàn máa ṣàfihàn fún mi àti ẹnikẹ́ni nínú alájọṣepọ̀ pe kò tíì tán síbẹ.
rows.output: This story will show me and anyone in the partnership that it's not yet over.
rows.reference: So history will show me and everybody on that team that this is not over.

rows.source: Wàá lọ̀ bí ó ṣe yẹ jùlọ́ ní ọ̀la.
rows.output: Act in the best way possible tomorrow.
rows.reference: You go full bore tomorrow.

rows.source: Jáde síta níbẹ̀yẹn kí o ṣe ohun tí ó yẹ
rows.output: Get out of there and do the right thing
rows.reference: Get out there and do all the right things.

rows.source: Eyi koiti Pati titi waa ni koko Lori boodu.
rows.output: This is not a party matter, but a matter of principle.
rows.reference: This is not over till you've got the points on the board.

rows.source: A ní àfojúsùn, ìyẹn ni láti gbìyànjú láti gba ife ẹ̀yẹ yìí, àtipé ibẹ̀yẹn gan an ní àfojúsùn wà’.
rows.output: Our goal is, that is to try to win this trophy, and that is really our goal.
rows.reference: We have a goal, and that is to try to win this trophy, and that's where the focus stays.

rows.source: Mo ti sọ mláti ìbẹ̀rẹ̀, Mo gbájúmọ́ àwọn èléré ìdárayá 12 tí wọ́n wà lápá ọ̀dọ̀ wa, ṣùgbọ́n a mọ ohun tí ó ń ṣẹlẹ̀ dáadáa ní apá kejì wa -. àwọn eléré ìdárayá tó dára jùlọ ní àgbáyé”
rows.output: I have always been a fan of the 12 sports that are on our side of the world, but we know what's going on over there - the best athletes in the world.
rows.reference: I've said all along, I focus on the 12 players that are in our side, but we are so well aware of what's standing across on the other side - the greatest players in the world."

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú bí inú rẹ̀ ṣe dùn lórí i bí àwọn elére ìdárayá rẹ̀ ṣe fakọyọ sí lórí pápá gọ́ọ̀fù, Bjorn ṣàláyè sí wípé: "Èmi kò ní síwájú ara mi lórí eléyìí.
rows.output: With how happy he was on the golf course, Bjorn said: "I'm not going to be ahead of myself on this one.
rows.reference: Delighted how his players have performed on a tough golf course, Bjorn added: "I would never get ahead of myself in this.

rows.source: Ohun to yàtọ̀ pátápátá ni ọ̀lá jẹ́.
rows.output: The most important thing is respect.
rows.reference: Tomorrow's a different beast.

rows.source: Ọ̀lá jẹ́ ìṣesí ẹ̀nì kọ̀ọ̀kan to ń farahàn, àtipé èyí jẹ́ ohun ti ó yàtọ̀ gedégbé láti ṣe.
rows.output: Pride is a personal attitude, and this is something that is very different from the norm.
rows.reference: Tomorrow is the individual performances that come forward, and that is a different thing to do.

rows.source: Ohun tí ó dára ni láti wà pẹ̀lú enìkan nígbàtí àwọn n[kan bá ńlọ dáradára, ṣùgbọ́n, nígbàtí o ẹ̀nìkọ̀ọ̀kan bá dá wà, nigbànáa ní ìdánwò àdánán máa ṣẹ̀lẹ̀ sí ọ̀ gẹ́gẹ́bí eléré ìdárayá gọ́ọ̀fù.
rows.output: It's better to be with someone when they're doing well, but when you're with someone who's doing poorly, then you're in for a test as if you were a golf ball.
rows.reference: It's great to be out there with a partner when things are going good, but when you're out there individually, then you're tested to the full of your capacity as a golfer.

rows.source: Ìyẹn ní ìfiránṣẹ́ tí o níláti fi ránṣẹ́ sí àwọn elérée ìdárayá, èyí ní láti mú ohun tó dára jùlọ jáde lára rẹ ní ọ̀la.
rows.output: That is the message you have to send to the athletes, in order to bring out the best in you in the future.
rows.reference: That's the message that you need to get across to players, is get the best out of yourself tomorrow.

rows.source: Nísìnyí, o fi ẹnìkejì rẹ sẹ́hìn ó sì níláti lọ mọ́ bí ó sẹ máa mu ohun tó dára jù jáde lát ara rẹ̀, bákan náà."
rows.output: Now, you put your second self behind and have to go find out how to get the best thing out of yourself, too."
rows.reference: Now, you leave your partner behind and he has to go and get the best out of himself, as well."

rows.source: Ní ìdàyàtọ̀ sí Bjorn, opposite number Jim Furyk tí ó jẹ́ nọ́ńbà ìdàkejì máa ma wá àwọn eléré ìdárayá rẹ̀ láti le ní ìṣesí tó dára ní ẹlẹ́nìkọ̀ọ̀kan ju bí wọ́n ṣe ṣe lọ ní aláṣepọ̀, àwọn tó dáyàtọ̀ Jordan Spieth àti Justin Thomas, tí wọ́n ní máàkì mẹ́ta nínú mẹ́rin
rows.output: In contrast to Bjorn, his opposite number Jim Furyk, who is always the second number, will often bring his players to a better feeling in singles than they did in doubles, the contrasting Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas, who have three majors in four.
rows.reference: In contrast to Bjorn, opposite number Jim Furyk will be looking for his players to perform better individually than they did as partners, the exceptions being Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas, who picked up three points out of four.

rows.source: Furyk funra ara rẹ ti wà ní apá méjèèjì ibi ti àwọn ọjọ́ tó kẹ́hìn ńlá ti ṣàdédé yípadà, lẹ́yìn tí ó ti jẹ́ ara àwọn alájọṣepọ̀tó tò borí ní kí ó tó parí rẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́bí aláìláṣeyọrí ní Yúrópù mú kí “Ìyànu ńlá ní Mẹ̀dínà” ti ara rẹ̀ jáde.
rows.output: Furyk himself was on both sides of the great turning point of the last days, after having been a partner in the great European failure, which led to his "Great Miracle in the Middle East" emerging from himself.
rows.reference: Furyk himself has been on both ends of those big last-day turnarounds, having been part of the winning team at Brookline before ending up a loser as Europe pulled off the "Miracle at Medinah."

rows.source: “Mo ránti gbogbo gbolohun kọ̀ọ̀kan tó jẹ jáde nínú rẹ̀,” ó sọ̀rọ̀ ní ìfèsì sí ìbéèrè bí Ben Crenshaw, olórí ilé ní 1999, ṣe ṣàtòjọ̀ àwọn eléré ìdárayá rẹ̀ lásìkò ìgbà ìkẹ̀hìn náà.
rows.output: "I remember every word of it," he said in response to a question about how Ben Crenshaw, the 1999 champion, had listed his players during the final round.
rows.reference: "I remember every damn word of it," he said in reply to being asked how Ben Crenshaw, the captain in 1999, had rallied his players heading into the last day.

rows.source: "A ní ìfigagbága 12 tó ṣe pàtàkì lóla, ṣùgbọ́n o máa fẹ́ láti tètè dé ibi ìyára bẹ̀rẹ̀ bí i ọ ṣe rí i ní Brookline, bí o ṣe rí i ní Medinah.
rows.output: "We have 12 important goals for the year, but you will want to quickly reach the starting point as you see it in Brookline, as you see it in Medinah."
rows.reference: "We have 12 important matches tomorrow, but you'd like to get off to that fast start like you saw at Brookline, like you saw at Medinah.

rows.source: Nígbà abala kan bá ń lọ dáadáa, ó máa rán àwon ìfigagbaga ààrín lọ́wọ̀.
rows.output: When one part of the body is healthy, it can send nutrients to the other parts.
rows.reference: When that momentum gets going one way, it puts a lot of pressure on those middle matches.

rows.source: A ṣètò ìtọ̀ gbọorọ̀ wa lórí ìlà lọ́wọ̀ọ̀wọ́ tí a sí mú kí àwọn ẹni tiwa jẹ́ jádení ọ̀nà àrà ọ̀tọ̀ tí ó wù wá, o mọ̀, a ń gbìyànjú láti pidán lọla."
rows.output: We have set up our camp on the shore, and we have made our people into a den of thieves, you know, we are trying to loot the future.
rows.reference: We set up our line-up accordingly and put the guys out in the fashion that we felt like, you know, we're trying to make some magic tomorrow."

rows.source: Thomas ní ó gba iṣẹ́ pàtàkì lórí dídarí ìjagbara àti kíkojú Rory Mcllroy nínú ìfigagbaga to le jù, Pẹ̀lú Paul Casey, Justin Rose, Jon Rahim, Tommy Fleetwood and Ian Poulte tThomas has been handed the task of trying to lead the fightback and faces Rory McIlroy in the top match, with Paul Casey, Justin Rose, Jon Rahm, Tommy Fleetwood and Ian Poulter tí wọ́n jẹ́ ara Yúrópù núnú ìdámejì ìtòléra láti òkè.
rows.output: Thomas has been handed the task of trying to lead the fightback and faces Rory McIlroy in the top match, with Paul Casey, Justin Rose, Jon Rahm, Tommy Fleetwood and Ian Poulter all of Europe in the second tier from the top.
rows.reference: Thomas has been handed the task of trying to lead the fightback and faces Rory McIlroy in the top match, with Paul Casey, Justin Rose, Jon Rahm, Tommy Fleetwood and Ian Poulter the other Europeans in the top half of the order.

rows.source: "Mo ti wà pẹ̀lú àwọn ọ̀wọ̀ àwọn ẹni wọ̀nyìí nínú ìtòléra yìí nítorípé mo rò pé ó kó àkóyáwọ́,” Bjorn ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ nípa àwọn àkopa ẹlẹ́nìkọ̀ọ̀an rẹ̀.
rows.output: "I've been with these people in this camp because I think it's a very important cause," Bjorn said about his fellow competitors.
rows.reference: "I went with this group of guys in this order because I think it covers all the way through," said Bjorn of his singles selections.

rows.source: Ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi tuntun ti Germany ti di sísún síwájú lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi
rows.output: The new German warship has been launched for the first time
rows.reference: Germany's new warship postponed yet again

rows.source: Àkọ̀tun Ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi ti Jámáànù ní ó yẹ kí ó ti di fífi lọ́lẹ̀ ní ọdún 2014 láti pààrọ̀ àwọn ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi Sáà-ogún Dúkùú, ṣùgbọ́n kò ní rí bẹ́ẹ̀ títí di, ó kéré jù, ọdún í ó ń bọ̀ nítorí àwọn èròjà tó ti bàjẹ̀ àti àwọn ìnáwò tó ti ṣarajọ, ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn abẹ́léni ó jábọ̀ rẹ̀.
rows.output: The Royal Navy of Jamaica was expected to be decommissioned in 2014 to replace the 16-year-old Duke-class ships, but it did not happen until, at least, the following year due to damaged equipment and funding issues, local media reported.
rows.reference: German Navy's newest frigate should have been commissioned in 2014 to replace ageing Cold War-era warships, but it won't be there until at least the next year due to faulty systems and snowballing cost, local media reported.

rows.source: Síṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ "Rheinland-Pfalz," olórí ọkọ̀ ogun ojú omi tí ìsọ̀rí fírígéètì Baden-Wuerttemberg tuntun nini, ni ó ti di sísún ṣíwájú títi di ìdájì àkọ́kọ́ ọdún 2019, gẹ́gẹ́bi ìwé ìròyìn Die Zeit ṣe sọ tí ọgá ológun kan sọ.
rows.output: The launch of "Rheinland-Pfalz," the new flagship of the Baden-Wuerttemberg military district, has been accelerated to the first half of 2019, as reported by the newspaper Die Zeit, citing a military official.
rows.reference: Commissioning of the "Rheinland-Pfalz," the lead ship of the brand new Baden-Wuerttemberg-class frigates, has now been postponed until the first half of 2019, according to Die Zeit newspaper citing a military spokesman.

rows.source: Ó yẹ kí ọkọ̀ ojú omi nlá náà darapọ̀ ní 2014, ṣùgbọ̀n àwọn wàhálà ìṣòro lẹ́yìn ìfakalẹ̀ rẹ̀ ní ó mú kí ìgbẹ́kẹ́lé nínú itẹ̀síwájú àkànṣe iṣẹ́ náà já sófo.
rows.output: The ship should have been launched in 2014, but the troubles following its launch caused a loss of confidence in the project's progress.
rows.reference: The vessel should have joined the Navy in 2014, but the troubling post-delivery issues plagued the fate of the ambitious project.

rows.source: Àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá mẹ́rin ti ìsọ̀rí Baden-Wuerttemberg tí Àwọn ọmọ ogún ojú omi sànwó fún ;áti 2007 máa wá gẹ́gẹ́bí arọ́pò sí ìṣọ̀rí àwọn fírígéétì Bremen.
rows.output: Four large passenger ships of the Baden-Wuerttemberg series, which were built for the 2007 World Expo, will serve as replacements for the Bremen class frigates.
rows.reference: The four Baden-Wuerttemberg-class vessels the Navy ordered back in 2007 will come as replacement to the ageing Bremen-class frigates.

rows.source: Ó yé wá pé wọ́n máa ṣàfihàn Kanọ́ọ̀nù tó lágbara,ọ̀wọ́ àwọn mísáìlì aṣòdì-sí-bàálù àti aṣòdì-sí-ọkọ̀ orí omi àti àwọn ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ nǹka ìjagun mìíràn, bíi rédà, ínfúrárẹ́ẹ̀dì àti àwọn ìfọ́wọ́sí abáfẹfẹ́ṣiṣẹ́.
rows.output: They will also demonstrate the latest in cruise missiles, torpedoes, and other naval gunnery systems, such as the Red Storm and the Harpoon air-launched missile.
rows.reference: It is understood they will feature a powerful cannon, an array of anti-aircraft and anti-ship missiles as well as some stealth technologies, such as reduced radar, infrared and acoustic signatures.

rows.source: Àwọn ohun pàtàkì mìràn gẹ́gẹ́bí ìgbà ìṣàbójútó lóòrèkóòrè - p yẹ kó ṣeéṣe láti ṣàfillẹ̀ awọn fírígéètì fún bí ọdún méjì jìnnà sí ìbúdó \kọ ojú omi.
rows.output: Other important factors such as the seasonality of the fishery - for example, it may be possible to freeze the fish for up to two years from the port of departure.
rows.reference: Other important features include longer maintenance periods - it should be possible to deploy the newest frigates for up to two years away from home ports.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀síbẹ̀, ìdádúró gbogbo ìgbà túmọ̀ sí wípé àwọn ọkọ̀ ojú omi ìṣaajú - tí wọn sọ pé ó jẹ́ kí ilẹ̀ jámánì ní agbara ní òkè òkun - ti máa di èyí tí kò bá ìgbà mu mọ́ ní àkókò tí wọ́n bá wọ iṣẹ́. Die Zelt ló pe àkíyèsí yìí.
rows.output: However, the continuous stoppage means that the old cargo ships - which are said to give Germany dominance at sea - will only be able to stay in service for a short time when they enter the workforce. The Zelt refers to this observation.
rows.reference: However, continuous delays mean that the cutting-edge warships - said to allow Germany to project power overseas - will already become outdated by the time they enter service, Die Zeit notes.

rows.source: Fírígèètì F125 tí ó kùnà náà gba gogbo ìròyìn kan ní ọdún tó kọjá, nígbàtí Àwọn ọmọ ogun ojú omi kọ̀ jàlẹ̀ láti ṣafilọlẹ̀ ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá náà tí wọ́n sì dá a padà sí ìlé iṣẹ́ ọkọ̀ ojú omi Blohm & Voss ní Hamburb.
rows.output: The failed F125 project took up all the news last year, while the Navy refused to release the aircraft carrier and returned it to the Blohm & Voss shipyard in Hamburg.
rows.reference: The ill-fated F125 frigate made headlines last year, when the German Navy officially refused to commission the vessel and returned it to Blohm & Voss shipyard in Hamburg.

rows.source: Èyí jẹ ìgbà àkọ́kọ́ tí Àwọn ọ́mọ ogun ojú omi máa dá ọkọ̀ ojú omi padà fún ilé iṣẹ́ ọkọ̀ ojú omi ṣiṣe lẹ́yìn tí wọn ti fà á kalẹ̀.
rows.output: This is the first time that the Navy will return a ship to the shipbuilding industry since it was decommissioned.
rows.reference: This was the first time the Navy has returned a ship to a shipbuilder after delivery.

rows.source: Díẹ̀ ní a mọ̀ nípa ìdí tí ọkọ̀ ojú omi náà fi di dídá padà, ṣùgbọ́n àwọn oníwè ìròyìn jámànù sọ díẹ nípa “àṣìṣe sọ́fútìwíà àti hádìwíà” tí ó mú kí ọkọ̀ ìfijagun ojú omi náà má wúlò tí ó bá di lílò ní ojú ogun.
rows.output: Some things are known about why the ship was converted, but the ship's owners have said little about "software and hardware errors" that made the ship useless when it was put into service.
rows.reference: Little was known about the reasons behind the return, but German media cited a number of crucial "software and hardware defects" that made the warship useless if deployed on a combat mission.

rows.source: Àìpé sọ́fùtiwìà jẹ́ ohún tí ó ṣe pàtàkì gan nítorí awọn 120 awakọ̀ ojú omi ni wọ́n máa wa ìsọ̀rí ọkọ̀ ojú omi ńlá Baden-Wuerttemberg-class náà - èyí tí ó jẹ́ ìdájí àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ nínú àwọn fírígéètì ìsọ̀rí Bremen àtijọ́.
rows.output: The lack of software is a major problem because 120 seafarers are needed to navigate the large Baden-Wuerttemberg-class ships - this is a significant increase from the 30 employees in the Bremen-class ships.

rows.source: O ti to ọdun mẹwa lati igbati igberiko Gusu ti New York ti ṣe idajọ ẹjọ iku kan.

rows.source: Ni igba ikẹhin ti a funni ni idajọ iku nni ẹjọ Gbogboogbo New York ni 1953 fun Julius ati Ethel Rosenberg, tọkọtaya kan ti a pa lẹhin ti wọn ti fi ẹsun iyọkẹlẹ wolu fun Soviet Union nigba ogun buburu ni ọdun meji ṣaaju.
rows.output: In the last year of the death penalty in the United States, the Supreme Court of New York in 1953 sentenced Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple who were executed after being convicted of espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War two years earlier.
rows.reference: The last time the death penalty was carried out in a New York federal case was in 1953 for Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple executed after they were convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War two years before.

rows.output: Both Rosenbergs were executed by electric chair on June 19, 1953.
