rows.source: Sashen Turai na Thomas Bjorn, mai neman riƙe kofin ba su ci nasara ba a Hazeltine shekaru biyu da suka wuce, da mamaye wani rashin sa’a a sashen Amurka a cikin ƙwallaye huɗu na safe, inda suka ɗauki jere-jere 3 da 1.
rows.output: The European section of Thomas Bjorn, who were seeking to retain the title, did not win at Hazeltine two years ago, and were plagued by bad luck in the American section in the first four holes, where they took a 3-1 lead.
rows.reference: Thomas Bjorn's European side, bidding to retain the trophy they lost at Hazeltine two years ago, dominated a misfiring American side in the morning fourballs, taking the series 3-1.

rows.source: Amurka ta ƙara turjiya a cikin huɗu-huɗun, tana ci nasarar wasanni biyu, amma sun gagara ci a cikin tawayar.
rows.output: The United States added four more points in the fourth quarter, winning two games, but failed to score in the comeback.
rows.reference: The U.S. offered more resistance in the foursomes, winning two matches, but they could not eat into the deficit.

rows.source: Sashen Jim Furyk suna buƙatar ɗigo-ɗigo daga wasanni ɗaiɗaiku 12 na ranar Lahadi don riƙe kofin.
rows.output: The Jim Furyk Group needs to dig deep from their 12 individual games on Sunday to hold the cup.
rows.reference: Jim Furyk's side need eight points from Sunday's 12 singles matches to retain the trophy.

rows.source: Fleetwood shi ne farkon rookie na Turai da ya ci ɗigo-ɗigo huɗu a yayin da shi da Molinari, da aka cewa "Molliwood" bayan wani ƙarshen mako da ake magana kuma kawai su ne haɗin biyu da suka ci ɗigo-ɗigo hudu daga budewa wasanninsu huɗu a cikin tarihin Ryder Cup.
rows.output: Fleetwood was the first European rookie to win four holes in a row during the opening two days, along with Molinari, who were dubbed "Molliwood" after a weekend that was spoken of and the only pair to win four holes from the start of their four matches in the history of the Ryder Cup.
rows.reference: Fleetwood is the first European rookie to win four points in a row while he and Molinari, dubbed "Molliwood" after a sensational weekend are only the second pair to win four points from their opening four matches in Ryder Cup history.

rows.source: Bayan sun buge Woods da Patrick Reed a cikin ƙwallaye huɗun sai kuma suka tashi suke buge Woods da rookie na Amurka Bryson Dechambeau ta kuma wani abin gani na 5 da 4.
rows.output: After they beat Woods and Patrick Reed in the four-ball, they rose to beat Woods and American rookie Bryson DeChambeau by another 5 and 4.
rows.reference: Having crushed Woods and Patrick Reed in the fourballs they then gelled superbly to beat a deflated Woods and American rookie Bryson Dechambeau by an even more emphatic 5&4.

rows.source: Woods, wanda ya ja kansa zuwa cikin wasanni biyu a ranar Asabar, ya nuna wata bayyana ta ilimi amma yanzu ya rasa 19 na wasanninsa a cikin ƙwallaye huɗu da wasannin huɗu-huɗu da bakwai a cikin wani jeri.
rows.output: Woods, who pulled himself into two games on Saturday, showed a display of academic intelligence but now has lost 19 of his games in four-pointers and four-quarter games and seven in a row in a streak.

rows.source: Justin Rose, ya huta don ƙwallaye huɗu na safen, ya dawo ga abokin hulɗa Henrik Stenson a cikin wasannin huɗu-huɗu zuwa ga wata dokewa 2 da 1 ci na Dustin Johnson da Brooks Koepka - mai kima ɗaya da uku a cikin duniya.
rows.output: Justin Rose, who had four birdies in the first round, returned to partner Henrik Stenson in the four-ball match against Dustin Johnson and Brooks Koepka - who were both ranked one and three in the world.

rows.source: Turai ba ta samu ba yadda take da sauki, ranar kudu-maso-yamma mai iska ta Paris.
rows.output: Europe has not been as easy to navigate as the sunny southwest of France.

rows.output: Three-time major winner Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas set up an all-American final round with two under-par scores on Saturday.

rows.source: Kawai sau ɗaya ne a tarihin Ryder Cup wata ƙungiya ta sake dawowa daga wani rasa ɗigo huɗu a cikin ɗaiɗaiku,  kodayake kamar yadda masu riƙon na sashen Furyk ke buƙatar kawai tsayuwar doki don riƙe kofin.
rows.output: Only once in the history of the Ryder Cup has a team come back from a deficit of four points in singles, although as it turned out, all that was needed was a steady horse to hold the cup.

rows.output: After being the second best for two days, but, a Sunday attack was like it would be their strongest.

rows.source: Koriya ta Arewa ta ce ‘ba yadda’ za ta rage makami ita kaɗai ba tare da aminci ba

rows.output: The North Korean Foreign Minister told the United Nations on Saturday that continued sanctions are pushing the country further into the arms of the United States and that there is no way the country will give up its nuclear weapons under any circumstances.
rows.reference: North Korea's foreign minister told the United Nations on Saturday continued sanctions were deepening its mistrust in the United States and there was no way the country would give up its nuclear weapons unilaterally under such circumstances.

rows.source: Ri Yong ya faɗa wa Babban Taro na shekara na na hukumar duniya cewa Koriya ta Arewa ta yi “masu matakai na mutunci” a cikin shekarar ta da wuce, kamar tsaida gwaje-gwajen nukiliya da makamai masu linzami, rusa wurin gwajin nukiliya, kuma da yin alkawari ba za ta ƙara makaman nukiliya da fasahar nukiliya ba.
rows.output: Ri Yong told the UN General Assembly that North Korea had taken "measures of self-restraint" in the previous year, such as halting nuclear tests and ballistic missile launches, dismantling the nuclear test site, and promising not to add more nuclear weapons and nuclear technology.
rows.reference: Ri Yong Ho told the world body's annual General Assembly that North Korea had taken "significant goodwill measures" in the past year, such as stopping nuclear and missiles tests, dismantling the nuclear test site, and pledging not to proliferate nuclear weapons and nuclear technology.

rows.source: "Amma, ba mu ga kowane abu na martani daga Amurka,” inji shi.
rows.output: "But we haven't seen any reaction from America," he said.

rows.source: “Ba tare da kowane aminci ba na Amurka ba za a sami ƙarfin gwiwa a cikin tsaronmu na ƙasa kuma a ƙarƙashin ire-iren yanayin babu wata hanya da mu kaɗai za mu rage makamai mu da farko.”
rows.output: “Without the safety of the United States, there will be no strength in our national security and under any circumstances we alone will not be able to reduce our weapons first.”
rows.reference: "Without any trust in the U.S. there will be no confidence in our national security and under such circumstances there is no way we will unilaterally disarm ourselves first."

rows.source: A yayin da Rike same maimaita koke-koken Koriya ta Kudu da aka sani game da ƙin Washington na bin wata hanyar “a hankali” don rage makaman nukiliyat a ƙarƙashinsa da za a ba da kyauta ga Koriya ta Arewan a yayin da ɗauki wasu matakai a hankali, jawabin nasa ya bayyana da muhimmanci saboda ba ta ƙi rage makaman nukiliyar ita kaɗai ba haka kawai kamar yadda Pyongyang ɗin ta yi a baya ba.
rows.output: While Riek repeated the familiar South Korean refrain that Washington should follow a "phased" approach to reducing its nuclear arsenal and give North Korea a "peaceful" reward in exchange for denuclearization, his statement was important because it did not simply echo Pyongyang's previous demands.
rows.reference: While Ri reprised familiar North Korean complaints about Washington's resistance to a "phased" approach to denuclearization under which North Korea would be rewarded as it took gradual steps, his statement appeared significant in that it did not reject unilateral denuclearization out of hand as Pyongyang has done in the past.

rows.source: Ri ya yi dube ne ga wani jawabin hadin gwiwa daga Kim Jong Un da Donald Trump a wani babban taro da aka taba yi tsakanin shugaban Amurka mai ci da wani shugaban Koriya ta Arewa a cikin Singapore a ranar 12 ga Yuni, a lokacin da Kim ya yi alkawari yin aiki zuwa ga "rage makaman nukiliya a zirin Koriya" a lokacin da Trump ya yi alkawarin ba da garanti na tsaron Koriya ta Arewa din.
rows.output: He looked at a joint statement from Kim Jong Un and Donald Trump at a summit between the US president and North Korean leader in Singapore on June 12, when Kim pledged to work towards "denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula" while Trump promised to provide a guarantee of North Korea's security.
rows.reference: Ri referred to a joint statement issued by Kim Jong Un and Donald Trump at a first ever summit between a serving U.S. president and a North Korean leader in Singapore on June 12, when Kim pledged to work toward "denuclearization of the Korean peninsula" while Trump promised guarantees of North Korea's security.

rows.source: Koriya ta Arewa tana neman wani kawo wa ƙarshen Yakin Koriya na shekarun 1950 zuwa 53, amma Amurkan ta ce Pyongyang dole ta bar makamanta na nukiliya daga farko.
rows.output: North Korea is seeking a way to end the Korean War of 1950-53, but the US says Pyongyang must first give up its nuclear weapons.
rows.reference: North Korea has been seeking a formal end to the 1950-53 Korea War, but the United States has said Pyongyang must give up its nuclear weapons first.

rows.source: Haka kuma Washington ta ki kiraye-kiraye na ta sassauta takunkumin ƙasa-da-ƙasa a kan Koriya ta Arewa.
rows.output: And Washington also rejected calls to ease international sanctions on North Korea.
rows.reference: Washington has also resisted calls to relax tough international sanctions on North Korea.

rows.source: “Amurka ta jajirce a kan “barin nukiliya daga farko” kuma ta ƙara matakin matsai ta takunkumi don cimma manufarta a cikin halin tilastawa, da kuma ma ƙin “furuci na ƙarshen yaƙi,”” inji Ri.
rows.output: "United States is committed to 'zero nuclear first use' and has increased the level of its deterrence to achieve its goal in a coercive manner, and to reject the 'end of war declaration," said Ri.
rows.reference: "The U.S. insists on the "denuclearization-first" and increases the level of pressure by sanctions to achieve their purpose in a coercive manner, and even objecting to the "declaration of the end of war,"" Ri said.

rows.source: “Fahimta ta cewa takunkumi zai iya kawo mu kan gwiwowinmu wani mafarki ne na mutane waɗanda suka zahilci abu game da mu.
rows.output: "Understanding that restrictions can bring us to our knees is a dream of people who are ignorant about us.

rows.source: Amma matsalar ita ce ci gaba da takunkumi suna kara rashin yardarmu.”
rows.output: But the problem is that the continued restrictions are only making us more unpopular.

rows.source: Ri bai yi furuci na shirye-shirye don wani babban taro na biyu tsakanin Kim da Trump wanda shugaban Amurka da ya tsokaci a Majalisar Ɗinkin Duniya a cikin farkon makon.
rows.output: He did not make any specific predictions for a second summit between Kim and Trump, who was addressing the United Nations General Assembly in the early part of the week.

rows.output: Instead, the minister made a reference to three meetings between Kim and South Korean President Moon Jae-in in the past five months and added that: "If a country in this issue is leaving nuclear weapons, it would be South Korea, not the United States leaving nuclear weapons in the Korean Peninsula, which has not had such a problem."
rows.reference: The minister instead highlighted three meetings between Kim and South Korean leader Moon Jae-in in the past five months and added: "If the party to this issue of denuclearization were South Korea and not the U.S., the denuclearization of the Korean peninsula would not have come to such a deadlock."

rows.source: Duk da haka, lafazin jawabin na Ri ya dan zama daban daga na shekarar da ta gabata, a lokacin da ya gaya wa Babban Taro na Majalisar Ɗinkin Duniyar cewa cikin yankin Amurka da rokokin Koriya wani abu ne da dole zai wakana bayan “Mista Shugaba Mai Neman Bala’i” Trup ya kira Kim da wani “mutum mai roka” da ke neman kashe kansa.
rows.output: However, the tone of Ri's speech was slightly different from that of the previous year, when he told the General Assembly of the United Nations that something had to be done about the "Mr. President of the Apocalypse" Trup called Kim a "rocket man" seeking to commit suicide.
rows.reference: Even so, the tone of Ri's speech was dramatically different from last year, when he told the U.N. General Assembly that targeting the U.S. mainland with North Korea's rockets was inevitable after "Mr Evil President" Trump called Kim a "rocket man" on a suicide mission.

rows.source: Wannan shekarar a Majalisar Ɗinkin Duniya, Trump, wanda shekarar da ta gabata ya yi barazana ta “rusa gaba ɗaya” Koriya ta Arewa, ya yabi Kim don karfin halinsa na ɗaukan matakai na rage makamai, amma ya ce har yanzu a akwai aiki da dole za a yi kuma takunkumi suna nan sa har Koriya ta Arewan ta bar nukiliya.
rows.output: This year at the United Nations, Trump, who last year threatened to "completely destroy" North Korea, praised Kim for his willingness to take steps to reduce his nuclear arsenal, but said that there was still work to be done and that sanctions would remain in place until North Korea denuclearized.
rows.reference: This year at the United Nations, Trump, who last year threatened to "totally destroy" North Korea, heaped praise on Kim for his courage in taking steps to disarm, but said much work still had to be done and sanctions must remain in place until North Korea denuclearizes.

rows.source: A ranar Laraba, Trump ya ce ba ya da lokaci ƙayyadedde don wannan, yana cewa “Idan zai ɗauki shekaru biyu, shekaru uku ko shekaru biyar - ba damuwa.”
rows.output: On Wednesday, Trump said he didn't have a specific time for this, saying, "If it takes two years, three years or five years - no problem."

rows.output: But U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo told the United Nations Security Council on Thursday that: "The sanctions of the Security Council must be maintained in full force and effect until we see the complete, verified, irreversible dismantlement of nuclear weapons."
rows.reference: However, U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo told the U.N. Security Council on Thursday that: "Enforcement of Security Council sanctions must continue vigorously and without fail until we realize the fully, final, verified denuclearization."

rows.output: The United Nations Security Council has imposed sanctions on North Korea since 2006 in an effort to curb funding for Pyongyang's nuclear and ballistic missile programs.

rows.output: Pompeo met with Ri on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, where he said after that he would be returning to Pyongyang next month to prepare for a second summit.

rows.output: A new course at Harvard University this year has provided all students with additional sleep in an effort to combat the growing trend of all-night study sessions by consuming caffeine.

rows.output: The course began with a first session this year, explaining to students the benefits of good sleep habits in helping with learning and athletic performance, as well as improving their overall health.

rows.output: Paul Barreira, a professor of psychiatry at the Harvard Medical School's Department of Psychiatry and the director of the school's Center for Medical Ethics, said the school decided to offer the course after it found that students were being severely restricted in their ability to sleep during the week.

rows.output: The UK "will always be aware of it" if it fails to maintain its position as the world's leading car manufacturer after Brexit, said Secretary of State for Business Greg Clark.

rows.source: Ya kara cewa abun “damuwa ne” cewa Toyota UK ta fada wa BBC cewa idan Britain ta fita EU ba tare da yarjejeniya ba zata sayar da aiki na dan wani lokaci a masana’antar ta a Burnaston, kusa da Derby.
rows.output: He added that it was "concerning" that Toyota UK had told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal, it would temporarily halt production at its factory in Burnaston, near Derby.

rows.source: Masana’antar Burnaston din - wanda ke hada Toyota Auris da Avensis - sun kera kusan motoci 150,000 bara wanda a ciki kashi 90 aka fitar zuwa sauran kasashen Turai.

rows.source: “A gani na shi ne idan Britain ta fita EU a karshen Maris zamu ga sayawar kira a masana;antar mu,” inji Mavin Cooke, Manajin Direkta na Toyota a Burnaston.
rows.output: "I can see it now that if Britain leaves the EU at the end of March we will see a surge in demand for our cars," said Mavin Cooke, director of manufacturing at Toyota in Burnaston.
rows.reference: "My view is that if Britain crashes out of the EU at the end of March we will see production stops in our factory," said Marvin Cooke, Toyota's managing director at Burnaston.

rows.output: Some UK car manufacturers have expressed concern about the UK leaving the EU without a deal on how the border trade will be, including Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.

rows.output: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on 29 March, there could be problems at the border which the industry says can cause delays and shortages.

rows.output: This attack required "significant planning and preparation," the prosecutors said, describing how Saipov took it as "a deliberate, evil act and a cowardly act."

rows.source: Labour abughịzị ụka gbasara agbasa.

rows.source: Elee anya, abụ onye nke kachasị ọhụrụ n’ahịrị nke MP ndị Labour agwara na anabataghị - naanị maka ikwu uche anyị.
rows.output: However, I am the most recent person in the line of Labour MPs who have been told that they are not welcome - just to make a point.

rows.output: In my opinion, the anti-Semitism accusations criticized me for questioning Jeremy Corbyn.
rows.reference: In my case, the censure motion criticised me for disagreeing with Jeremy Corbyn.

rows.source: Na mkpa nke iwu akụnụba obodo ziri ezi, nche obodo, yana Europe, n’ụzọ ọzọ otu nsogbu ndị Jeremy jiri na ekwenyeghị na ndị isi gara aga.
rows.output: In the need for sound national economic policy, national security, and Europe, in other words, one of the problems Jeremy has with the previous leadership.
rows.reference: On the importance of a responsible economic policy, on national security, on Europe, ironically similar issues on which Jeremy disagreed with previous leaders.

rows.source: Ọkwa maka nzụkọ Nottingham East Labour na Fraịde kwuru na “anyị chọrọ nzụkọ ndị ahụ bụrụ nke dum ma mịpụta mkpụrụ.”
rows.output: The level for the Nottingham East Labour meeting on Friday said that "we need the meetings to be full and to bear fruit."
rows.reference: The notice for the Nottingham East Labour meeting on Friday stated that "we want the meetings to be inclusive and productive."

rows.source: N’imirikiti afọ asatọ m ka MP Labour mpaghara ahụ, abalị Fraịde nzụkọ GC na abụkarị nke ahụ.
rows.output: In the last eight years, I have been the Labour MP for the area, and the Friday night GC meeting is usually mine.
rows.reference: For most of my eight years as the local Labour MP, the Friday night GC meetings have been exactly that.

rows.source: Na mwute taa, ọ bụghị olu nke imirikiti nzụkọ yana ndọrọndọrọ “obi ọma, ume ala” ekwere na nkwa bụ ihe ndị echefugoro kemgbe ma ọ bụrụ, n’ezie, o bidoro ma ncha.
rows.output: Today, it is the voice of the meeting of the minds and the "goodwill, soft power" that were promised are the things that have been forgotten since, or rather, they have been starting points but have been washed away.
rows.reference: Sadly today, it is not the tone of many meetings and the promise of "kinder, gentler" politics has long been forgotten if, indeed, it ever began.

rows.source: Ọ bụ ihe pụtara ihie nke ukwuu na anaghị anabata nghọta dị iche iche na ndọrọndọrọ Labour, ọzọkwa a na ekpezi echiche ọ bụla ma a ga-anabata ya n’ọchịchị ndọrọndọrọ ahụ.
rows.output: It is a significant issue that the Labour Party does not accept different interpretations of its policies, and any opinion is not accepted in the party's leadership.
rows.reference: It has become increasingly apparent that differing views are not tolerated in the Labour party and every opinion is judged on whether it is acceptable to the party leadership.

rows.source: Nke a bidoro ozugbo Jeremy bụrụ onye isi, ndị ọrụ ibe m, ndị m chere na mụ na ha na ekekọrịta otu nghọta ndọrọndọrọ bidoro tụba anya na m ga-atụgharị ozugbo ma were ọnọdụ ndị m ga-agaghị ekwekọrịta na ya otu ọ bụla - ma ọ bụ na nchedo obodo ma ọ bụ otu ahịa EU.
rows.output: This started immediately when Jeremy became leader, my colleagues, with whom I thought I shared a common understanding of the political direction, began to push me to turn around and take up positions that I would never agree with - either on national security or the EU market.
rows.reference: This started shortly after Jeremy became leader, as colleagues with whom I had previously thought I shared a similar political outlook began expecting me to do a U-turn and take positions I would never have otherwise agreed with - whether on national security or the EU single market.

rows.source: Mgbe ọ bụla m kwuru okwu n’ọhaneze - ọ gaghị agbasata ihe m kwuru - a na enwe nkwụtọ dị ukwuu na esote ozugbo n’ebe mmerịkọta ọhaneze na akpọ maka mwepu, nkatọ ndọrọndọrọ nke etiti, na agwa m na m ekwesịghị ịnọ na ndọrọndọrọ Labour.
rows.output: Whenever I speak in public - it will not be reported - there is a great deal of pressure following immediately on the media and calls for my removal, criticism of my centrality, and the fact that I should not be in the Labour Party.
rows.reference: Whenever I speak publicly - and it doesn't really matter what I say - there follows a tirade of abuse on social media calling for deselection, denouncing the politics of the centre, telling me I should not be in the Labour party.

rows.source: Ma nke a abụghị naanị m.
rows.output: But this is not just about me.
rows.reference: And that is not just my experience.

rows.source: N’ezie, ama m na m ka nwee ihu ọma karịa ụfọdụ ndị ọrụ ibe m n’ihi asịsa ndị ezitere m na abụkarị maka ndọrọndọrọ.
rows.output: Of course, I know I'm better than some of my colleagues because I'm always the one who's sent to do the dirty work.
rows.reference: Indeed, I know I am more fortunate than some of my colleagues as the comments directed at me tend to be political.

rows.source: Enwere m ntụmanya n’arụmọrụ na mkpebi nke ndị ọrụ ibe m ndị ahụ na enweta nkatọ okike mmadụ ma ọ bụ agbụrụ ya kwa ụbọchị mana ha anaghị agba ọsọ.
rows.output: I have high expectations for the performance and decisions of my colleagues, who are constantly receiving criticism of their creativity or race, but they are not running away.
rows.reference: I am in awe of the professionalism and determination of those colleagues who face a torrent of sexist or racist abuse every day but never shy away.

rows.source: Otu n’ime akụkụ kachasị ada mmụọ nke oge ndọrọndọrọ a bụ otu okwu nkatọ ndị jọrọ njọ si buru ihe nkịtị.
rows.output: One of the most depressing aspects of this era is how harsh criticism can make something mundane seem so extraordinary.
rows.reference: One of the most disappointing aspects of this era of politics is how levels of abuse have become normalised.

rows.source: Jeremy Corbyn na arịọ n’izu gara aga na ndọrọndọrọ Labour kwesịrị ịmụta omume nke ndidi.

rows.source: Eziokwu bụ na anyị abụghịzị ụka ahụ gbasara agbasa, kwa ụkpụrụ “enweghị ntụkwasị obi” ọ bụla ma ọ bụ mgbanwe nke iwu nhọrọ, ndọrọndọrọ ahụ na akpụkọkwa akpụkọ.
rows.output: The truth is that we are not the church that spreads the doctrine of "unreliability" or any other changes to the selection laws, the party's internal rules, or the party's publications.
rows.reference: The reality is we are no longer that broad church and with every "no-confidence" motion or change of selection rules the party becomes narrower.

rows.source: Enwere m ọtụtụ ndụmọdụ n’ofe afọ abụọ gara aga na agwa m ka m owe isi n’ala, ịhapụ ikwu oke okwu mgbe ahụ ‘m agaghị enwe nsogbu.”
rows.output: I have had many suggestions over the past two years to get up and leave the field, to stop talking so much and then I wouldn't have any problems.
rows.reference: I have had lots of advice over the past two years urging me to keep my head down, not to be so vocal and then I would "be all right."

rows.source: Mana nke ahụ abụghị ihe m banyere ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị ịme.
rows.output: But that's not what I'm about in politics.
rows.reference: But that is not what I came into politics to do.

rows.source: Kemgbe m sonyere Labour afọ 32 ka nwa akwụkwọ, nke nlegharị anya gọọmentị Thatcher kpalitere, nke hapụrụ ime ụlọ akwụkwọ m na nnukwu mmebi, achọrọ m na mbụ idu ọrụ mara mma nke ọhaneze maka ndị kachasị chọọ ha - ma abụ m onye ndu obere mpaghara ma ọ bụ minista gọọmentị.
rows.output: Since I joined Labour 32 years ago as a student, inspired by the government's Thatcherite gaze, which left my school in disrepair, I have always wanted to lead a public service that is a model for those who need it most - whether as a local leader or government minister.
rows.reference: Ever since I joined Labour 32 years ago as a school pupil, provoked by the Thatcher government's neglect that had left my comprehensive school classroom literally falling down, I've sought to champion better public services for those who need them most - whether as a local councillor or government minister.

rows.source: Ezobeghị m ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị m na mbụ, gụnyere ntuli aka ikpeazụ.
rows.output: I have never been involved in politics before, including the last election.
rows.reference: I have never hidden my politics, including at the last election.

rows.source: Ọnweghị onye ọ bụla nọ na Nottingham East ga-enwe mgbagwoju anya gbasara ọnọdụ iwu m yana mpaghara ndị mụ ekwenyeghị n’ọchịchị dị ugbu a.
rows.output: No one in Nottingham East should be confused about my legal position and the areas where I have not agreed with the current government's policies.
rows.reference: No one in Nottingham East could have been in any way confused about my policy positions and areas of disagreement with the current leadership.

rows.source: Maka ndị ahụ kwadoro ụkpụrụ ahụ na Fraịde, ihe niile m nwere ike ikwu bụ na mgbe obodo na aga ịnwe Brexit ga-enwe mmetụta adịghị mma n’ọtụtụ ezinụlọ, azụmahịa na ọrụ ọhaneze anyị, aghọtaghị m agụụ iji gbuo oge na ike maka nkwado m na ndị isi ndọrọndọrọ Labour.
rows.output: For those who supported the motion on Friday, all I can say is that when the country goes through Brexit, it will have a negative impact on many families, businesses, and public services, and I don't understand the hunger to waste time and energy in supporting me and the Labour leadership.
rows.reference: To those who promoted the motion on Friday, all I would say is that when the country is ploughing towards a Brexit that will hurt households, businesses and our public services, I do not understand the desire to waste time and energy on my loyalty to the Labour party leader.

rows.source: Mana n’eziokwu otu ozi m nwere abụghị maka Nottingham Momentum, ọ bụ maka ndị mmebe m, ma ọ bụ ndị otu Labour ma ha abụghị: Enwere m afọ ojuju ijere unu ozi ma na ekwe nkwa na ọnweghị ihe egwu mwepu ole ma ọ bụ ngwangwa ndọrọndọrọ ga-akwụsị m ịme ihe m kwere kachasị dịịrị unu niile mma.
rows.output: But in truth, one message I have is not about Nottingham Momentum, it's about my makers, or the Labour Party, and they are not: I am satisfied to serve you and I promise that no threat of expulsion or disciplinary action will stop me from doing what I owe to all of you.
rows.reference: But really the one message I have is not to Nottingham Momentum, it is to my constituents, whether Labour members or not: I am proud to serve you and I promise that no amount of deselection threats or political expediency will deter me from acting in what I believe are the best interests of you all.

rows.source: North Korea kwuru “ọ gaghị eme” ịgbarapụ ngwa ọgụ na anataghị nkwenye
rows.output: North Korea said "it won't happen" to disarm and not to receive verification
rows.reference: North Korea says 'no way' will disarm unilaterally without trust

rows.source: Onye Mịnịsta nke mba ofesi North Korea gwara United Nations na Satọde na ịga n’ihu amachibido ha na-ebute atụkwasịghị obi na United State nke na ọ nweghịkwa ka obodo ha ga-esi gbarapụ ngwa ọgụ nuklịa ha n’ụdị ọnọdụ ahụ.
rows.output: The North Korean Minister of Foreign Affairs told the United Nations on Saturday that continuing to impose sanctions on them would only increase their distrust of the United States and that there was no way for their country to get rid of their nuclear weapons under such conditions.
rows.reference: North Korea's foreign minister told the United Nations on Saturday continued sanctions were deepening its mistrust in the United States and there was no way the country would give up its nuclear weapons unilaterally under such circumstances.

rows.source: Ri Yong Ho gwara otu mba ụwa na Mgbakọ Ezumezu ha kwa afọ na North Korea esorola “ezigbo ụzọ pụtara ihie” n’afọ gara aga, dị ka nkwụsị nlele ngwa nuklịa na ogbunigwe, ntọsa ebe nlele ngwa nuklịa ma kwee nkwa na ọ gaghị arụkasị ngwa ọgụ nuklịa na teknụzụ nuklịa.
rows.output: Ri Yong Ho told the international community at the General Assembly that North Korea has taken a "very important step" in the past year, such as the suspension of nuclear tests and weapons, the dismantling of nuclear test sites, and the commitment not to conduct any further nuclear weapons tests or develop nuclear technology.
rows.reference: Ri Yong Ho told the world body's annual General Assembly that North Korea had taken "significant goodwill measures" in the past year, such as stopping nuclear and missiles tests, dismantling the nuclear test site, and pledging not to proliferate nuclear weapons and nuclear technology.

rows.source: “Kosiladị, anyị ahụghị asịsa na-esote ya sitere na U,S” o kwuru.
rows.output: "However, we did not see any follow-up on that from the U.S," he said.
rows.reference: "However, we do not see any corresponding response from the U.S.," he said.

rows.source: “N’enweghị ntụkwasị obi na U.S, agaghị enwekwa okwukwe na nchekwa nke obodo anyị, na n’ụdị ọnọdụ a, ọ nweghị ka anyị ga-esi buru ụzọ gbarapụ ngwa ọgụ anyị.”
rows.output: Without the support of the U.S., we will also have no faith in the safety of our country, and in this situation, we will not be able to withdraw our weapons first.
rows.reference: "Without any trust in the U.S. there will be no confidence in our national security and under such circumstances there is no way we will unilaterally disarm ourselves first."

rows.source: Ebe Ri gbanwere mkpesa ndị North Korea banyere ọjụjụ nke Washington ime usoro “agba” mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa n’okpuru nke North Korea ga-erite elele dịka ọ na-esonye usoro obere obere, okwu ya bara uru n’ihi na ọ jụghị mgbarapụ ngwa nuklliya ozugbo dịka Pyongyang siri mee n’oge gara aga.
rows.output: The change in Ri's position was based on North Korea's complaints about Washington's failure to implement a "step-by-step" dismantling of its nuclear arsenal, which Pyongyang would be closely monitored as it participates in the process.
rows.reference: While Ri reprised familiar North Korean complaints about Washington's resistance to a "phased" approach to denuclearization under which North Korea would be rewarded as it took gradual steps, his statement appeared significant in that it did not reject unilateral denuclearization out of hand as Pyongyang has done in the past.

rows.source: Ri rụtụrụ aka na nkwuputa Kim Jong Un na Donald Trump kwukọrịtara na ọgbakọ nke izizi n’etiti onye isi ala U.S nọ n’ọchịchị na onye ọchịchị North Korea na Singapore na Juun 12, mgbe Kim kwere nkwa ịhụ banyere “mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa nke okirikiri Korea” ebe Trump kwere nkwa nchekwa nke North Korea.
rows.output: Referring to the statement by Kim Jong Un that Donald Trump agreed to a meeting between the U.S. president and the North Korean leader in Singapore on June 12, when Kim promised to see about "the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula" and Trump promised the security of North Korea.
rows.reference: Ri referred to a joint statement issued by Kim Jong Un and Donald Trump at a first ever summit between a serving U.S. president and a North Korean leader in Singapore on June 12, when Kim pledged to work toward "denuclearization of the Korean peninsula" while Trump promised guarantees of North Korea's security.

rows.source: North Korea na-achọ njedebe agha 1950-53 nke Korea, mana United States ekwuola na Pyongyang ga-ebu ụzọ gbarapụ ngwa ọgụ nuklliya ya.
rows.output: North Korea is seeking an end to the 1950-53 Korean War, but the United States has said that Pyongyang must first dismantle its nuclear weapons.
rows.reference: North Korea has been seeking a formal end to the 1950-53 Korea War, but the United States has said Pyongyang must give up its nuclear weapons first.

rows.source: Washington ajụkwala oku ibelata mmachibido mba ụwa a siri ike nke North Korea.
rows.output: Washington has refused to call for easing of the international sanctions that are severely restricting North Korea.
rows.reference: Washington has also resisted calls to relax tough international sanctions on North Korea.

rows.source: “U.S kwụgidere na “mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa-izizi” ma bulikwuo nkwanye ya site na mmachibido iji mezuo ebumnuche ha n’ụzọ nkwanye, ma jụkwuo “nkwuputa nke njedebe agha” Ri kwuru.
rows.output: The U.S. maintained its "nuclear umbrella" and reinforced its support by imposing a ban to achieve their goals in a manner of respect, and rejected the "proclamation of the end of the war" Ri said.
rows.reference: "The U.S. insists on the "denuclearization-first" and increases the level of pressure by sanctions to achieve their purpose in a coercive manner, and even objecting to the "declaration of the end of war,"" Ri said.

rows.source: “Nghọta na mmachibido ga-akputu anyị n’ikpere anyị bụ nrọ efu nke ndị na amaghị anyị.
rows.output: Understanding and prohibition will only make us more determined in our knees is a dream of those who do not know us.
rows.reference: "The perception that sanctions can bring us on our knees is a pipe dream of the people who are ignorant about us.

rows.source: Mana nsogbu bụ na ịganihu eme machibido na-emina enweghị ntụkwasị obi anyị.”
rows.output: But the problem is that progress is hindered by our lack of trust.
rows.reference: But the problem is that the continued sanctions are deepening our mistrust."

rows.source: Ri ekwughị maka atụmatụ ọgbakọ nke abụọ n’etiti Kim na Trump nke onye ọchịchị U.S kwuturu na United Nation n’izu ahụ.
rows.output: He did not mention the second summit between Kim and Trump, which the U.S. president canceled at the United Nations last week.
rows.reference: Ri made no mention of plans for a second summit between Kim and Trump that the U.S. leader highlighted at the United Nations earlier in the week.

rows.source: Kama mịnịsta ahụ kwuturu maka nzụkọ atọ n’etiti Kim na onye ọchịchị South Korea Moon Jae-in n’ime ọnwa ise gara aga were tinyekwa: “Ọ bụrụ na ndị ọ metutara n’okwu nke mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa bụ South Korea na ọ bụghị U.S, mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa nke okirikiri Korea agaghị abịa n’ụdị nkụchikọ a.”
rows.output: The minister said that there were three meetings between Kim and South Korean President Moon Jae-in in the past five months, and added: "If the parties involved in the issue of nuclear dismantlement are South Korea and not the U.S., the dismantlement of the Korean Peninsula's nuclear weapons will not come in this form."
rows.reference: The minister instead highlighted three meetings between Kim and South Korean leader Moon Jae-in in the past five months and added: "If the party to this issue of denuclearization were South Korea and not the U.S., the denuclearization of the Korean peninsula would not have come to such a deadlock."

rows.source: Ọbụlagodi otu a, olu okwu Ri tụgharịrị nke ukwuu site na afọ gara aga, mgbe ọ gwara Mgbakọ Ezumezu U.N. kwuru na iji rọketị ndị North Korea wee nweta isi ala U.S. apụghị ime, ka “Ajọ Onye Isi Ala” Trump kpọrọ Kim “nwoke rọketị” nọ n’ọrụ igbu ọchụ.
rows.output: Even so, the tone of the U.N. Security Council's statement from last year, when it said that using North Korean rockets to reach the U.S. president was "unacceptable," was echoed by the "Wicked President" Trump, who called Kim "a rocket man" in the service of murder.
rows.reference: Even so, the tone of Ri's speech was dramatically different from last year, when he told the U.N. General Assembly that targeting the U.S. mainland with North Korea's rockets was inevitable after "Mr Evil President" Trump called Kim a "rocket man" on a suicide mission.

rows.source: N’afọ a na United Nations, Trump onye nke majara n’afọ gara aga “imebi kpam kpam” North Korea, kpokwasara Kim otito maka obi ọ nwere n’isoro usoro mgbarapụ ngwa agha, mana o kwuru na a ka nwere ọtụtụ ọrụ nke na mmachibido ka ga-adịgide ruo mgbe North Korea kwụsịrị ngwa nuklịa.
rows.output: This year at the United Nations, Trump, who was the most recent president to "completely destroy" North Korea, met with Kim in person to express his genuine interest in the process of denuclearization, but said that there are still many tasks that need to be done in order for the sanctions to be lifted, and that will not happen until North Korea completely gives up its nuclear weapons.
rows.reference: This year at the United Nations, Trump, who last year threatened to "totally destroy" North Korea, heaped praise on Kim for his courage in taking steps to disarm, but said much work still had to be done and sanctions must remain in place until North Korea denuclearizes.

rows.source: Na Wenesde, Trump kwuru na ọ nweghị oge ewepụtara maka nke a, na-ekwu “ọ bụrụ na ọ ga-ewe afọ abụọ, afọ atọ ma ọ bụ ọnwa ise- ọ nweghị ihe ọ pụtara.”
rows.output: On Wednesday, Trump said there was no time for this, saying, "If it takes two years, three years or five months, it doesn't matter."
rows.reference: On Wednesday, Trump said he did not have a time frame for this, saying "If it takes two years, three years or five months - doesn't matter."

rows.source: China na Russia na-arụrịta ụka na Ọgbakọ Nchekwa U.N. kwesịrị inye Pyongyang elele maka usoro ndị ha megoro.
rows.output: China and Russia argue that the U.N. Security Council should monitor Pyongyang for its compliance with the measures it has taken.
rows.reference: China and Russia argue that the U.N. Security Council should reward Pyongyang for steps taken.

rows.source: Kosiladị, U.S Mike Pompeo gwara Ọgbakọ Nchekwa U,N Na Tọsde na “Mmanye nke mmachibido Ọgbakọ Nchekwa ga-aga n’ihu ike n’ike na-adaghị mba ruo mgbe anyị mezuru mgbarapụ ngwa nuklịa kpam kpam, na njedebe.”
rows.output: However, U.S. Mike Pompeo told the United Nations Security Council on Thursday that "the enforcement of the arms embargo will continue to be strong and unrelenting until we achieve complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization, and the end of the Korean Peninsula."
rows.reference: However, U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo told the U.N. Security Council on Thursday that: "Enforcement of Security Council sanctions must continue vigorously and without fail until we realize the fully, final, verified denuclearization."

rows.source: Ọgbakọ Nchekwa ahụ jikọrọ aka ọnụ kwalite mmachibido North Korea kemgbe 2006, n’ụzọ ịgbachi ego maka mmemme ngwa nuklịa na ogbunigwe Pyongyang.
rows.output: The Security Council has strengthened the sanctions on North Korea since 2006, in a bid to choke off funding for Pyongyang's nuclear and missile programs.
rows.reference: The Security Council has unanimously boosted sanctions on North Korea since 2006 in a bid to choke off funding for Pyongyang's nuclear and ballistic missile programs.

rows.source: Pompeo zutere Ri n’akụkụ nke Mgbakọ Ezumezu U.N. wee gwa ya ka emechara na ọ ga-abịa Pyongyang ọzọ n’ọnwa na-abịa iji kwado maka ọgbakọ nke abụọ.
rows.output: Pompeo met Ri at the UN General Assembly and told him after the fact that he would be going to Pyongyang again next month to prepare for the second summit.
rows.reference: Pompeo met Ri on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly and said afterwards that he would visit Pyongyang again next month to prepare for a second summit.

rows.source: Pompeo ejeela North Korea ugboro atọ n’afọ a, mana njem ikpeazụ ya agaghị nke ọma.
rows.output: Pompeo has visited North Korea three times this year, but his last trip was unsuccessful.
rows.reference: Pompeo has visited North Korea three times already this year, but his last trip did not go well.

rows.source: Ọ hapụrụ Pyongyang na Julaị na-ekwu na enwela agamnihu, naanị ka North Korea jụ ya n’ime awa ole ma ole maka iti “iwu yiri nke ndị agboro.”
rows.output: He left Pyongyang in July saying that he had made progress, only to be denied entry by North Korea a few hours later for "acting like a spy."
rows.reference: He left Pyongyang in July saying that progress had been made, only for North Korea within hours to denounce him for making "gangster-like demands."

rows.source: North Korea kwere nkwa na nzụkọ yana Moon mere n’ime ọnwa a ịtọsa ebe ogbunigwe nakwa ụlọ ọrụ nuklịa ma ọ bụrụ na United States esoro “usoro dabara.”
rows.output: North Korea promised a meeting with Moon in the month to discuss the dismantling of its nuclear weapons and facilities if the United States followed a "corresponding" path.
rows.reference: North Korea pledged in a meeting with Moon this month to dismantle a missile site and also a nuclear complex if the United States took "corresponding measures."

rows.source: O kwuru na Kim gwara ya, “usoro dabara” nke ọ na-achọ bụ nkwa nchekwa Trump kwere ya na nkwa na Singapore yana ịga n’ihu mee ka mmekọrịta dị n’etiti Washington dị mma.
rows.output: He said that Kim told him, "the system of trust" that he was looking for was the commitment of security that Trump promised him in the commitment in Singapore and to continue to make the relationship between Washington good.
rows.reference: He said Kim had told him the "corresponding measures" he was seeking were security guarantees Trump pledged in Singapore and moves toward normalization of relations with Washington.

rows.source: Ụmụ akwụkwọ Harvard na-eme mmụta ka-esi enwe ezumike zuru ezu
rows.output: Harvard students learn to take a complete break
rows.reference: Harvard students take course in getting enough rest

rows.source: Mmụta ọ hụrụ dị na Mahadum Harvard n’afọ a mere ụmụ akwụkwọ niile na-agụ akwụkwọ ịrahụzu ụra, ime ka echere omenala iji kafin agụ akwụkwọ ‘abalị niile’ aka mgba.’
rows.output: The learning she saw at Harvard this year made all students who were studying for exams take a break, making a cultural practice of taking a nap before studying 'all night' a challenge.
rows.reference: A new course at Harvard University this year has got all its undergraduates getting more sleep in a bid to combat the growing macho culture of studying through caffeine-fuelled 'all-nighters.'

rows.source: Onye mmụta chọpụtara na ụmụ akwụkwọ enwere na Mahadum mbu n’ụwa niile anaghị amakarị ihe kwesịrị ma abịa n’ilekọta onwe ha anya.
rows.output: A scholar discovered that students at the first university in the world were not aware of what they should do and how to take care of themselves.
rows.reference: An academic found students at the world's number one university are often clueless when it comes to the very basics about how to look after themselves.

rows.source: Charles Czeisler, ọkammụta ahụike nke ụra na Havard Medical School yana onye ọkachamara na Brigham yana Women Hospital haziri mmụta ahụ, nke ọ kwenyere na ọ bụ ụdịdị ya mbu na US.
rows.output: Charles Czeisler, a professor of sleep medicine at Harvard Medical School and a specialist at Brigham and Women's Hospital, organized the study, which he believed was the first of its kind in the US.
rows.reference: Charles Czeisler, professor of sleep medicine at Harvard Medical School and a specialist at the Brigham and Women's Hospital, designed the course, which he believes is the first of its kind in the US.

rows.source: Ọ nwetara echiche ịmalite mmụta ahụ ka ọ nyechara nkuzi banyere nsonazụ arahụghị ụra na-eme mmụta.
rows.output: He received the idea of starting the study after giving a lecture on the consequences of not getting enough sleep for learning.
rows.reference: He was inspired to start the course after giving a talk on the impact sleep deprivation had on learning.

rows.source: ‘Ka emechara nke ahụ otu nwa agbọghọ biakwutere m nwee sị: ‘Kedu ihe kpatara o jiri bụrụ ugbu a ka a na-agwa m ihe a, n’afọ senịọ m?’
rows.output: After that, a young woman came up to me and said, 'Why are you telling me this now, at the age of eighty?'
rows.reference: 'At the end of it one girl came up to me and said: 'Why am I only being told this now, in my senior year?'

rows.source: O kwuru na ọ nwebeghị onye gwara ya uru ụra bara- bụ ihe tụrụ m n’anya.’ ọ gwara The Telegraph.
rows.output: He said he had never been told the value of sleep - it was a surprise to me. he told The Telegraph.
rows.reference: She said no one had ever told her about the importance of sleep - which surprised me,' he told The Telegraph.

rows.source: Nkuzi ahụ, nke ebupụtara n’izizi ya n’afọ a, kọwaara ụmụ akwụkwọ ka uru akparamagwa ezigbo ụra si enyere agumakwụkwọ yana ime mmemme egwuregwu aka, ma dozikwaa ahụ ha niile.
rows.output: The study, which was first published this year, informed students about the benefits of good sleep for their academic performance and the physical health of their bodies.
rows.reference: The course, rolled out for the first time this year, explains to students the essentials of how good sleep habits help academic and athletic performance, as well as improve their general wellbeing.

rows.source: Paul Barreira, ọkammụta ọrịa ọgụgụ isi na mmụọ na Harvard Medical School yana onye isi oche ọrụ ahụike nke mahadum, kwuru na mahadum ahụ kpebiri ịmalite mmụta ahụ ka achọpụtara na ụmụ akwụkwọ anaghị arahụzu ụra n’ime izu.
rows.output: Paul Barreira, a professor of neurology and psychiatry at Harvard Medical School and the chair of the university's health services, said the university decided to launch the study after it was found that students were not getting enough sleep over the weekend.
rows.reference: Paul Barreira, professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School and executive director of the university's health services, said the university decided to introduce the course after finding students were seriously sleep deprived during the week.

rows.source: Mmụta ahụ ruru otu awa tinyere usoro ọrụ mkparịta ụka.
rows.output: The training lasted one hour and included a discussion session.
rows.reference: The hour long course involves a series of interactive tasks.

rows.source: N’otu ngalaba enwere onyonyo ime ụlọ ụra, ebe ụmụ akwụkwọ na-apịdo n’iko kọfị, akwa mgbochi, akpụkpụ ụkwụ egwuregwu yana akwụkwọ iji gwa ha banyere nsonazụ kafin na ihie yana ka arahụghị ụra siri emetụta mmemme egwuregwu, n’uru mmemme oge ụra dị.
rows.output: In one section, there is a video room, where students are lying on mattresses, drinking coffee, wearing sports shoes, and reading books to tell them about the consequences of caffeine and sleep deprivation on athletic performance, during the time of sleep.
rows.reference: In one section there is an image of a dorm room, where students click on coffee cups, curtains, trainers and books to be told about the effects of caffeine and light and how athletic performance is impacted by sleep deficiency, and the importance of a bedtime routine.

rows.source: Na ngalaba ọzọ, agwara ndị sonyere ka arahụghị ụra ogologo oge siri akpalite ihe egwu obi nkolopu, mkpọnwu ahụ, mmụọ ịda mba yana oria mkpụrụ akụ.
rows.output: In another section, participants were told not to sleep for a long time and were asked to identify the risks of heart palpitations, muscle cramps, loss of consciousness, and seed germination.
rows.reference: In another section, participants are told how long-term sleep deprivation can increase risks of heart attacks, stroke, depression and cancer.

rows.source: Maapu ụlọ akwụkwọ nwere akara ngosi mkparịta ụka, wee na-akwado ndị sonyere ka ha chee banyere ihe ha na-eme kwa ụbọchị.
rows.output: The school map has a dialogue mark, and it encourages participants to think about what they do every day.
rows.reference: A map of the campus, with interactive icons, then encourages participants to think about their daily routine.

rows.source: ‘Anyị maara na ọ gaghị agbanwe agwa ụmụ akwụkwọ ozugbo.
rows.output: We know that it will not change the character of the students immediately.
rows.reference: 'We know it won't change students' behaviour instantly.

rows.source: Mana anyị kwenyere na ha nwere ikike ịmata- dịka inwere ikike ịmata nsonazụ nhọrọ ise siga n’ahụike,’ Ọkammụta Czeisler gbakwunyere.
rows.output: But we believe that they have the right to know - just as they have the right to know the consequences of their choice to smoke.
rows.reference: But we believe they have a right to know - just as you have a right to know the health effects of choosing to smoke cigarettes,' Prof Czeisler added.

rows.source: Omenala ngala ‘ịmụ anya abalị niile’ ka dịkwa, o kwuru, tinyere teknụzụ agbara ọhụrụ yana mbawanye nkwanye na-adakwasa ụmụ akwụkwọ, pụtara na arahụghị ụra bụ nsogbu n’ebuwaye.
rows.output: The old saying of "keeping an eye open all night" still holds, he said, along with new technology and increased recognition of the challenges faced by students, meaning that insomnia is a problem to be carried.
rows.reference: The culture of pride in 'pulling an all-nighter' still exists, he said, adding that modern technology and ever-increasing pressure on students meant sleep deprivation was a growing problem.

rows.source: Ịgba mbọ hụ na inwetara ụra zuru ezu, dị mma, kwesịrị ịbụ ngwa agha nwata akwụkwọ’ iji chere mgbakasị ahụ, ike ọgwụgwụ na obi mmapụ aka mgba, o kwuru - ọbụlagodi izenari ntinye ahụ, ka arahụghị ụra na-etinye ụbụrụ n’ọnọdụ oke agụụ, na-eme ha agụụ kwa mgbe.
rows.output: Ensure you get enough, good quality sleep, as it is a weapon for students to fight off fatigue, stress and anxiety, he said - even during the exam period, lack of sleep puts the brain in a state of extreme hunger, making it crave for it every time.
rows.reference: Ensuring you have enough sleep, of a good quality, should be a student's 'secret weapon' to combat stress, exhaustion and anxiety, he said - even to avoid putting on weight, as sleep deprivation puts the brain into starvation mode, making them constantly hungry.

rows.source: Raymond So, nwata gbara afọ 19 nke California na-agụ kemikal na fisikal baịyọlọji nyere Ọkammụta Czeisler aka ịhazi mmụta ahụ, ebe o megoro otu klaasị ya n’afọ gara aga n’ime oge afọ izizi ya na Harvard.
rows.output: Raymond So, a 19-year-old student from California who is studying chemistry and physical biology, helped Professor Czeisler organize the course, as he had taken one of his classes the previous year during his first year at Harvard.
rows.reference: Raymond So, a 19-year-old Californian studying chemical and physical biology, helped Professor Czeisler design the course, having taken one of his classes last year during his first year at Harvard.

rows.source: O kwuru na mmụta ahụ mepere anya ya wee kpalite echiche ya ịkwanye ka mmụta a bụrụ maka ụlọ akwụkwọ niile.
rows.output: He said that the learning opened his eyes and inspired his thinking to push for this learning to be for all schools.
rows.reference: He said the course had opened his eyes and inspired him to push for a campus-wide course.

rows.source: Nke na-esote ya, ọ na-enwe olile anya ịrịọ ụmụ akwụkwọ ndị gụchagoro mmụta izizi ka ha mejuputa mmụta yitebere nke a tupu ha abanye n’ụlọ akwụkwọ ahụ.
rows.output: Next, you are expected to request students who have completed their first degree to implement this learning before they enter the school.
rows.reference: The next step, he hopes, it to ask all postgraduate students to complete a similar study programme before joining the competitive institution.

rows.source: Ọkammụta Czeisler kwadoro ka ụmụ akwụkwọ chee banyere itinye otimkpu maka mgbe ha chọrọ ịrahụ ụra, yana mgbe ha chọrọ ikuli, ma marakwa maka nsonazụ mmerụ ahụ ihuenyo ngwa eletrọnịk “ihie agba elu igwe” na-ebute yana ihie LED, nke nwere ike kụpụ usoro ka ahụ gị si akpa agwa, we bute nsogbu ịrahụ ụra.
rows.output: Professor Czeisler recommended that students consider setting an alarm for when they need to sleep, and when they need to wake up, and be aware of the consequences of physical injury from screen glare caused by electronic devices, such as computers and LEDs, which can disrupt your body's natural rhythm and lead to sleep disorders.
rows.reference: Prof Czeisler recommended that students should consider setting an alarm for when to go to bed, as well as for when to wake, and be aware of the harmful effects of 'blue light' emitted by electronic screens and LED lighting, which can throw your circadian rhythm out of kilter, leading to problems falling asleep.

rows.output: Rangers suffered a blow as Dolly Menga's goal was ruled out for Steven Gerrard's challenge in a 1-0 defeat to Livingston.

rows.source: Akụkụ Ibrox ahụ na-achọ inweta mmeri nke izizi ha n’ụzọ kemgbe ha meriri 4-1 na Febuarị na St Johnstone, mana ndị otu Gary Holt nyere Gerrard mmeri nke abụọ emeriri ha n’egwuregwu 18 dịka onye njikwa jiri akara asatọ esegharị n’elu nke ndị mbu na Ladbrokes Premiership, Hearts.
rows.output: The Ibrox side were looking to secure their first win since their 4-1 victory over St Johnstone in February, but the team managed by Gary Holt denied Gerrard his second win in 18 games as manager, with the scoreline finishing 8-2 in favor of the first team in the Ladbrokes Premiership, Hearts.
rows.reference: The Ibrox side were looking to record their first win on the road since February's 4-1 triumph at St Johnstone, but Gary Holt's team inflicted just Gerrard's second defeat in 18 games as manager to leave his side eight points adrift of runaway Ladbrokes Premiership leaders Hearts.

rows.source: Menga jiri tupu nkeji asaa nke ọkara oge were gbanye ọkpụ, na ndị Rangers n’enweghị mkpalite mmụọ adịghị ka ndị ga-agbanyekwa nke ha.
rows.output: The Rangers were seven minutes into the second half when they scored, and the Rangers were not as inspired as they were when they scored their own.

rows.output: The Rangers dropped to sixth place, while Livingston climbed to third and were only two points behind Hibernian.

rows.source: Nyocha Johnny English Strikes Again - buturu ihe nkiri nzuzo ịkpa ọchị Rowan Atkinson
rows.output: Johnny English Strikes Again - a comedy spy film starring Rowan Atkinson
rows.reference: Johnny English Strikes Again review - underpowered Rowan Atkinson spy spoof

rows.source: Ọ bụ omenala ugbu a ịchọ mkpa Brexit n’ihe nkiri ọhụrụ ọ bụla nwere nribama Britain, na nke a dịka ọ metụtara mmegharị ihe nkiri ịkpa ọchị nke Johnny English - bụ nke ejiri Johnny English malite na 2003, wee laghachikwa azụ na 2011 ka Johnny English Reborn.
rows.output: It is now a tradition to seek a Brexit angle in every new film with a British cast, and this one is no exception as it relates to the Johnny English comedy franchise - which was first introduced with Johnny English in 2003, and then returned in 2011 as Johnny English Reborn.
rows.reference: It's traditional now to look for Brexit significances in any new film with a British slant and that does seem applicable to this revival of the Johnny English action-comedy spoof franchise - which started back in 2003 with Johnny English and spluttered back to life in 2011 with Johnny English Reborn.

rows.source: Ọ pụtara na ihe nkiri njakịrị nke isiokwu otu anyị siri bụrụ ndị iberibe pụtara ihie, bụzi oghere nbufe ahịa ọhụrụ anyị?
rows.output: It appears that the comedic film with the theme of our division into fragments has become a new channel for our commercial interests.
rows.reference: Will tongue-in-cheek self-satire on the subject of how obviously rubbish we are be the nation's new export opportunity?

rows.source: Kosiladị, onye nzuzu anya ọkpụ, ihu rọba Johnny English emegharịala ikike ya ịkwalite ihe nke ugboro abụọ - aha ya karịa ihe ọ bụla na-egosi na ọ bụ nchepụta ihe ịkpa ọchị emebere maka akụkụ obodo ndị anaghị asụ Bekee.
rows.output: However, the blind fool, the plastic face of Johnny English, has once again reinvented his ability to promote something - his name more than anything else - as a parody of a comedy created for the non-English speaking parts of the country.
rows.reference: At any rate, the pop-eyed, rubber-faced incompetent Johnny English has had his licence to cock things up renewed for the second time - that name of his signalling more than anything else that he is a broad comic creation designed for non-English-speaking cinemagoing territories.

rows.source: N’ezie ọ bụ onye iberibe ọrụ nzuzo nke agbanyeghị ṅṅomi ya gbagwojuru anya, nwere obere Clouseau, ntakịrị Mr Bean na nfechalụ nke nwoke ahụ n’etinye otu olu na isiokwu Chariots of Fire na mmalite mmemme Olympics London 2012.
rows.output: Indeed, he is a piece of secret work, regardless of his clumsy appearance, with a little Clouseau, a little Mr Bean and the man's obsession with placing one voice on the theme of Chariots of Fire and the opening ceremony of the London 2012 Olympics.
rows.reference: He is of course the daft secret agent who despite his bizarre pretensions to smoothie glamour has got a little bit of Clouseau, a dash of Mr Bean and a dollop of that chap contributing a single note to the Chariots of Fire theme tune at the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony.

rows.source: N’izizi ọ dabere n’onye njem yana nwoke nzuzo mba ụwa Atkinson nke emere na ihe mgbasa ozi Barclaycard TV echefugoro, na-ahapu ọgbaghara n’azụ ya.
rows.output: At first, you relied on a travel agent and a mysterious international man named Atkinson who appeared in a Barclaycard TV advertisement, leaving a trail of chaos in his wake.
rows.reference: He's also originally based on the traveller and international man of mystery Atkinson once played in the now forgotten Barclaycard TV ads, leaving chaos in his wake.

rows.source: Enwere otu oge ma ọ bụ abụọ mara mma na JE ọhụrụ a.
rows.output: There is one or two beautiful things in this new JE.

rows.source: Ọ masịrị m ka Johnny English na-erute nso n’ụgbọ elu ebe oyi uwe agha ndị agba ochie, igwe nkucha were na-akụta n’okpu agha ya.
rows.output: I liked how Johnny English got close to the plane where the old war uniforms, the washing machine, and the helmet were.
rows.reference: I loved Johnny English approaching a helicopter while dressed in a medieval suit of armour and the rotor blades briefly clanging against his helmet.

rows.source: Onyinye Atkinson nwere maka ịkpa ọchị a na-ahụ anya pụtara ihie, mana ịkpa ọchị ahụ esighi ike ma mafee oke, tụmadị ihe nkiri ndị ahụ “anaghị akpa ọchị” dịka 007 na Mission Impossible n’onwe ha na-enwekwa ihe ịkpa ọchị n’ime ya ugbu a.
rows.output: Atkinson's gift for slapstick comedy is evident, but the comedy is weak and overdone, resembling the "non-comedic" films like 007 and Mission Impossible, which are now also trying to incorporate comedy into them.
rows.reference: Atkinson's gift for physical comedy is on display, but the humour feels pretty underpowered and weirdly superfluous, especially as the "serious" film brands like 007 and Mission Impossible themselves now confidently offer comedy as an ingredient.

rows.source: Ihe ịkpa ọchị ahụ dịka ọ bụ ụmụaka ka emebere ya karịa ndị okenye, maka mụ onwe m njegheri Johnny English enweghị ihe nchepụta pụrụ iche yana ebumnuche ya dịka ihe nkiri anaghị ekwu okwu nke Atkinson, n’onye nke Bean.
rows.output: The humor of the film was more for children than for adults, for me personally, Johnny English's journey lacked originality and its purpose as a non-verbal comedy by Atkinson, in whom Bean excelled.
rows.reference: The humour feels as if it is pitched at kids rather than adults, and for me Johnny English's wacky misadventures aren't as inventive and focused as Atkinson's silent-movie gags in the persona of Bean.

rows.source: Ebe mgbado ukwu isiokwu ugbu a bụ na Great Britain nọ n’oke nsogbu.
rows.output: The main topic of discussion at the moment is that Great Britain is in a great crisis.
rows.reference: The perennially topical premise now is that Great Britain is in serious trouble.

rows.source: Onye nbanye ịntanetị anataghị ikike banyere na netwọk ndị ọrụ nzuzo kachasị dị nzuzo nke Britain, kpughee ndị ọrụ nzuzo niile nọ n’ọrụ, na mgbagwoju anya onye ọrụ nzuzo nọ ọrụ - obere ihe omume maka Kelvin Eldon.
rows.output: A computer user who was not authorized to access the most secret network of British intelligence operatives accidentally revealed all the operatives in service and the identity of the agent working undercover - a small feat for Kelvin Eldon.
rows.reference: A cyber-hacker has infiltrated Britain's super-secret web network of spies, revealing the identities of all Britain's agents in the field, to the dismay of the agent on duty - a regrettably small role for Kevin Eldon.

rows.source: Ọ bụ nke ikpeazụ maka onye isi ala bụ onye mpako nwere nsogbu, nke enweghịzi nkwado ọchịchị ọ bụla kpamkpam: Emma Thompson nwara ike ya na ime ihe omume a yitebere Teresa-May mana enwekebeghị ihe dị n’akwụkwọ ọ ga-eji rụọ ọrụ.
rows.output: It was the last for the president who was a proud man with problems, no longer supported by any political party: Emma Thompson tried her best in this role, which was prepared for Theresa May, but there was nothing in the script for her to work with.
rows.reference: It's the last straw for a prime minister who is a pompous and embattled figure, already suffering a complete meltdown of political unpopularity: Emma Thompson does her very best with this quasi-Teresa-May character but there's nothing much in the script to work with.

rows.source: Ndị na-enye ya ndụmọdụ nchekwa gwara ya na ebe amagoro ndị ọrụ nzuzo ya niile, ọ ga-akpọpụta onye lagoro ezumike nka.
rows.output: The security advisers told her that since all of her secret agents had been discovered, she should summon a retired agent.

rows.reference: And that means bumbling Johnny English himself, now employed as a schoolmaster in some posh establishment, but giving off-the-record lessons in how to be an undercover operative: some nice gags here, as English offers a School of Rock-type academy of spying.

rows.output: The English and Bough embarked on a journey of their own comedic antics: they transformed into a waiter, they set fire in a French restaurant; they caused a stir by sneaking into a Volta River cruise; the English caused confusion by trying to use a Virtual Reality headset with the Volta's interior.
rows.reference: English and Bough begin their odyssey of farcical high-jinks: disguised as waiters, they set fire to a flash French restaurant; they create mayhem smuggling themselves aboard Volta's luxury yacht; and English triggers pure anarchy as he attempts to use a Virtual Reality headset to familiarise himself with the interior of Volta's house.

rows.source: Labour na-agọnarị na ha anaghị akpa nkata atụmatụ ka ndị Britain na-arụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu ma nara ụgwọ ọrụ maka ụbọchị ise
rows.output: The Labour Party denies that they are planning to force the British to work four days a week and pay them for five.
rows.reference: Labour denies it is devising a plan for Britons to work a four day week but be paid for five days

rows.source: Labour Party nke Jeremy Corbyn na-atule atụmatụ ga-agbanwe ihe nke ga-ahụ na ndị Britain rụọ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu ha anara ụgwọ ọrụ maka ụbọchị ise.
rows.output: The Labour Party, led by Jeremy Corbyn, is proposing a plan that would see workers in Britain working four days a week and earning a full five-day salary.
rows.reference: Jeremy Corbyn's Labour Party is to consider a radical plan which will see Britons working a four day week - but getting paid for five.

rows.source: Ndị otu a chọrọ ka ndị isi nwe ụlọ ọrụ na-enyefe akụ ha chekwabara n’aka ndị ọrụ siterena mgbanwe artificial intelligence (AI) site na inye ha ụbọchị ụma agaghị arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: This group wants company executives to transfer their accumulated wealth to employees through a change in artificial intelligence (AI) by giving them a day off.
rows.reference: The party reportedly wants company bosses to pass on savings made through the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution to workers by giving them an extra day off.

rows.source: Ọ ga-eme na ndị na-arụ ọrụ ga-erite elele ụbọchị atọ n’izu ụka ma welakwaa otu ụgwọ ọnwa.
rows.output: He will make the workers receive three days of leave in a week and pay them a full salary.
rows.reference: It would see employees enjoy a three-day weekend - but still take home the same pay.

rows.source: Ndị nzuputa okwu kwuru na echiche a “ga-adaba” na ebumnuche yana atụmatụ akụnụba nke otu a ime ka ọ dabaara ndị ọrụ.
rows.output: The spokespersons for the group said that this idea "will be in line" with the economic objectives and plans of the group to make it more beneficial for the workers.
rows.reference: Sources said the idea would 'fit' with the party's economic agenda and plans to tilt the country in favour of workers.

rows.source: Ndị otu Trades Union Congress akwadola ịmalite ụbọchị anọ n’ime izu dịka ụzọ ndị ọrụ ga-esi rite elele na akụnụba na-agbanwe.
rows.output: The Trade Union Congress has endorsed a four-day workweek as a way for workers to cope with the changing economy.
rows.reference: Shifting to a four-day week has been endorsed by the Trades Union Congress as a way for workers to take advantage of the changing economy.

rows.source: Onye senịọ nzuputa okwu nke Labour Party gwara Sunday Times: ‘A na-atu anya ịma ọkwa nyocha amụma tupu ngwucha afọ a.
rows.output: The Labour Party's spokesperson for the parliamentary group told Sunday Times: 'We are expecting to announce the results of the policy review before the end of the year.
rows.reference: A senior Labour Party source told The Sunday Times: 'A policy review is expected to be announced before the end of the year.

rows.source: ‘Ọ gaghị eme ozugbo mana ịrụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu bụ ebumnobi ndị otu a dabara n’usoro ihazi akụnụba ka ọ dabaara ndị ọrụ yana mkpokota ụzọ nrụpụta ihe nke ndị otu ahụ.’
rows.output: ‘It won’t be immediate, but working four days a week is the goal of this group to match the economic planning schedule as it suits the workers and the collection of production methods of the group.’
rows.reference: 'It won't happen overnight but a four-day working week is an aspiration that fits in with the party's approach to rebalancing the economy in favour of the worker as well as the party's overall industrial strategy.'

rows.source: Labour Party agaghị abụ ndị izizi kwadoro echiche a, ebe Green Party kwere nkwa ịrụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu n’ime oge ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị 2017.
rows.output: The Labour Party will not be the first to endorse this idea, while the Green Party has promised to work four days a week during the 2017 election period.
rows.reference: The Labour Party would not be the first to endorse such an idea, with the Green Party pledging a four-day working week during its 2017 general election campaign.

rows.source: Labour Party anaghị akwado ebumnuche ahụ ugbu a dịka otu, kosiladị.
rows.output: The Labour Party does not currently support the goal as a party, however.
rows.reference: The aspiration is currently not being endorsed by the Labour Party as a whole, however.

rows.source: Onye nkwuchite okwu Labour Party kwuru: ‘Ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu abughị amụma ndị otu a nke na ndị otu a anaghị atule ya.’
rows.output: The Labour Party spokesperson said: 'The four-day workweek is not a policy of this group, which is why this group does not consider it.'
rows.reference: A Labour Party spokesman said: 'A four-day working week is not party policy and it is not being considered by the party.'

rows.source: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell jiri ọgbakọ Labour mere izu gara aga were kọwapụta echiche ya maka mgbanwe na akụnụba.
rows.output: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used the Labour Party conference last week to outline his ideas for changing the economy.
rows.reference: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used last week's Labour conference to flesh out his vision for a socialist revolution in the economy.

rows.source: Mazị McDonnell kwuru na o kpebiri iweghachite ikike site na n’aka ndị ‘isi ụlọ ọrụ amaghị’ yana “ndị nrite oke uru’ n’ụlọ ọrụ ndị eji ebi ndụ.
rows.output: Mr. McDonnell said he decided to reclaim the right from "unknown corporate insiders" and "excessive compensation" in companies that were "used as personal piggy banks."
rows.reference: Mr McDonnell said he was determined to claw back power from 'faceless directors' and 'profiteers' at utility firms.

rows.source: Atụmatụ shadow chancellor ahụ pụtakwara na ndị nwere oke n’ụlọ ọrụ mmiri nwere ike ha agaghị enwetacha isi ego ha, maka gọọmentị Labour nwere ike ‘ime mwepu’ na ndabere ebumnobi ihe ezighi ezi.
rows.output: The shadow chancellor's plan also means that those who are well off in the water industry may not get the same level of profit as they would under Labour government, because the government may 'make cuts' in the basis of the wrong objectives.
rows.reference: The shadow chancellor's plans also mean current shareholders in water companies may not get back their entire stake as a Labour government could make 'deductions' on the grounds of perceived wrongdoing.

rows.source: O kwuputakwara atụmatụ itinye ndị ọrụ na bọdụ ụlọ ọrụ ma mepụta Inclusive Ownership Fund ga-enyefe pesenti 10 n’oke ụlọ ọrụ ndị nkịtị n’aka ndị ọrụ, ndị nwere ike inweta uru isi ego ruru £500.
rows.output: He also announced plans to put workers on the boards of companies and create an Inclusive Ownership Fund that will distribute 10 percent of the equity of publicly traded companies to employees, who can benefit from a maximum value of £500.
rows.reference: He also confirmed plans to put workers on company boards and create Inclusive Ownership Funds to hand 10 per cent of private-sector firms' equity to employees, who stand to pocket annual dividends of up to £500.

rows.source: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy gwa “60 minutes” ma nyocha ndị FBI enwere ike ịgbanwe obi ha
rows.output: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy told "60 minutes" that the FBI investigation could change their minds
