rows.source: Terry Branstad, onye nnọchite anya U.S na China bụkwa onye chịburu Iowa, onye mbupu ahịa nri ubi nke ukwuu na China, kwuru na China merụrụ ndị ọrụ, ndị ọrụ ugbo na azụmahịa nke America ahụ.
rows.output: Terry Branstad, the U.S. trade representative to China and a former governor of Iowa, which is a major exporter of agricultural products to China, said that China has harmed American workers, farmers and businesses.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: China, Branstad dere n’echiche ya na Des Moines Register na Sọnde, “na-ekwusi ike maka mmegide ahụ site na itinye mgbasa ozi n’akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi anyị.”
rows.output: China, in his column for the Des Moines Register on Sunday, emphasized the opposition by placing ads in our media outlets.
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: “N’ịgbasa ozi asị a, gọọmentị China na ewere oghere omenala America hụrụ n’anya bụ nke onye kwuo uche ya na mgbasa ozi enweghị mkpagbu were tinye mgbasa ozi akwụrụ ụgwọ na Des Moines Register.” Branstad dere.
rows.output: "In spreading this message, the Chinese government has taken advantage of the cultural openness of the United States, which is a free and open society, to place paid advertising in the Des Moines Register." Branstad wrote.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: “Ma ịtụlee ya n’ọdụ akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi dị n’okporo beijing ebe a, ịga ahụ na enwere obere olu ndịiche nke na ịghaghị ahụ ihe n’egosi n’ezie echiche di iche ndị China nwere ike nwee maka usoro akụnụba China nọ na nsogbu, ebe ọ bụ n’ụlọ mgbasa ozi nọ na njikwa nke China Communist Party,” ọ dere.
rows.output: "But when you look at the media landscape in Beijing, you can see that there is a small number of voices that are not really representative of the different views that the Chinese people may have about the Chinese economic system, which is in crisis, because the media is controlled by the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ọ gbakwunyere na “otu n’ime akwụkwọ akụkọ ama ama na China zenarịrị ibiputa” ederede ya, n’agbanyeghị na o kwughị akwụkwọ akụkọ nke ọ bụ.
rows.output: He added that "one of the most famous Chinese-language newspapers in the world has avoided publishing" his article, although he did not mention the newspaper.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ndị Repọblikan Na-akpachapụ Ndị Ntuli Aka Ụmụ-nwanyị Tupu Ntuli Aka Ọkara Ọchịchị Maka Ọgbaghara Kavanaugh, Ndị Nyocha Dọrọ Aka na Ntị
rows.output: The Republican Women's Committee is urging women to vote before the midterm elections for the Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh, who is under investigation for sexual misconduct.
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Dị ka ọtụtụ ndị isi Repọblikan kwụnyere ma kwuchitere Onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu Brett Kavanaugh n’ihu ebubo dị iche iche nke mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị, ndị nyocha adọọla aka na ntị na ha ga-ahụ ndapụta iwe ga-esite ọkachasị n’aka ụmụ-nwanyị, n’oge ntuli aka ọkara ọchịchị na-abịa.
rows.output: Like many Republican leaders who endorsed and defended Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of numerous allegations of sexual misconduct, investigators have warned that they will be looking for signs of the most intense backlash to come from women, in the upcoming midterm elections.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Mmetụta sochiri nke a dị elu nke ukwuu, na ọtụtụ ndị Repọblikan ka edekọbara na ha egosila na ha chọrọ ịga n’ihu mee ntuli aka.
rows.output: The consequences of this are so severe that many Republicans have been recorded as saying that they want to continue to hold elections.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Enweghị ike iweghachi ihe ndị ahụ,” Grant Reeher, onye ọkammụta nke sayensị ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na Syracuse University Maxwell School gwara The Hill maka ederede nke ebiputara na Satọde.
rows.output: "Unable to recover the items," Grant Reeher, a political science professor at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill in a written statement on Saturday.
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reeher kwuru na ya na-agbagha n’ọkwụkwa ikpeazụ nke Onye Ọmebe Iwu Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) mere maka nyocha FBI a ga-ezu iji wetuo iwe ndị ntuli aka.
rows.output: Reeher said he was voting against the final amendment of the bill by Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) that would have ended the FBI's investigation into the allegations of Russian interference in the 2016 election.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: “Ụmụ-nwanyị agaghị echefu ihe mere ụnyahụ - ha agaghị echefu echi niile ma Nọvemba, “ Karine Jean-Pierre, onye ndụmọdụ senịọ na onye nkwuchite okwu obodo maka otu ọganihu MoveOn kwuru na Fraịde, dabere na akwụkwọ akụkọ Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday - they will not forget tomorrow and November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, said on Friday, according to the Washington Post.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: N’ụtụtụ Fraịde, ndị ngagharị iwe kwere ukwe “Nọvemba na-abịa!” ka ha na-agagharị ngagharị iwe n’ogologo ụzọ Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu ebe ndị Repọblikan ji Ọgbakọ Ọka Ikpe họrọ ịga n’ihu na nhọrọ Kavanaugh agbanyeghị nkwuputa Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic kwuputara.
rows.output: On Friday morning, protesters chanted "November is coming!" as they marched through the streets of the Capitol, where Republicans in the Senate Judiciary Committee decided to proceed with the confirmation of Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, reported Mic.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: “Ịnụ ọkụ n’obi na mkpalite mmụọ nke Demokrat ga-apụ iche,” Stu Rothenberg, onye nyocha ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị enweghị otu o binyere gwara ndị akụkọ.
rows.output: "Enthusiasm and the inspiration of the Democrats will be different," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told reporters.
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: “Ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọ dịla elu; nke a bụ eziokwu.
rows.output: "People say it's high; this is true."
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Mana ọ nwere ike ịgbagokwu ọkachasị n’etiti ụmụ-nwanyị n’enweghị otu ha binyere n’ime obodo yana ndị ntuli aka na-etolite etolite, gbara afọ 18- ruo 29-, bụ ndị ebe onye isi ala anaghị amasị, anaghị eme ntuli aka kwa mgbe.”
rows.output: But you can also see the most striking thing among women without a party affiliation and among young voters, aged 18 to 29, who are in a country where the president is not liked, and who do not vote regularly.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Ọbụlagodi tupu nkwuputanke ọha Ford mere na-akọwa ebubo mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị megide onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe kachasị Elu, ndị nyocha na-atụ elo na ndapụta iwe nwere ike sote ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Repọblikan gaa n’ihu mee nkwado ahụ.
rows.output: Even before Ford's public statement, investigators were suggesting that a resignation might follow if Republicans continued to support the nominee for the Supreme Court.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Nke a abụrụla ọgbaghara dịịrị GOP,” Michael Steele kwuru, onye isi chịburu Ọgbakọ Otu Repọblikan, na mbido izug ara aga, dabere na NBC News.
rows.output: "This has become a nightmare for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, on the first day of the Republican debate, as reported by NBC News.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ bụghị naanị maka ntuli aka ndị ọgbakọ ma ọ bụ maka ntuli aka ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma etinyere Kavanaugh n’oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Repọblikan siri jikwaa ihe a ma ka ha siri meso ya omume,” Guy Cecil, onye isi Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka ahọpụta ndị Demokrat, rụtụrụ ndị akụkọ aka.
rows.output: "It's not just about the vote for the Senate or the vote for the Supreme Court or whether Kavanaugh is on the bench, but also about how Republicans have managed this issue and how they've treated it," Guy Cecil, the president of Priorities USA, a group that helps elect Democrats, told reporters.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, Ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n’onye ha ga-ekwenyere na ndapụta nkwuputa Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwụnyere onye nke ikpeazụ.
rows.output: However, Americans are split on who they trust more, Ford or Kavanaugh, with more trusting the latter.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Nyocha ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov gosiri na pesentị 41 ndị zara ajụjụ kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ nkwuputa Ford, ebe pesentị 35 kwuru na ha kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ Kavanaugh.
rows.output: A recent survey from YouGov showed that 41% of respondents either strongly agree or somewhat agree with Ford's statement, while 35% either strongly agree or somewhat agree with Kavanaugh's statement.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Na mgbakwunye, pesentị 38 kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh eleghị anya sịrị asị ma ọ bụ sịa asị kpamkpam n’oge nkwuputa ya, ebe naanị pesentị 30 kwuru otu ihe ahụ maka Ford.
rows.output: Furthermore, 38 percent said they believed that Kavanaugh was probably lying or definitely lying during his testimony, while only 30 percent said the same about Ford.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: Ka Flake mechara nkwanye, ndị FBI na-eme nyocha ugbu a n’ebubo Ford boro, yana opekempe otu onye ebubo ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez mere, The Guardian kwuputara.
rows.output: After Flake's acquittal, the FBI is currently investigating Ford's allegations, as well as at least one other accusation, made by Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford mere nkwuputa n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’okpuru iyi n’izu gara aga na Kavanaugh dakporo ya n’anya mmanya mgbe ọ gbara afọ 17.
rows.output: Ford made a statement in front of the House Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh assaulted her with alcohol when she was 17 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez boro ebubo n’onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ahụ gosiri ya ike ya mgbe ha na-eme ọgbakọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ n’oge ha na-agụ akwụkwọ na Yale n’ime 1980s.
rows.output: Ramirez accused the Supreme Court nominee of showing off his wealth during social gatherings during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Onye Mmepụta World Wide Web Na-ama Atụmatụ Ịmalite Ịntanetị Ọhụrụ Iji Sonyere Google na Facebook
rows.output: The World Wide Web Consortium is Planning to Launch a New Internet Initiative to Collaborate with Google and Facebook
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, onye mmepụta World Wide Web, na-amalite ụlọ ọrụ ọhụrụ nke ga-achụso Facebook, Amazon na Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the creator of the World Wide Web, is starting a new company that will compete with Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Atụmatụ ọhụrụ ahụ nke ọkaibe teknụzụ, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-agbakwasa ụkwụ na ngwanro ghe oghe Berners-Lee, Solid.
rows.output: The new plan, Inrupt, a tech-savvy startup, is a company that is building on top of the open-source software framework, Solid, created by Berners-Lee.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere ịhọrọ ebe ha ga-echekwa data ha yana ozi ndị mmadụ nwere ike nweta.
rows.output: Solid provides users with the opportunity to choose where they want to store their data and information that people can access.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: N’ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche Fast Company mere, Berners-Lee mara njakịrị na ebumnuche ejiri mebe Inrupt bụ “ịchị mba ụwa.”
rows.output: In a special interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the purpose of Inrupt was "to rule the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a,” o kwuru maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.
rows.output: "We will do it now," he said for the new house.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: “Ọ bụ oge a ga-edebanye na akụkọ.”
rows.output: "It's time to register for the history."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ngwa ahụ na-eji teknụzụ Solid enye ndị mmadụ oghere imepụta “ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị” ma ọ bụ POD.
rows.output: The device uses Solid technology to give people the opportunity to create their own "personal online data storage" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ọ nwere ike inwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe omume, kalenda, ọba egwu yana ngwa nkeonwe na nke eji arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: It may have a contact list, a to-do list, a calendar, a music player, and personal and work apps.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ọ dị ka Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack na Spotify dị n’otu nchọgharị ma ha niile n’otu oge.
rows.output: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify all in one browser and all at once.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ihe pụrụ iche na ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị bụ na ọ dịịrị naanị onye ji ya arụ ọrụ ịhọrọ onye ga-enweta ozi nke ọ bụla.
rows.output: The unique thing about personal data storage on the internet is that it is up to the person who owns it to decide who will have access to it.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya “ikike nkeonwe site na data.”
rows.output: The company calls it "personalization through data."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Ebumnuche Inrupt, dabere na CEO John Bruce, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ kpokọba, akụrụngwa, usoro na nka dabara daba iji nyere aka mee ka Solid rute onye ọ bụla.
rows.output: The mission of Inrupt, based on CEO John Bruce, is to bring together the company's resources, infrastructure, systems, and expertise to help Solid reach everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nwere naanị Berners-Lee, Bruce, ebe nchekwa IBM zụtara na ya, ndị ọrụ nrụpụta ewere n’ọrụ ịrụ n’atụmatụ ahụ yana ọgbakọ ndị koodu wepụtara onwe ha.
rows.output: The company was only Berners-Lee, Bruce, where IBM's storage division had purchased a stake in it, and a team of engineers were hired to work on the project, along with a group of volunteer coders.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Site n’izu a, ndị nrụpụta teknụzụ ụwa gbaa gburugburu ga-enwe ike mebe ngwa agaghị ekpokọba ọnụ nke ha site n’iji ngwa mebere na websaịtị Inrupt.
rows.output: By the end of this week, global tech manufacturers will be able to create non-removable software applications of their own using the Inrupt-developed application builder on the Inrupt website.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya ndị otu ya anaghị agwa ndị “Facebook na Google okwu banyere ma ha a ga-amalite ma ọ bụ hapụ mmalite mgbanwe kpamkpam ebe ụdịdị azụmahịa na-atụgharị ozugbo na ntabi anya.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that his team was not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether they would start or abandon the radical change where the business model is turned upside down and the focus is immediately on the user.
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: “Anyị anaghị anata ha ikike.”
rows.output: "We do not accept them."
rows.reference: "We are not asking their permission."

rows.source: Na mbipụta emere na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na “ebumnuche Inrupt bụ inye ike azụmahịa na gburugburu inyere aka chekwaa ntụkwasị obi na ịdị mma weebu ọhụrụ ahụ arụrụ na Solid.”
rows.output: In a Medium post on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that "the mission of Inrupt is to empower businesses and the environment to help maintain the trust and integrity of the new web platform built on Solid."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Na 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ mepụtara World Wide Web Consortuim na Massachusetts Institue of Technology.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee revolutionized the Internet by creating the World Wide Web Consortium at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: N’ọnwa ndị adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee bụ olu na-ada ụda na arụmarụ ụka nnwere onwe ọrụ ịntanetị.
rows.output: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been a vocal advocate for the freedom of the internet.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Ọbulagodi mgbe a na-ebuputa Inrupt, Berners-Lee ga-anọrọ dịka onye Mmepụta na Onye Isi nke World Wide Web Consortuim, Web Foundation na Open Data Institute.
rows.output: Even after the launch of Inrupt, Berners-Lee would remain as the Founder and Chairman of the World Wide Web Consortium, Web Foundation, and Open Data Institute.
rows.reference: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: “A na m enwe olile anya nke ukwuu maka oge na-abịa n’ihu nke weebu,” Berners-Lee gbakwunyere.
rows.output: "We are very optimistic about the future of the web," Berners-Lee added.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.source: Bernard Vann: Emere emume onye ụkọchukwu Victoria Cross WW1
rows.output: Bernard Vann: A ceremony for the Victoria Cross WW1 priest
rows.reference: Bernard Vann: WW1 Victoria Cross cleric celebrated

rows.source: Emeela emume nke naanị ụkọchukwu Church of England nwetara mmeri Victoria Cross n’oge World War One dị ka onye agha n’obodo ya ka afọ gbara 100.
rows.output: A ceremony was held for the only Church of England priest to receive the Victoria Cross during World War One as a soldier in his home country 100 years ago.
rows.reference: The only Church of England cleric to win a Victoria Cross during World War One as a combatant has been celebrated in his hometown 100 years on.

rows.source: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann nwetara awọdụ na 29, Septemba 1918 na mbuso agha emere na Bellenglise na Lehaucourt.
rows.output: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann was awarded the Distinguished Service Order on 29 September 1918 for the attack made on Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.
rows.reference: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann won the award on 29 September 1918 in the attack at Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, mgbọ ọkaibe n’ịgba egbe tụrụ ya ka ụbọchị anọ gachara na ọ maghị ncha ncha na etubere ya ugo ndị agha kachasị na Britain.
rows.output: However, a bullet wound in the leg forced him to rest for four days, during which he learned to appreciate the comforts of a soft bed and the company of his fellow soldiers.
rows.reference: However, he was killed by a sniper four days later and never knew he had won the highest British military honour.

rows.source: Ụmụ ụmụ ya ndị nwoke abụọ kpughere okwute iji na-eme ncheta ya na ngarube emere na Rushden, Northamptonshire, na Satọde.
rows.output: His two sons unveiled a stone to commemorate him at a memorial service held in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.

rows.output: We want to impose higher stamp duty on foreign buyers when they purchase assets in the UK - the money will be used to help those in need, Theresa May will announce this today.

rows.output: The government will impose a stamp duty on individuals and companies that do not pay taxes in the UK, and the revenue generated will be used to increase the government's efforts to combat tax avoidance.

rows.source: Ekpebiri na pasentị 13 bụ ndị na abụghị ndị bi na UK na azụta akụ ndị London arụrụ ọhụrụ, na ebugo ụgwọ ma na eme ka o sie ike maka ndị na eme nzụta izizi ha iji nweta ọganihu n’nzọụkwụ obibi ụlọ.
rows.output: The government has decided that 13 percent of the buyers of new-build homes in London are not UK residents, and that they are bringing in debt and making it difficult for first-time buyers to get on the housing ladder.
rows.reference: An estimated 13 per cent of new-build London properties are bought by non-UK residents, driving up prices and making it harder for first-time buyers to get a foot on the housing ladder.

rows.source: Imirikiti mpaghara ndị nwere ego n’obodo ahụ - karịchara n’isi ala - nwere “ime obodo tọgbọ nkịtị” n’ihi ọnụọgụ nke ndị nzụta ofesi dị elu, ndị na anọ ọtụtụ oge ha na mpụga nke obodo ahụ.
rows.output: The local elite in the city - especially in the lower strata - had "ordinary urban" incomes due to the high number of foreign buyers, who often spent most of their time outside the city.
rows.reference: Many wealthy areas of the country - particularly in the capital - have become "ghost towns" because of the high number of foreign buyers who spend most of their time out of the country.

rows.source: Iwu ọhụrụ ahụ na abịa n’izu ole ma ole ka Boris Johnson kpọchara oku maka mgbubi n’ọrụ stampụ iji nyere ndị ntorobịa aka ịnwe ụlọ izizi nke ha.
rows.output: The new law is coming in a few weeks after Boris Johnson called for a ban on stamp duty to help first-time buyers.
rows.reference: The new policy comes just weeks after Boris Johnson called for a stamp duty cut to help more young people own their first home.

rows.source: O boro ndị nnukwu ụlọ ọrụ nrụpụta ebubo maka idowe akụ n’ọnụego dị elu site na ịnapụ ala mana ha anaghị eji ya, ma rịọ Nwada May ka ọ hapụ oke n’ụlọ ndị dị ọnụ ala iji dozie “ihere ụlọ obibi” nke Britain.
rows.output: He accused large landowners of hoarding land at high prices by not using it, and asked Mrs. May to remove the cap on low-cost housing to address the "housing shame" of Britain.
rows.reference: He accused big construction firms of keeping property prices high by snapping up land but not using it, and urged Mrs May to abandon quotas on affordable homes to fix Britain's "housing disgrace."

rows.source: Maazị Corbyn ekwuputela usoro mmezi ụlọ obibi na adọta ntinye uche, gụnyere njikwa ụgwọ ụlọ yana nkwụsị nke nchụpụ “abụghị ụta mmadụ”.
rows.output: Mr. Corbyn has announced a series of measures to address the housing crisis, including rent control and the abolition of "no-fault" evictions.
rows.reference: Mr Corbyn has announced an eye-catching series of proposed housing reforms, including rent controls and an end to "no-fault" evictions.

rows.source: Ọ chọkwara ịnyekwu ndị kansụl ikike iji rụpụta ụlọ ọhụrụ.
rows.output: He also wanted to give more power to the council to build new houses.
rows.reference: He also wants to give councils greater powers to build new homes.

rows.source: Nwada May kwuru: “Afọ gara aga m kwuru m ga-ewepụta ọchịchị m iji weghachite nrọ Britain - ndụ ahụ kwesịrị ka mma maka agbụrụ ọhụrụ ọ bụla.
rows.output: Ms. May said: "Last year I said I would take the leadership of the country to restore the British dream - life should be better for any new generation.
rows.reference: Mrs May said: "Last year I said I would dedicate my premiership to restoring the British dream - that life should be better for each new generation.

rows.source: Ma nke ahụ pụtara idozi ahịa ụlọ obibi anyị mebiri emebi.
rows.output: That means fixing our broken housing market.

rows.source: Britain ga-ekpughere oge niile maka ndị mmadụ chọrọ ibi, rụọ ọrụ ma bido ndụ ebe a.

rows.reference: Britain will always be open to people who want to live, work and build a life here.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, ọ nweghị ike ịdị mma na ọ dị mfe maka ndị mmadụ na ebighi n’ime UK, yanakwa ụlọ ọrụ ndị ofesi, iji zụta ụlọ ka ndị obibi Britain na arụsị ọrụ ike.
rows.output: However, it is not possible to be too good and too easy for people and foreign companies to buy homes when British citizens are struggling to afford them.

rows.output: For many people, the dream of owning their own home is within reach, the pollution of homelessness is a reality.

rows.source: Jack Ross: ‘Ọchịchọ m kachasị bụ ijikwa Scotland’
rows.output: Jack Ross: 'My greatest ambition is to manage Scotland'

rows.source: Onye isi nke Sunderland Jack Ross kwuru na “ọchịchọ ya kachasị” bụ ịbụrụ onye ndu Scotland otu oge.
rows.output: Sunderland's head coach Jack Ross said his "biggest wish" is to be Scotland's manager one day.
rows.reference: Sunderland boss Jack Ross says his "ultimate ambition" is to become the Scotland manager at some stage.

rows.source: Onye Scotland ahụ, 42, na enwe obi ụtọ maka mgba nke iweghachite otu asọmpi North-East, ndị nọ ugbu a n’ọkwa atọ na League One, akara atọ n’okpuru nke isi.
rows.output: The 42-year-old Scot is delighted with the challenge of bringing back the North-East title, currently held by the third-placed team in League One, three points below the top.
rows.reference: The Scot, 42, is relishing the challenge of reviving the North-East club, who currently sit third place in League One, three points off the top.

rows.source: Ọ gara na Stadium of Light n’ọkọchị a ka o duchara St Mirren laghachite na Scottish Premiership n’afọ asọmpi gara aga.
rows.output: He went to the Stadium of Light in the autumn to watch St Mirren return to the Scottish Premiership in the previous season's campaign.
rows.reference: He moved to the Stadium of Light this summer after guiding St Mirren back to the Scottish Premiership last season.

rows.source: “Achọburu m ịgbara obodo m bọọlụ ka m bụ onye egwu.
rows.output: I wanted to play football for my country as a player.
rows.reference: "I wanted to play for my country as a player.

rows.source: Enwetara m cap B nke ahụ bụ ya,” Ross gwara Sportsound nke BBC Scotland.
rows.output: I got that B cap, and that was it," Ross told BBC Scotland's Sportsound.
rows.reference: I got a B cap and that was it," Ross told BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

rows.source: “Mana etolitere m na elele Scotland na Hampden ọtụtụ oge, mụ na nna m ka m bụ nwata, ọ bụ ihe na adọghachi m oge niile.
rows.output: But I grew up watching Scotland at Hampden many times, with my dad when I was a kid, it's something that always drew me in.
rows.reference: "But I grew up watching Scotland at Hampden a lot with my dad as a kid, and it is always something that has drawn me back.

rows.output: The opportunity will come, however, if I do well in managing the team.
rows.reference: That opportunity would only come, though, if I am successful in club management."

rows.reference: Ross's predecessors as Sunderland manager include Dick Advocaat, David Moyes, Sam Allardyce, Martin O'Neill, Roy Keane, Gus Poyet and Paulo Di Canio.

rows.source: Onye isi nke Alloa Athletic gara aga kwuru na ọ naghị enwe ụjọ n’isochi aha ndị ahụ ama ama n’ụdịrị nnukwu otu ahụ, ka ọ jụchara arịrịọ ndị si na Barnsley na Ipswich Town.
rows.output: The former chairman of Alloa Athletic said he was not afraid to follow in the footsteps of the famous names in the club's history, after rejecting approaches from Barnsley and Ipswich Town.
rows.reference: The former Alloa Athletic boss says he felt no trepidation in following such established names at such a big club, having previously rejected overtures from Barnsley and Ipswich Town.

rows.source: “Ọganihu maka m n’oge a ka a ga-atụ site na “enwere m ike idughachi otu a na Premier League?’
rows.output: "Progress for me in this period will be measured by 'can I bring this team back to the Premier League?'"
rows.reference: "Success for me at the moment will be gauged by 'can I return this club to the Premier League?'

rows.source: N’ihi nyiwe na ụlọ nke otu a, na enweghị mgbagha kwesịrị ịnọ na Premier League,” o kwuru.

rows.output: "It's not an easy task to go back there, but I can only see myself as a person who did well here if I can bring that same mentality back there."
rows.reference: "It is not an easy task to get it there, but I would probably only view myself as being successful here if I can get the club back there."

rows.source: Ross nọ naanị afọ atọ n’ọrụ njikwa ya, ka obere oge gachara ka onye enyemaka na Dumbarton yana ọnụnọ ọnwa 15 n’otu ndị ọrụ Hearts.
rows.output: Ross was only in his third year of management, having had only a short period as an assistant at Dumbarton and 15 months in the staff at Hearts.

rows.source: “Ekwenyere n’ezie na njikwa bụ ihe ziri m nke ọma, karịa ịgba agba.
rows.output: I believe that management is something I'm good at, better than just talking.

rows.output: It's better to be good because I did well, had a good life with it, and had some vision of what the higher things are.

rows.source: Mana ịgba agba na esi ike.
rows.output: But the paint is very hard.

rows.output: I passed through that part of the conversation that dealt with the problems and challenges of the project, but the management was good in my eyes.
rows.reference: I still go through that in terms of the stresses and pressure of the job but management just feels right.

rows.source: Bido na mbụ achọrọ m ịme njikwa, ugbu a ana m eme ya, ọ kachasị enye m mmetụta obi ume ala, abụ m onwe m na ndụ okenye m niile.”
rows.output: First, I wanted to be in control, now I am, it's the most empowering feeling, I am myself in my adult life."
rows.reference: I always wanted to manage and now I am doing it, it feels the most comfortable I have been in my own skin throughout my entire adult life."

rows.source: Okpomọkụ ọkọchị etipuola ego maka ụlọ mmanya ndị Britain ndị na aghọ ada mana dosakwuo nsogbu n’elu ndị azụmahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ.
rows.output: The cold weather has caused significant losses for British-owned bars, but has also created problems for local restaurants.
rows.reference: The summer heatwave has boosted takings for Britain's struggling pubs but heaped more pressure on restaurant chains.

rows.source: Otu ndị ụlọ mmanya hụrụ ka ahịa rịgoro pasentị 2.7 na Julaị - mana nrite n’ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ dara pasentị 4.8, ọnụọgụ gosiri.
rows.output: The Hotel and Restaurant Association reported a 2.7% increase in sales in July - but the award for restaurants fell 4.8%, the data showed.
rows.reference: Pub and bar groups saw sales rise 2.7 per cent in July - but takings in restaurants were down 4.8 per cent, figures revealed.

rows.source: Peter Martin, nke ndị ndụmọdụ azụmahịa CGA, nke kpokọrọ ọnụọgụ ahụ, kwuru: “Anyanwụ ka dị yana nsonye England na World Cup toro ogologo ole atụrụ anya pụtara na Julaị sochiri otu usoro ka ọnwa nke Juun gara aga, mgbe ụlọ mmanya rịgoro pasentị 2.8, belụsọ na ndị ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ nwere nnukwu nhịahụ.
rows.output: Peter Martin, from CGA's business advisory group, which compiled the figures, said: "The sun is still shining and England's participation in the World Cup has meant that the long-expected rise in sales in July followed a similar pattern to that in June, when pubs rose by 2.8%, except for restaurants, which had a poor month.
rows.reference: Peter Martin, of business consultancy CGA, which compiled the figures, said: "Continued sunshine and England's longer than expected participation in the World Cup meant July followed a similar pattern to the previous month of June, when pubs were up 2.8 per cent, except that restaurants were hit even harder.

rows.source: Nrịda nke pasentị 1.8 n’azụmahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ na Juun kawanyere njọ na Julai.
rows.output: A decline of 1.8 percent in the restaurant business in June was worse than in July.
rows.reference: The fall of 1.8 per cent in restaurant trading in June just got worse in July.

rows.source: Ụlọ mmanya kachasị mee nke ọma otu yitere ihe dị ka otu ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ si gbadaa.
rows.output: The best bar in the world is like one big restaurant.
rows.reference: Drink-led pubs and bars performed by far the strongest with like-for-likes up more than restaurants were down.

rows.source: Ụlọ mmanya na ere nri tara ahụhụ n’anyanwụ, mana ọbụghị ka nke ndị na azụ ahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ.
rows.output: The bars and restaurants suffered losses in the afternoon, but not as much as those of the hotels.

rows.output: The judges in New York are seeking the death penalty for Sayfullo Saipov, who is suspected of a terror attack in New York that killed eight people -- a penalty that has not been carried out in the state for a crime committed in the city center since 1953.

rows.source: Iji gosi ihe kpatara ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ ji dị mma, ndị ọkaikpe ga-egosi na Saipov “kpachara anya” gbuo ndị mmadụ asatọ ma “kpachara anya” merụọ ndị mmadụ nnukwu ahụ, site n’ọkwa nke ebumnuche iji chọọ ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ, nke Southern District nke New York gbara n’akwụkwọ.
rows.output: To demonstrate the justification for the death penalty, judges must show that Saipov “premeditated” the deaths of eight people and “intentionally” injured many others, from the level of intent to seek the death penalty, which the Southern District of New York has filed.
rows.reference: In order to justify a death sentence, prosecutors will have to prove that Saipov "intentionally" killed the eight victims and "intentionally" inflicted serious bodily injury, according to the notice of intent to seek the death penalty, filed in the Southern District of New York.

rows.source: Ebubo abụọ ndị a nwere ike ibu ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ, site n’aka akwụkwọ ụlọ ikpe ahụ.
rows.output: The two charges can carry the death penalty, according to the court documents.
rows.reference: Both of those counts carry a possibly death sentence, according to the court document.

rows.source: Izu sotechara mbuso agha ahụ, ndị otu ikpe etiti obodo manyere Saipov ebubo ngụ-22 nke gụnyere ebubo asatọ maka igbu mmadụ n’enyemaka nke izu oyi, nke ndị ọkaikpe etiti obodo na ejikarị n’okwu ajọ mpu, yana ebubo nke ihe ike na mmebi nke ụgbọ ala.
rows.output: The following week, the Central District Court charged Saipov with 22 counts, including eight counts of murder in the first degree, which is typically reserved for cases of extreme atrocity or heinous crimes, as well as counts of terrorism and destruction of property.
rows.reference: Weeks after the attack, a federal grand jury slapped Saipov with a 22-count indictment that included eight charges of murder in aid of racketeering, typically used by federal prosecutors in organized crime cases, and a charge of violence and destruction of motor vehicles.

rows.source: Mbuso agha ahụ chọrọ “nhazi na ntụle echiche dị ọkpụrụkpụ,” ndị ọkaikpe kwuru, na akọwara omume nke Saipov jiri mee ya ka “arụ, jọrọ njọ na mmetọ.”
rows.output: The attack's objective was "a sophisticated thought-out plan," the judges said, and described Saipov's actions as "brutal, inhumane and degrading."
rows.reference: The attack required "substantial planning and premeditation," prosecutors said, describing the manner in which Saipov carried it out as "heinous, cruel and depraved."

rows.source: "Sayfullo Habibullaevic Saipov butere mmerụ ahụ, mmekpa ahụ, na mbibi maka ezinụlọ na ndị enyi nke Diego Enrique Angelini, Nicholas Cleves, Ann-Laure Decadt, Darren Drake, Ariel Erlij, Hernan Ferruchi, Hernan Diego Mendoza, na Alejandro Damian Pagnucco," ọkwa nke ebumnuche kwuru.
rows.output: "Sayfullo Habibullaevic Saipov caused harm, suffering, and destruction to the families and friends of Diego Enrique Angelini, Nicholas Cleves, Ann-Laure Decadt, Darren Drake, Ariel Erlij, Hernan Ferruchi, Hernan Diego Mendoza, and Alejandro Damian Pagnucco," the statement said.

rows.source: Oge ikpeazụ emere ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ na okwu etiti obodo nke New York bụ na 1953 maka Julius na Ethel Rosenberg, di na nwunye egburu ka amachara ha ikpe maka ịkpa nkata iji mee ọrụ sabo maka Soviet Union n’oge Cold War afọ abụọ ya gara aga.
rows.output: The last time capital punishment was carried out in the city of New York was in 1953 for Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple convicted of espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War of the two preceding years.
rows.reference: The last time the death penalty was carried out in a New York federal case was in 1953 for Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple executed after they were convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War two years before.

rows.source: Eji oche latrik wee gbuo Rosenberg abụọ ahụ na Juun 19, 1953.

rows.output: David Patton, one of the lawyers for the middle class in the case of Saipov, said they had "deep regret" for the decision of the court.

rows.source: “Anyị chere na mkpebi iji chọọ ntaramahụhụ ọnwụ kama ịnara arịrịọ ikpe ọmụma maka ndụ niile n’ime nga na enweghị ohere nke nhapụ naanị ga-adọtịkwu ụjọ nke mmemme ndị ahụ maka mmadụ niile emetụtara,” Patton kwuru.
rows.output: "We believe that the decision to seek the death penalty instead of a life sentence in prison with no chance of parole will only increase the fear of the events for all those affected," Patton said.

rows.reference: It's hard to explain, but it was on the flight I felt this overwhelming sense of sympathy for Nad.

rows.source: Na ọ chọrọ ịhụnanya na nghọta m.
rows.output: I just want your love and understanding.
rows.reference: That he needed my love and understanding.

rows.source: Ama m otu o si hụ ya n’anya.”
rows.output: I know how she feels and I love her too.”

rows.source: Ụmụ nwanyị na eru uju na ebisa kaadị iji gbochie ịkwụ ụdọ n’akwa mmiri
rows.output: Women in distress signal for help by flashing their identity cards to prevent being lured into the sea
rows.reference: Grieving women post cards to prevent suicides on bridge

rows.source: Ụmụ nwanyị abụọ ndị ịkwụ ụdọ napụrụ ndị ha hụrụ n’anya na arụ ọrụ iji gbochie ndị ọzọ n’igbu onwe ha.
rows.output: Two women who were hanged for their love of each other worked to prevent others from committing suicide.
rows.reference: Two women who lost loved ones to suicide are working to prevent others from taking their own lives.

rows.source: Sharon Davis na Kelly Humphreys na ebisa kaadị nwere ozi na akpalite mmụọ na akara ekwentị kemgbe n’akwa mmiri Welsh nke ndị mmadụ nwere ike ịkpọ maka enyemaka.
rows.output: Sharon Davis and Kelly Humphreys have been posting cards with messages and phone numbers on the Welsh coast, where people can call for help.
rows.reference: Sharon Davis and Kelly Humphreys have been posting cards on a Welsh bridge with inspirational messages and phone numbers that people can call for support.

rows.source: Nwa nwoke Nwada Davis bụ Tyler dị afọ 13 mgbe o bidoro nwebe obi ịda mba wee gbuo onwe ya n’afọ 18.
rows.output: Ms. Davis's son, Tyler, was 13 years old when he began experiencing severe depression and committed suicide at the age of 18.
rows.reference: Ms Davis' son Tyler was 13 when he began suffering with depression and killed himself aged 18.

rows.source: O kwuru “achọghị m ka nne na nna ọ bụla nwee ụdị mmetụta m na enwe kwa ụbọchị,”.
rows.output: He said, "I don't want any parent to feel the kind of pain I feel every day."
rows.reference: "I don't want any parent to feel the way I have to feel everyday," she said.

rows.source: Nwada Davis, afọ 45, onye bi na Lydney, kwuru na nwa nwoke ya bụ osi nri na ekwe nkwa n’ọdịnihu nwere ọchị na efe efe.
rows.output: Ms. Davis, 45, from Lydney, said her son is a talented cook and has a promising future with humor and dance.
rows.reference: Ms Davis, aged 45, who lives in Lydney, said her son was a promising chef with an infectious grin.

rows.source: “Mmadụ niile ma ya maka ọchị ya.
rows.output: Everyone laughed at his joke.
rows.reference: "Everyone knew him for his smile.

rows.source: Ha na ekwu oge niile na ọchị ya na ebulite ime ụlọ ọ bụla.”
rows.output: They always say that his laughter and the lifting of every room are the best things.
rows.reference: They always said his smile lit up any room."

rows.source: Kaosiladị, ọ kwụsịrị ọrụ tupu ọ nwụọ, n’ihi na ọ “n’ebe jọrọ oke njọ.”
rows.output: However, he stopped working before he died, because he was "in a very bad state."
rows.reference: However, he gave up work before he died, as he was "in a really dark place."

rows.source: Na 2014, nwanne nwoke Tyler, onye dị 11 n’oge ahụ, bụ onye nke hụrụ nwanne ya ka o gbuchara onwe ya.
rows.output: In 2014, Tyler's younger brother, who was 11 at the time, witnessed his brother's suicide.
rows.reference: In 2014, Tyler's brother, who was 11 at the time, was the one to find his sibling after he had taken his own life.

rows.source: Nwada Davis kwuru: “Ọ na eche m oge niile na a ga-enwe mmetụta nsotanso.”
rows.output: Ms. Davis said: "I always thought we would eventually have a sense of normalcy."
rows.reference: Ms Davis said: "I continually worry that there's going to be a knock on effect."

rows.source: Nwada Davis mere kaadị ndị ahụ, “iji mee ka ndị mmadụ mara na enwere ndị mmadụ nọ ebe a ha nwere ike ịgakwu ma gwa okwu, ọbụlagodi na ọ bụ enyi.
rows.output: Ms. Davis made those cards, "to make people aware that there are people here who can go out and talk, even if it's just a friend.
rows.reference: Ms Davis created the cards, "to let people know there are people out there that you can go to and you can talk to, even if it's a friend.

rows.source: Etukwuna na nkịtị - ị kwesịrị ikwu okwu.”
rows.output: The common man - you should speak up.
rows.reference: Don't sit in silence - you need to talk."

rows.source: Nwada Humphreys, onye bụ enyi Nwada Davies ọtụtụ afọ, enweghịzị Mark, di ya nke afọ 15, n’obere oge ka nne ya nwụchara.
rows.output: Ms. Humphreys, who had been friends with Ms. Davies for many years, did not know Mark, her husband of 15 years, for a short time after his mother's death.
rows.reference: Ms Humphreys, who has been friends with Ms Davies for years, lost Mark, her partner of 15 years, not long after the death of his mother.

rows.source: O kwuru “o kwughi na ọ na enwe obi umeala ma ọ bụ ịda mba ma ọ bụ ihe ọ bụla,”.
rows.output: He said, "You're not feeling any more confident or insecure or anything like that,".
rows.reference: "He didn't say that he was feeling down or depressed or anything," she said.

rows.source: “Ụbọchị ole ma ole tupu Ekeresimesi anyị chọpụtara mgbanwe n’omume ya.
rows.output: A few days before Christmas, we discovered a change in his behavior.
rows.reference: "A couple of days before Christmas we noticed his change in attitude.

rows.source: Ọ nọ n’ala ala na Ubọchi Ekeresimesi - mgbe ụmụaka mepere onyinye ha anya ya na nke ha akụtaghị ma ọ bụ ihe ọ bụla.”
rows.output: He was on the floor on Christmas morning - when the children opened their presents and he saw what they had received and what they hadn't.
rows.reference: He was at rock bottom on Christmas Day - when the kids opened their presents he didn't make eye contact with them or anything."

rows.source: O kwuru na ọnwụ ya bụ nnukwu nkụja n’ebe ha nọ, mana ha ga-arụkọta ọrụ iji gafere ya: “Ọ gbapuru oghere n’ime ezinụlọ ahụ.
rows.output: He said his death was a big blow to them, but they would have to work together to get over it: "It created a hole in the family.
rows.reference: She said his death was a huge trauma to them, but they have to work through it: "It rips a hole through the family.

rows.source: Ọ na ekewa anyị.
rows.output: He is dividing us.
rows.reference: It tears us apart.

rows.source: Mana anyị niile ga-aga n’ihu na agba mgba.”
rows.output: But we all have to keep moving forward and fight.
rows.reference: But we've all got to carry on and fight."

rows.source: Ọ bụrụ na ị na enwe nhịahụ ịga n’ihu, ị nwere ike ịkpọ Samaritans n’efu na 116 123 (UK and Ireland), email jo@samaritans.org, ma ọ bụ gaa na weebụsaịtị ndị Samaritans ebe a.
rows.output: If you are feeling overwhelmed and want to continue, you can call Samaritans free on 116 123 (UK and Ireland), email jo@samaritans.org, or go to the Samaritans website here.

rows.source: Ọdịnihu Brett Kavanaugh tọgbọ n’ikuku ka ndị FBI na ebido nyocha
rows.output: Brett Kavanaugh's future is hanging in the balance as the FBI begins an investigation
rows.reference: Brett Kavanaugh's future hangs in the balance as FBI begins investigation

rows.source: “Echere m, ọ bụrụ na anyị nwere ike ịnweta ihe dị ka ihe ọ na arịọ - nyocha amachiri n’oge, amachiri n’oke - anyị nwere ike iwete obere ịdị n’otu,” Maazị Flake kwuru na Satọde, na etinye na ọ na atụ ụjọ na ọgbakọ ahụ na “etisasi” n’ime mkpọchi ndọrọndọrọ gozusiri ike.
rows.output: I think, if we can get something like what it's asking for - a review of the process in real time, a review of the scope - we might be able to bring a little more orderliness to the proceedings," Mr. Flake said on Saturday, referring to the conference and the "entrenchment" in the partisan lock.
rows.reference: "I thought, if we could actually get something like what he was asking for - an investigation limited in time, limited in scope - we could maybe bring a little unity," said Mr Flake on Saturday, adding that he feared the committee was "falling apart" amid entrenched partisan gridlock.

rows.source: Gịnị kpatara na Maazị Kavanaugh na ndị nkwado Repọblikan achọghị ka ndị FBI mee nyocha?
rows.output: Why do Mr. Kavanaugh and his Republican supporters not want the FBI to conduct an investigation?
rows.reference: Why didn't Mr Kavanaugh and his Republican supporters want the FBI to investigate?

rows.source: Enweghị mmasị bụ n’ihi oge.
rows.output: Lack of interest is due to time.
rows.reference: Their reluctance is all due to timing.

rows.source: Ntuli aka etiti oge bụ naanị n’ime izu ise na abịa, na Nọvemba 6 - ọ bụrụ na, dị ka atụrụ anya, ndị Repọblikan emeghị nke ọma, mgbe ahụ ha agaghị enwe ọtụtụ ike n’ọnwụnwa ha iji nweta nwoke ha chọrọ ka ahọpụta maka ụlọ ikpe kachasị n’ala.
rows.output: The midterm elections are just five weeks away, and on November 6 - if, as expected, the Republicans do poorly, then they will have little leverage in their efforts to secure the nomination of the man they want for the Supreme Court.
rows.reference: The midterm elections are only five weeks away, on November 6 - if, as expected, the Republicans do badly, then they will be severely weakened in their attempts to get the man they want elected to the highest court in the land.

rows.source: George W. Bush na ewelite ekwentị iji kpọọ Ndị Ọmeiwu, na arịọ ha ka ha kwado Maazị Kavanaugh, onye rụrụ ọrụ na White House n’aka Maazị Bush ma site n’aka ya zute nwunye ya Ashley, onye nke bụ ọde akwụkwọ nkeonwe Maazị Bush.
rows.output: George W. Bush pulled out his phone to call the Senators, asking them to support Mr. Kavanaugh, who worked in the White House for Mr. Bush and met his wife Ashley, who was Mr. Bush's personal secretary.
rows.reference: George W. Bush has been picking up the phone to call Senators, lobbying them to support Mr Kavanaugh, who worked in the White House for Mr Bush and through him met his wife Ashley, who was Mr Bush's personal secretary.

rows.source: Gịnị ga-eme mgbe ndị FBI weputere mkpesa ya?
rows.output: What will happen when the FBI releases its report?
rows.reference: What happens after the FBI produces its report?

rows.source: A ga-enwe ntuli aka na Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu, ebe ndị Repọblikan 51 na Demokrat 49 nọ ugbu a.
rows.output: There will be a vote in the House of Representatives, where 51 Republicans and 49 Democrats are currently present.
rows.reference: There will be a vote in the Senate, where 51 Republicans and 49 Democrats currently sit.

rows.source: O dobeghi anya ma Maazị Kavanaugh enwere ike ịnweta opekata mpe ntuli aka 50 n’ala Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu, nke ga-enye Mike Pence ohere, osote onye isi ala, ịkpọ ndapụta ya ma tinye ya na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị.
rows.output: Mr. Kavanaugh may not receive even a simple majority of votes in the Senate, which would allow Vice President Mike Pence to break the tie and put him on the Supreme Court.
rows.reference: It's still not clear whether Mr Kavanaugh can get to at least 50 votes on the Senate floor, which would allow Mike Pence, the vice president, to break a tie and confirm him to the Supreme Court.

rows.source: Ọnụọgụ ndị gbapụrụ na North Korea ‘gbadara’ n’okpuru Kim
rows.output: The number of defectors from North Korea 'fell' under Kim.
rows.reference: North Korea defector numbers 'drop' under Kim

rows.source: Ọnụọgụ ndị gbapụrụ na North Korea gbagara South Korea agbadaala kemgbe Kim Jong-un banyere n’ọchịchị afọ asaa gara aga, onye ọmebe iwu South Korea kwuru.
rows.output: The number of defectors from North Korea who fled to South Korea has dropped since Kim Jong-un took power seven years ago, a South Korean lawmaker said.
rows.reference: The number of North Korean defectors to South Korea has fallen since Kim Jong-un came to power seven years ago, a South Korean lawmaker has said.

rows.source: Park Byeong-seun, na arụtụ aka na data si na minitri njikọta South, kwuru na enweela mgbapụ 1,127 n’afọ gara aga - tụlee yana 2,706 na 2011.
rows.output: Park Byeong-seun, citing data from the Ministry of Unification of South Korea, stated that there were 1,127 escapes last year - compare with 2,706 in 2011.
rows.reference: Park Byeong-seug, citing data from the South's unification ministry, said there had been 1,127 defections last year - compared with 2,706 in 2011.

rows.source: Maazị Park kwuru njikwa oke ala kpachikwuru akpachi n’etiti North Korea na China yana ụgwọ dị elu ndị na akpọfe ndị mmadụ na ana socha n’ihe ndị kpatara ya.
rows.output: Mr. Park said the management of the border between North Korea and China is a very high cost and a very high-risk business.
rows.reference: Mr Park said tighter border controls between North Korea and China and higher rates charged by people smugglers were key factors.

rows.source: Pyongyang agwabeghị ọhaneze ihe ọ bụla.
rows.output: Pyongyang has not yet made any public comments.
rows.reference: Pyongyang has made no public comments.

rows.source: A na enye ọtụtụ nke ndị gbapụrụ si na North akwụkwọ amaala nke South Korea.
rows.output: We provide many of the refugees from the North with the citizenship papers of the South.
rows.reference: The vast majority of defectors from the North are eventually offered South Korean citizenship.

rows.source: Seoul kwuru na ihe gafere ndị North Korea 30,000 gafere oke ala ahụ n’ụzọ dara iwu kemgbe ngwụcha nke Ọgụ Korea na 1953.
rows.output: Seoul said that more than 30,000 North Koreans have crossed the border illegally since the end of the Korean War in 1953.
rows.reference: Seoul says more than 30,000 North Koreans have illegally crossed the border since the end of the Korean War in 1953.

rows.source: Imirikiti na esi China agbapụ, nke nwere oke ala kachasị ogologo n’etiti North Korea ma ka dị mfe ịgafe karịa Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) echedosiri ike n’etiti Korea abụọ ahụ.
rows.output: The Chinese border is porous, with the longest land border between North Korea and the DMZ, which is heavily militarized, between the two Koreas.
rows.reference: Most flee via China, which has the longest border with North Korea and is easier to cross than the heavily protected Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) between the two Koreas.

rows.source: China na ahụta ndị ahụ gbapụrụ ọsọ ka ndị mgbabata dara iwu karịa ndị mgbabata ọsọ ndụ ma jiri iwe kpọghachi ha.
rows.output: China is treating those who attempt to flee as criminals, and is repatriating them with anger.
rows.reference: China regards the defectors as illegal migrants rather than refugees and often forcibly repatriates them.

rows.source: Mmekọrịta n’etiti North na South - ndị ka nọ n’ọgụ - enwela mmelite ahụrụ anya n’ọnwa nso nso a.
rows.output: The relationship between the North and South, which are still in conflict, has seen some positive developments in recent months.
rows.reference: Relations between the North and the South - who are still technically at war - have markedly improved in recent months.

rows.source: Na mbido ọnwa a, ndị isi nke obodo abụọ ahụ hụrụ na Pyongyang maka ekwumekwu gbadoro na ụbụbọ mkposa ngwa ọgụ nuklịa.
rows.output: At the beginning of the month, the leaders of the two countries met in Pyongyang for talks focused on the dismantling of nuclear weapons.
rows.reference: Earlier this month, the leaders of the two countries met in Pyongyang for talks that centred on the stalled denuclearisation negotiations.

rows.source: Nke a bịara ka nnukwu nzụkọ Juun mere n’etiti Onye Isi Ala Donald Trump na Kim Jong-un na Singapore, mgbe ha kwenyere n’isiokwu sara mbara iji rụkọta ọrụ maka ala mmiri Korea na enweghị ngwa ọgụ nuklịa.
rows.output: This came after a major summit in June between US President Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un in Singapore, where they agreed on a broad range of issues to work towards a denuclearized Korean Peninsula and a peace treaty.
rows.reference: This came after June's historic meeting between US President Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un in Singapore, when they agreed in broad terms to work towards the nuclear-free Korean peninsula.

rows.source: Mana na Satọde, Minista Ofesi nke North Korea Ri Yong-ho tara ntaramahụhụ ndị US ụta maka ọganihu na adịghị kemgbe ahụ.
rows.output: But on Saturday, North Korean Foreign Minister Ri Yong-ho accused the US of being responsible for the lack of progress in the talks.
rows.reference: But on Saturday, North Korean Foreign Minister Ri Yong-ho blamed US sanctions for the lack of progress since then.

rows.source: “Na enweghị ntụkwasị obi na US, agaghị enwe okwukwe na nchedo obodo anyị yana n’ụdịrị ọnọdụ ndị ahụ, enweghị ụzọ ọ bụla anyị ga-esi bụrụ ụzọ kwekọrịta otu oge ịkwasa ngwa ọgụ anyị,” Maazị Ri kwuru n’okwu na Mgbakọ Ezumezu UN na New York.
rows.output: “Without the trust in the US, we will not have faith in our national security and in the kind of situation that exists, there is no way we can be a partner in time to share our weapons,” Mr. Ri said in a speech at the UN General Assembly in New York.
rows.reference: "Without any trust in the US, there will be no confidence in our national security and under such circumstances, there is no way we will unilaterally disarm ourselves first," Mr Ri said in a speech to the UN General Assembly in New York.

rows.source: Nancy Pelosi kpọrọ Brett Kavanaugh “isi mgbaka,” o kwuru na o tozughi iji rụọ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị
rows.output: Nancy Pelosi called Brett Kavanaugh "a coward," saying he was not prepared to serve on the Supreme Court.
rows.reference: Nancy Pelosi calls Brett Kavanaugh "hysterical," says he is unfit to serve on the Supreme Court

rows.source: Onye Ndu Ndị Ntakịrị N’ụlọ Nzụkọ Nancy Pelosi kpọrọ onye nhọpụta maka Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Kavanaugh “isi mgbaka” ma kwuo na ọ na ewe iwe ọkụ iji rụọ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị.
rows.output: Nancy Pelosi, the Speaker of the House, called the Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh a "handmaid" and said he is "on fire" to work in the Supreme Court.
rows.reference: House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi called Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh "hysterical" and said that he was temperamentally unfit to serve on the Supreme Court.

rows.source: Pelosi kwuru okwu ndị ahụ n’ajụjụ ọnụ na Satọde na Texas Tribune Festival na Austin, Texas.
rows.output: Pelosi made the comments in an interview on Saturday at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin, Texas.
rows.reference: Pelosi made the comments in an interview Saturday at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin, Texas.

rows.source: “Enwenwughi m ike ịkwụsị ịche na ọ bụrụ na nwanyị mee ụdịrị ihe ahụ, ha ga-ekwu ‘isi mgbaka,”” Pelosi kwuru maka mmetụta ya n’ihe akaebe Kavanaugh n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe nke Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu na Tọsde.
rows.output: "I can't stop thinking that if a woman did the same thing, they would say 'head of the snake,'" said Pelosi, referring to the impact of Kavanaugh's testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Thursday.
rows.reference: "I couldn't help but think that if a woman had ever performed that way, they would say 'hysterical,'" Pelosi said about her reaction to Kavanaugh's testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Thursday.

rows.source: Kavanaugh jiri nnukwu mwute gọnarị ebubo ndị ahụ na ọ wakporo Dk. Christine Blasey Ford n’ike mgbe ha abụọ bụ ndị ntorobịa.
rows.output: Kavanaugh denied the allegations of assaulting Dr. Christine Blasey Ford with great remorse, as both were young at the time.
rows.reference: Kavanaugh emotionally denied allegations that he had sexually assaulted Dr. Christine Blasey Ford when they were both teenagers.

rows.source: N’oge nkwupute mmepe ya, mmụọ Kavanaugh di elu nke ukwuu, oge ụfọdụ ọ na achọ iti mkpu ma olu a na agbagbu ya ka ọ na ekwu maka ezinụlọ ya yana afọ ụlọ akwụkwọ kọleji ya.
rows.output: During his confirmation hearing, Kavanaugh's spirit was soaring, sometimes he would want to shout, but his voice was suppressed as he spoke about his family and his college years.
rows.reference: During his opening statement, Kavanaugh was very emotional, at times nearly shouting and choking up while discussing his family and his high school years.

rows.source: Ọ kọtọkwara ndị Demokrat nọ n’ọgbakọ ahụ n’ụzọ doro anya, na akpọ ebubo emere ya “mgbagbu omume dị egwu n’anya, akpara akpa” nke ndị mmesapụ ahụ na ewe iwe na Hillary Clinton dara na ntuli aka onye isi ala 2016 haziri.
rows.output: He also clearly labeled the Democrats in the room as "outrageous behavior, character assassination" by the radical leftists who were angry at Hillary Clinton's defeat in the 2016 presidential election.
rows.reference: He also explicitly condemned Democrats on the committee, calling the allegations against him a "grotesque and coordinated character assassination" organized by liberals angry that Hillary Clinton lost the 2016 presidential election.

rows.source: Pelosi kwuru na ọ kwenyere na akaebe nke Kavanaugh gosiri ọ nweghị ike ịrụ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị, n’ihi o gosiri na ọ nweghị mmasị n’ebe ndị Demokrat nọ.
rows.output: Pelosi said she believes the evidence of Kavanaugh shows that he cannot work in the Supreme Court, because it shows that he has no interest in the Democrats.
rows.reference: Pelosi said that she believed Kavanaugh's testimony proved that he could not serve on the Supreme Court, because it showed that he is biased against Democrats.

rows.source: O kwuru “echere m na ọ kagburu onwe ya site na iji okwu ndị ahụ yana n’ụzọ o si kwutọọ Clintons yana ndị Demokrat,”
rows.output: He said, "I think you're just trying to insult yourself with the use of those words and the way you're attacking the Clintons and the Democrats."
rows.reference: "I think that he disqualifies himself with those statements and the manner in which he went after the Clintons and the Democrats," she said.

rows.source: Pelosi dajụrụ mgbe ajụrụ ma ọ ga-achọ iwepu Kavanaugh ma ọ bụrụ na etinye ya n’oche, ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Demokrat nweta ọnụọgụgụ karịrị na Ụlọ nke Ndị Nnọchite.
rows.output: Pelosi refused to say whether she would support removing Kavanaugh if he were seated, if the Democrats were to gain the majority in the House of Representatives.
rows.reference: Pelosi demurred when asked if she would try to impeach Kavanaugh if he is confirmed, and if Democrats gain the majority in the House of Representatives.

rows.source: “M ga-ekwu nke a -- ọ bụrụ na ọ naghị agwa Kọngress ma ọ bụ ndị FBI eziokwu, mgbe ahụ ọ bụghị naanị na o tozughi ịnọ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị, ma ị nọ n’ụlọ ikpe ọ nọ na ya ugbu a,” Pelosi kwuru.
rows.output: "I'm going to say this -- if he's not telling the truth to Congress or the FBI, then he's not only not worthy of being in the Supreme Court, but you're in a court that you're in now."
rows.reference: "I will say this -- if he is not telling the truth to Congress or to the FBI, then he's not fit not only to be on the Supreme Court, but to be on the court he's on right now," Pelosi said.

rows.source: Kavanaugh bụ nnukwu ọka ikpe na D.C. Ụlọ Ikpe Sekuit nke Arịrịọ Mkpegharị.
rows.output: Kavanaugh is a senior judge on the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals.
rows.reference: Kavanaugh is currently a judge on the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals.

rows.source: Pelosi kwukwara na ka onye Demokrat na ọ nwere nchegbu maka ntimiwu Kavanaugh ga-adị maka Affordable Care Act ma ọ bụ Roe v. Wade, ebe a na ahụta ya ka akwụmụtọ na egbochi mgbanwe.
